b84e1dce761127c79606ace6d31611b944e5e532.data: Published studies using wind farm and meteorological station time series and numerical weather prediction inputs; no new data (abstract unavailable).
b84e1dce761127c79606ace6d31611b944e5e532.result: Not reported in the abstract (unavailable); the review categorizes deep learning methods and discusses preprocessing, model structures and performance trends.
b84e1dce761127c79606ace6d31611b944e5e532.open_work: Likely directions include probabilistic forecasting, spatiotemporal modelling across wind farms and better integration of weather prediction inputs.
b84e1dce761127c79606ace6d31611b944e5e532.issues: Abstract unavailable, so the card is based on the title and general knowledge of this review; specific conclusions are not verified.

7a7e2cf62f7ed45a009a06baacc815979b72bf4d.goal: Predicts maize hybrid yield from genotype and environment (weather and soil) data, as part of the 2018 Syngenta Crop Challenge.
7a7e2cf62f7ed45a009a06baacc815979b72bf4d.architecture: Deep neural network (deep feedforward MLP with residual connections) for yield, with a separate model to predict weather, plus DNN-based feature selection.
7a7e2cf62f7ed45a009a06baacc815979b72bf4d.data: Syngenta Crop Challenge 2018 data: genotypes and yields of 2,267 maize hybrids at 2,247 locations, 2008-2016, with weather and soil data; 2017 yields as target.
7a7e2cf62f7ed45a009a06baacc815979b72bf4d.result: RMSE is 12% of average yield using predicted weather and 11% with perfect weather, outperforming Lasso, shallow neural networks and regression trees; environment matters more than genotype.
7a7e2cf62f7ed45a009a06baacc815979b72bf4d.open_work: Improving weather prediction for the growing season and better interpretability of genotype-by-environment interactions.
7a7e2cf62f7ed45a009a06baacc815979b72bf4d.issues: Single competition dataset; results depend on weather predictions; limited interpretability of the deep network.

8d25708abc05c1a7f4c500212e4957396c7a49e3.goal: Evaluates random forests for predicting crop yield responses to climate and biophysical variables at global and regional scales.
8d25708abc05c1a7f4c500212e4957396c7a49e3.architecture: Random forest regression compared with multiple linear regression as a benchmark.
8d25708abc05c1a7f4c500212e4957396c7a49e3.data: Gridded global wheat yield, US county maize grain yield over thirty years, and potato and maize silage yields from the US northeastern seaboard, with climate and biophysical predictors.
8d25708abc05c1a7f4c500212e4957396c7a49e3.result: Random forest RMSE ranges 6-14% of mean observed yield versus 14-49% for multiple linear regression, outperforming the benchmark in all statistics.
8d25708abc05c1a7f4c500212e4957396c7a49e3.open_work: Testing under climate conditions outside the training range and for climate change impact projection.
8d25708abc05c1a7f4c500212e4957396c7a49e3.issues: Random forests lose accuracy at extreme ends and for responses beyond the training data range, limiting extrapolation under future climate.

4408f88d5b9b990e1a0c7118c3bfd6a5e9d38267.goal: Tests whether LSTMs can predict streamflow in ungauged basins, a long-standing hydrological challenge.
4408f88d5b9b990e1a0c7118c3bfd6a5e9d38267.architecture: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural networks using meteorological forcing and static catchment attributes, evaluated with k-fold cross-validation over basins.
4408f88d5b9b990e1a0c7118c3bfd6a5e9d38267.data: 531 CAMELS basins (4-2,000 km2) with about 30 years of daily data; benchmarked against basin-calibrated SAC-SMA and the NOAA National Water Model reanalysis over a 15-year validation period.
4408f88d5b9b990e1a0c7118c3bfd6a5e9d38267.result: Out-of-sample LSTM median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency is 0.69, above calibrated SAC-SMA (0.64) and the National Water Model (0.58).
4408f88d5b9b990e1a0c7118c3bfd6a5e9d38267.open_work: Adding physical constraints to LSTMs (physics-guided machine learning) is suggested as future research.
4408f88d5b9b990e1a0c7118c3bfd6a5e9d38267.issues: Limited to US catchments with good attribute data; ungauged performance relies on informative catchment attributes; no uncertainty quantification.

62d4aaaf562df94c4bdb116ee1e5cc2843c88bec.goal: Asks what role hydrological process understanding should play as machine learning increasingly dominates rainfall-runoff modelling.
62d4aaaf562df94c4bdb116ee1e5cc2843c88bec.architecture: Commentary/perspective (non-ML method) derived from a keynote; discusses deep learning (LSTM) results relative to process-based models.
62d4aaaf562df94c4bdb116ee1e5cc2843c88bec.data: Draws on recent deep learning rainfall-runoff experiments on large-sample datasets such as CAMELS; no new dataset.
62d4aaaf562df94c4bdb116ee1e5cc2843c88bec.result: Argues large-scale hydrological datasets contain more information than current theory or models capture, and that preferences for process-based models are often not evidence-based.
62d4aaaf562df94c4bdb116ee1e5cc2843c88bec.open_work: Calls for quantitative assessment of where and when process understanding adds value in an ML-dominated modelling discipline.
62d4aaaf562df94c4bdb116ee1e5cc2843c88bec.issues: Opinion piece with only preliminary examples; conclusions rest largely on streamflow prediction rather than other hydrological variables.

a09b55a914bd64e301650b63fcbbc96ac91a483d.goal: Evaluates FLUXCOM machine-learning upscaling of eddy covariance carbon fluxes (GPP and NEE) from flux towers to the globe.
a09b55a914bd64e301650b63fcbbc96ac91a483d.architecture: Ensemble of machine learning methods (e.g., random forests, neural networks, model trees, kernel methods) with different forcing data and predictor sets; evaluation study rather than a new model.
a09b55a914bd64e301650b63fcbbc96ac91a483d.data: FLUXNET eddy covariance sites with remote sensing (MODIS) and meteorological forcing; compared with atmospheric inversions, sun-induced fluorescence (SIF) and dynamic global vegetation models.
a09b55a914bd64e301650b63fcbbc96ac91a483d.result: Global mean GPP is 106-130 PgC/yr; seasonal SIF agrees better with FLUXCOM (R2~0.75) than DGVMs (~0.6); NEE seasonality matches inversions (R2>0.92), but interannual NEE variability is underestimated.
a09b55a914bd64e301650b63fcbbc96ac91a483d.open_work: Exploiting more Earth observation data and machine learning concepts and improving flux tower quantity and quality, especially in the tropics.
a09b55a914bd64e301650b63fcbbc96ac91a483d.issues: Too strong tropical carbon sink likely from eddy covariance biases and missing site history; no CO2 fertilization, so flux trends are unrealistic.

84289c5530d65e843f059c5dc0d251b3100ab89b.goal: Predicts crop yield before harvest from inexpensive public remote sensing data to support agricultural monitoring and food security.
84289c5530d65e843f059c5dc0d251b3100ab89b.architecture: Convolutional neural network or LSTM trained on histograms of pixel values (dimensionality reduction), combined with a Gaussian process layer modelling spatio-temporal structure (deep Gaussian process).
84289c5530d65e843f059c5dc0d251b3100ab89b.data: Publicly available remote sensing data (MODIS surface reflectance and land surface temperature) with US county-level soybean yields.
84289c5530d65e843f059c5dc0d251b3100ab89b.result: Outperforms competing techniques for county-level US soybean yield prediction; the Gaussian process component further improves accuracy.
84289c5530d65e843f059c5dc0d251b3100ab89b.open_work: Extending to other crops and to data-scarce developing countries, where the method is aimed.
84289c5530d65e843f059c5dc0d251b3100ab89b.issues: Histogram representation discards spatial location within counties; evaluation limited to US soybean.

c3070ad9ebfe56cc7b2833e353c66392f5b7afb9.goal: Forecasts photovoltaic power output with deep learning to support solar integration into the grid.
c3070ad9ebfe56cc7b2833e353c66392f5b7afb9.architecture: Deep learning models combining an autoencoder for feature extraction with an LSTM recurrent neural network (Auto-LSTM), compared with MLP, deep belief networks and physical models.
c3070ad9ebfe56cc7b2833e353c66392f5b7afb9.data: Historical power measurements from a set of photovoltaic plants with numerical weather prediction inputs; details not available (abstract missing).
c3070ad9ebfe56cc7b2833e353c66392f5b7afb9.result: Not reported in the abstract (unavailable); the autoencoder-LSTM combination is reported to compare favourably with the other forecasting approaches.
c3070ad9ebfe56cc7b2833e353c66392f5b7afb9.open_work: Further evaluation on more sites and probabilistic forecasts would follow naturally.
c3070ad9ebfe56cc7b2833e353c66392f5b7afb9.issues: Abstract unavailable; dataset size, lead times and quantitative errors not verified.

84e32b0f5c7be87b72eab8956bab72a63ffbc3fc.goal: Predicts wheat yield across Australia and quantifies the relative contributions of climate and satellite data, comparing regression with machine learning.
84e32b0f5c7be87b72eab8956bab72a63ffbc3fc.architecture: LASSO regression benchmark compared with support vector machine, random forest and neural network (MLP) models.
84e32b0f5c7be87b72eab8956bab72a63ffbc3fc.data: Wheat yields at statistical division level, 2000-2014; climate data plus MODIS EVI and solar-induced fluorescence from GOME-2 and SCIAMACHY.
84e32b0f5c7be87b72eab8956bab72a63ffbc3fc.result: Machine learning outperforms LASSO; combined climate and satellite data reach R2 ~0.75; EVI beats noisy SIF; optimal prediction about two months before maturity.
84e32b0f5c7be87b72eab8956bab72a63ffbc3fc.open_work: Extension to other crops and regions and use of higher-resolution SIF products.
84e32b0f5c7be87b72eab8956bab72a63ffbc3fc.issues: Coarse spatial units and a short 15-year record; SIF input is noisy and coarse.

d0c7490ca113f57314b66751274e764dacfbfcc6.goal: Systematically reviews deep learning applications in hydrology and the water sector for monitoring, management, governance and communication.
d0c7490ca113f57314b66751274e764dacfbfcc6.architecture: Systematic review of deep learning approaches (CNNs, LSTM recurrent networks, generative adversarial networks, autoencoders and others) for generation, prediction, enhancement and classification tasks.
d0c7490ca113f57314b66751274e764dacfbfcc6.data: Published literature on water-related deep learning applications; no new data.
d0c7490ca113f57314b66751274e764dacfbfcc6.result: Provides a guide to state-of-the-art deep learning in water resources and discusses key issues including ethics for decision-making.
d0c7490ca113f57314b66751274e764dacfbfcc6.open_work: Gives recommendations and future directions for deep learning in hydrology and water resources.
d0c7490ca113f57314b66751274e764dacfbfcc6.issues: Broad scope limits depth of comparison; performance claims are not benchmarked across studies.

11de8a0efa86922300ef57ec40394f69536d4190.goal: Improves daily streamflow forecasts by integrating recent discharge observations of varied types into an LSTM model at continental scale.
11de8a0efa86922300ef57ec40394f69536d4190.architecture: LSTM recurrent neural network with a data integration (DI) procedure that feeds lagged discharge either directly or through a convolutional neural network unit.
11de8a0efa86922300ef57ec40394f69536d4190.data: CAMELS basins across the contiguous US with meteorological forcings, catchment attributes and recent discharge observations.
11de8a0efa86922300ef57ec40394f69536d4190.result: Data integration reaches a continental median Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.86; benefits are largest in high-autocorrelation basins and reduce baseflow bias in groundwater-dominated western basins.
11de8a0efa86922300ef57ec40394f69536d4190.open_work: Improving forecasts in high-aridity basins with flashy peaks and extending to operational forecasting.
11de8a0efa86922300ef57ec40394f69536d4190.issues: Requires recent discharge observations, so not applicable to ungauged basins; fails to improve high-aridity basins with 1-day flash peaks.

af35673327df71659f41b06388fdb1be3b8f2166.goal: Proposes differentiable modelling as a way to unify process-based models and machine learning in the geosciences, combining interpretability with data-driven skill.
af35673327df71659f41b06388fdb1be3b8f2166.architecture: Perspective on differentiable modelling: physics-based models implemented in differentiable form and coupled with neural networks (e.g., LSTM or MLP) for parameter learning and process representation; physics-informed machine learning.
af35673327df71659f41b06388fdb1be3b8f2166.data: Examples drawn from hydrological modelling, e.g., large-sample streamflow datasets such as CAMELS; no single new dataset.
af35673327df71659f41b06388fdb1be3b8f2166.result: Differentiable models achieve accuracy similar to pure ML with less data, better interpretability and extrapolation, and outperform ML under data scarcity for dynamics and decadal trends.
af35673327df71659f41b06388fdb1be3b8f2166.open_work: Address computational challenges, reduce uncertainty and verify the physical significance of learned outputs.
af35673327df71659f41b06388fdb1be3b8f2166.issues: Perspective with examples mostly from hydrology; computational cost and physical validation remain open.

130cd0e800f774a43e75798f46e9aad541c8a678.goal: Provides reliable flood warnings for extreme riverine events in ungauged watersheds worldwide, where gauge networks are sparse.
130cd0e800f774a43e75798f46e9aad541c8a678.architecture: LSTM-based recurrent neural network (encoder-decoder hindcast/forecast LSTMs) trained across thousands of gauged basins and applied to ungauged basins.
130cd0e800f774a43e75798f46e9aad541c8a678.data: Global streamflow gauge records (e.g., GRDC/Caravan) with meteorological reanalysis and forecast forcings (e.g., ERA5-Land, IFS HRES) and catchment attributes; benchmarked against GloFAS.
130cd0e800f774a43e75798f46e9aad541c8a678.result: AI forecasts at up to five-day lead time are as reliable as or better than GloFAS nowcasts, and skill for five-year return-period events matches GloFAS skill for one-year events.
130cd0e800f774a43e75798f46e9aad541c8a678.open_work: Increasing availability of hydrological data to further improve global flood warnings; model is operational in over 80 countries.
130cd0e800f774a43e75798f46e9aad541c8a678.issues: Performance depends on sparse gauge data, especially in data-poor regions; extreme events remain few for evaluation.

a134e20ad1aff2c898370c48649eb527c8414e46.goal: Compares machine learning methods for day-ahead photovoltaic power forecasting from numerical weather prediction inputs.
a134e20ad1aff2c898370c48649eb527c8414e46.architecture: Comparison of many machine learning regression methods, including linear models, kernel ridge regression, support vector regression, random forest, gradient boosting and MLP neural networks, with physical PV modelling as reference.
a134e20ad1aff2c898370c48649eb527c8414e46.data: Numerical weather prediction forecasts (ECMWF) and measured power from photovoltaic plants in Hungary; exact period not verified (abstract unavailable).
a134e20ad1aff2c898370c48649eb527c8414e46.result: Not reported in the abstract (unavailable); kernel ridge regression and MLP are reported among the best, and input selection and hyperparameter tuning strongly affect accuracy.
a134e20ad1aff2c898370c48649eb527c8414e46.open_work: Testing across more plants and climates and combining ML with physical model chains.
a134e20ad1aff2c898370c48649eb527c8414e46.issues: Abstract unavailable; limited geographic scope and dependence on a single NWP source.

039c1148106113a9f723e3bab22a07d7fad00a33.goal: Models the weather-yield relationship for crops to project climate change impacts on agriculture more accurately than classical statistical methods.
039c1148106113a9f723e3bab22a07d7fad00a33.architecture: Semiparametric deep neural network combining a nonparametric neural network (MLP) with parametric terms and fixed effects for cross-sectional heterogeneity.
039c1148106113a9f723e3bab22a07d7fad00a33.data: US Midwest corn yield data with weather variables; climate change scenarios from a suite of climate models.
039c1148106113a9f723e3bab22a07d7fad00a33.result: Outperforms classical statistical methods and fully nonparametric neural networks on held-out years; projects large negative climate impacts on corn yield, but less severe than classical methods, especially in the warmest regions and scenarios.
039c1148106113a9f723e3bab22a07d7fad00a33.open_work: Applying to other crops and regions and incorporating adaptation.
039c1148106113a9f723e3bab22a07d7fad00a33.issues: Projections extrapolate beyond observed climate; limited to US Midwest corn; does not account for future adaptation.

63169ec74fa19d5fee55c9b3dc35307e400458ae.goal: Tests whether coupling a process-based crop model with machine learning improves corn yield predictions in the US Corn Belt.
63169ec74fa19d5fee55c9b3dc35307e400458ae.architecture: Hybrid approach: APSIM crop model simulation outputs as input features to linear regression, LASSO, LightGBM, random forest and XGBoost, plus six ensemble models.
63169ec74fa19d5fee55c9b3dc35307e400458ae.data: US Corn Belt county corn yields with weather and soil data, plus APSIM-simulated variables (e.g., drought stress, water table depth).
63169ec74fa19d5fee55c9b3dc35307e400458ae.result: Adding APSIM variables reduces RMSE by 7-20%; soil-moisture-related variables, average drought stress and water table depth are most influential.
63169ec74fa19d5fee55c9b3dc35307e400458ae.open_work: More hydrological inputs and further hybrid designs for operational yield forecasting.
63169ec74fa19d5fee55c9b3dc35307e400458ae.issues: Requires running a calibrated crop model; confined to the US Corn Belt.

bca8e162da23226ca8ca251bef17ce8aada2e940.goal: Predicts depth-specific lake water temperature with a hybrid model that integrates physical theory with deep learning.
bca8e162da23226ca8ca251bef17ce8aada2e940.architecture: Process-Guided Deep Learning (PGDL): LSTM recurrent neural network with an energy-conservation penalty in the loss and pretraining on outputs of a process-based lake model.
bca8e162da23226ca8ca251bef17ce8aada2e940.data: In situ lake temperature observations and process-based (General Lake Model) simulations for two detailed study lakes and 68 additional lakes.
bca8e162da23226ca8ca251bef17ce8aada2e940.result: PGDL beats DL and process-based models; across 68 lakes median test RMSE is 1.65 °C versus 1.78 °C (DL) and 2.03 °C (PB).
bca8e162da23226ca8ca251bef17ce8aada2e940.open_work: Applying process-guided deep learning to other environmental variables and larger lake populations.
bca8e162da23226ca8ca251bef17ce8aada2e940.issues: Gains depend on pretraining data having more variability than the training period; in some lakes PB or DL is more accurate.

88af7ac2ed2f1051de05bda9e00644768b470c28.goal: Tests whether deep learning rainfall-runoff models remain reliable for extreme, high return-period events not seen in training.
88af7ac2ed2f1051de05bda9e00644768b470c28.architecture: LSTM recurrent neural network and a mass-conserving LSTM (MC-LSTM) variant architecturally constrained to conserve water mass.
88af7ac2ed2f1051de05bda9e00644768b470c28.data: CAMELS US basins with daily forcing and streamflow; benchmarks are the Sacramento conceptual model and the US National Water Model.
88af7ac2ed2f1051de05bda9e00644768b470c28.result: LSTM and MC-LSTM remain relatively accurate for extreme events, even when extremes are excluded from training; adding mass-balance constraints reduced skill during extremes.
88af7ac2ed2f1051de05bda9e00644768b470c28.open_work: Understanding why mass constraints hurt extremes and improving data-driven extrapolation.
88af7ac2ed2f1051de05bda9e00644768b470c28.issues: Limited to US basins and daily resolution; few truly extreme events available for evaluation.

baa18756bec822579b30d3b8e99ca2f8142060f7.goal: Evaluates global terrestrial evapotranspiration estimates from remote sensing, machine learning and land surface models, since ET cannot be measured directly globally.
baa18756bec822579b30d3b8e99ca2f8142060f7.architecture: Review and intercomparison of 4 remote-sensing physical models, 2 machine-learning upscaling algorithms and 14 land surface models (TRENDY ensemble); not a new ML model.
baa18756bec822579b30d3b8e99ca2f8142060f7.data: Global gridded ET products and land surface model simulations, 1982-2011.
baa18756bec822579b30d3b8e99ca2f8142060f7.result: Ensemble means agree at 589.6-617.1 mm/yr; remote sensing and ML ensembles show significant increasing trends (0.62 and 0.38 mm/yr2) while LSMs do not; greening increases ET.
baa18756bec822579b30d3b8e99ca2f8142060f7.open_work: Better water stress and canopy parameterization, new satellite retrievals, deep learning and model-data fusion.
baa18756bec822579b30d3b8e99ca2f8142060f7.issues: Large uncertainties in the Amazon and arid/semiarid regions; ML products inherit flux tower sampling biases.

d67c5996566d11f1e692fa3102abd3d3c80e3025.goal: Forecasts hourly solar irradiance for scheduling solar generation in smart grids despite its intermittency.
d67c5996566d11f1e692fa3102abd3d3c80e3025.architecture: Hybrid CEEMDAN decomposition followed by a CNN-LSTM network (convolutional neural network plus LSTM) with multiple strategies compared.
d67c5996566d11f1e692fa3102abd3d3c80e3025.data: Four real-world solar irradiance datasets from different climate types; station names not reported in the abstract.
d67c5996566d11f1e692fa3102abd3d3c80e3025.result: CEEMDAN-CNN-LSTM outperforms many alternatives with an average RMSE of 38.49 W/m2 across climates.
d67c5996566d11f1e692fa3102abd3d3c80e3025.open_work: Extension to longer horizons and probabilistic forecasts.
d67c5996566d11f1e692fa3102abd3d3c80e3025.issues: Decomposition of the full series can leak future information if not done causally; one-hour horizon only; no weather prediction inputs.

0dcffac2fca3accad5cb22e0ae920c264bbe55cf.goal: Monitors drought by blending multiple satellite drought indices with machine learning for different climate regions.
0dcffac2fca3accad5cb22e0ae920c264bbe55cf.architecture: Machine learning models including random forest, boosted regression trees and Cubist used to combine multi-sensor drought indices.
0dcffac2fca3accad5cb22e0ae920c264bbe55cf.data: Satellite indices from MODIS (vegetation and land surface temperature) and TRMM precipitation, evaluated against in situ drought indices and US Drought Monitor in arid and humid US regions.
0dcffac2fca3accad5cb22e0ae920c264bbe55cf.result: Not reported in the abstract (unavailable); random forest is reported to perform best and blended indices outperform individual indices.
0dcffac2fca3accad5cb22e0ae920c264bbe55cf.open_work: Extending to other regions and to drought forecasting.
0dcffac2fca3accad5cb22e0ae920c264bbe55cf.issues: Abstract unavailable; quantitative results and exact regions not verified.

5ab6e8f7fbaef1aa85dc84de9168c726f803d212.goal: Predicts discharge at multiple timescales (daily and hourly) with one model, since sub-daily flood peaks are missed by daily models.
5ab6e8f7fbaef1aa85dc84de9168c726f803d212.architecture: Two multi-timescale LSTM (MTS-LSTM) architectures that process long-past inputs at coarse resolution and recent inputs at fine resolution.
5ab6e8f7fbaef1aa85dc84de9168c726f803d212.data: 516 basins across the contiguous US with hourly and daily forcings and discharge; benchmark is the US National Water Model.
5ab6e8f7fbaef1aa85dc84de9168c726f803d212.result: MTS-LSTMs achieve significantly higher NSE than the National Water Model and match per-timescale LSTMs with lower computational cost.
5ab6e8f7fbaef1aa85dc84de9168c726f803d212.open_work: Operational use with forcings of differing lead times and resolutions.
5ab6e8f7fbaef1aa85dc84de9168c726f803d212.issues: US basins only; simulation with observed forcing rather than true forecasting; no uncertainty estimates.

6a517388cb7b25c32fd44dd8effd2f01e337223d.goal: Compares shallow and deep neural networks for groundwater level forecasting using only widely available meteorological inputs.
6a517388cb7b25c32fd44dd8effd2f01e337223d.architecture: Comparison of NARX (non-linear autoregressive network with exogenous input), LSTM recurrent networks and convolutional neural networks for seq2val and seq2seq forecasting.
6a517388cb7b25c32fd44dd8effd2f01e337223d.data: Groundwater level time series from wells with meteorological inputs (precipitation, temperature); 4-year test period; well locations not reported in the abstract.
6a517388cb7b25c32fd44dd8effd2f01e337223d.result: NARX performs best on average, CNNs are much faster and slightly worse; with small training data NARX clearly beats LSTM and CNN.
6a517388cb7b25c32fd44dd8effd2f01e337223d.open_work: Testing with larger datasets where deep learning may excel.
6a517388cb7b25c32fd44dd8effd2f01e337223d.issues: NARX is sensitive to initialization (handled by ensembles); conclusions depend on the small data typical of groundwater.

46e43cb76a01a9f7cd0c65cd3134928786251280.goal: Extends the short and irregular SMAP soil moisture record into a spatiotemporally seamless product over the continental US.
46e43cb76a01a9f7cd0c65cd3134928786251280.architecture: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network predicting SMAP soil moisture from forcing, model-simulated moisture and static attributes.
46e43cb76a01a9f7cd0c65cd3134928786251280.data: SMAP level-3 surface soil moisture, atmospheric forcings (NLDAS), Noah land surface model soil moisture and static physiographic attributes over CONUS.
46e43cb76a01a9f7cd0c65cd3134928786251280.result: Test RMSE below 0.035 and correlation above 0.87 over more than 75% of CONUS, removing most bias of model simulations, robust in temporal and spatial extrapolation.
46e43cb76a01a9f7cd0c65cd3134928786251280.open_work: Hindcasting, data assimilation and weather forecasting applications.
46e43cb76a01a9f7cd0c65cd3134928786251280.issues: Short SMAP training record; inherits SMAP retrieval errors; surface layer only.

ec607210dc5edf1aab8d41578dcbd9cacf3699dd.goal: Replaces inefficient, non-unique per-site calibration of process-based geoscientific models with a learned global mapping from inputs to spatially varying parameters.
ec607210dc5edf1aab8d41578dcbd9cacf3699dd.architecture: Differentiable parameter learning (dPL): a neural network (LSTM or MLP parameter network) coupled end-to-end with a differentiable process-based model, trained by backpropagation through the physics.
ec607210dc5edf1aab8d41578dcbd9cacf3699dd.data: Soil moisture (SMAP satellite retrievals with the VIC land surface model) and streamflow (CAMELS basins with the HBV hydrologic model) across the contiguous United States.
ec607210dc5edf1aab8d41578dcbd9cacf3699dd.result: dPL drastically outperforms evolutionary calibration and regionalization, improves with more training data, generalizes better to unseen locations and uncalibrated variables, and matches performance with only ~12.5% of the data at orders-of-magnitude lower cost.
ec607210dc5edf1aab8d41578dcbd9cacf3699dd.open_work: Extend dPL to more complex process models and Earth system components, and use it to learn missing physics rather than only parameters.
ec607210dc5edf1aab8d41578dcbd9cacf3699dd.issues: Requires process models to be rewritten or wrapped as differentiable code; results inherit structural deficiencies of the backbone model; demonstrated mainly over CONUS.

804f71ab26f32defe6ec5d2ed5e44fb4232106a5.goal: Provides a globally standardized large-sample hydrology dataset, since existing regional CAMELS datasets differ in format and content and hinder global studies.
804f71ab26f32defe6ec5d2ed5e44fb4232106a5.architecture: Benchmark dataset and open-source software: harmonizes seven CAMELS-style datasets and provides cloud-based (Google Earth Engine) code to extract forcings and catchment attributes for new basins. Not an ML model itself.
804f71ab26f32defe6ec5d2ed5e44fb4232106a5.data: 6830 catchments with streamflow, ERA5-Land meteorological forcing and static attributes (HydroATLAS geophysical, sociological and climatological attributes) aggregated from CAMELS (US, GB, BR, CL, AUS), LamaH-CE and HYSETS.
804f71ab26f32defe6ec5d2ed5e44fb4232106a5.result: Delivers a consistent global dataset of forcing, streamflow and attributes plus tooling that lets the community add catchments, supporting global training of models such as LSTMs.
804f71ab26f32defe6ec5d2ed5e44fb4232106a5.open_work: Community extension to under-represented regions (Africa, Asia), additional forcing products and variables, and use as a standard benchmark for global hydrological ML.
804f71ab26f32defe6ec5d2ed5e44fb4232106a5.issues: Reanalysis-based forcing (ERA5-Land) is coarser and more biased than local station products; geographic coverage is skewed to North America and Europe; streamflow quality varies by source.

bade2a6934dc388dd462b1140cda43738872fcdd.goal: Improves hourly global horizontal irradiance (GHI) forecasting to support integration of variable solar power into grids and energy markets.
bade2a6934dc388dd462b1140cda43738872fcdd.architecture: Hybrid LSTM-CNN: an LSTM extracts temporal features from irradiance time series and a convolutional neural network extracts spatial features from correlation matrices of meteorological variables at the target and neighboring sites.
bade2a6934dc388dd462b1140cda43738872fcdd.data: Hourly meteorological data (temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, cloud cover, etc.) and GHI at 23 locations in California, USA; evaluated over one year, by season and under three sky conditions.
bade2a6934dc388dd462b1140cda43738872fcdd.result: Forecast skill score improves by about 37–45% over smart persistence, SVM, ANN, standalone LSTM, CNN and other hybrid models across seasons and sky conditions.
bade2a6934dc388dd462b1140cda43738872fcdd.open_work: Test longer horizons and other climates, and incorporate satellite or numerical weather prediction inputs.
bade2a6934dc388dd462b1140cda43738872fcdd.issues: Single-region study; deterministic forecasts only with no uncertainty quantification; short-term horizon; sensitivity to the choice of neighboring sites not fully explored.

25df34dd651b0ec33cff6694539e67c43f5387fa.goal: Predicts seasonal groundwater level change and quantifies the relative importance of climate, pumping and surface-water drivers in agricultural aquifers without expensive physical models.
25df34dd651b0ec33cff6694539e67c43f5387fa.architecture: Ensemble framework combining spectral analysis, input selection by mutual information, genetic algorithms and lag analysis, and a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network, with uncertainty analysis.
25df34dd651b0ec33cff6694539e67c43f5387fa.data: Well observations in the High Plains aquifer and the Mississippi River Valley alluvial aquifer, USA, with climate, irrigation demand and streamflow predictors; testing period 2003–2012.
25df34dd651b0ec33cff6694539e67c43f5387fa.result: Irrigation demand is the dominant driver at most wells; held-out observations correlate with R > 0.8 at 88% (HPA) and 83% (MRVA) of wells; cumulative level-change error is under 2 m over most of the area.
25df34dd651b0ec33cff6694539e67c43f5387fa.open_work: Apply the framework to other aquifers and to scenario projections of water availability under changing climate and management.
25df34dd651b0ec33cff6694539e67c43f5387fa.issues: Purely statistical so physical consistency is not guaranteed; relies on proxy pumping/irrigation data; well-by-well models may not transfer to unmonitored locations.

9f989dfe90db8a12f77012d777b04a69548fd21f.goal: Forecasts monthly reservoir inflows for water management by combining artificial intelligence methods with large-scale climate phenomenon information (climate indices).
9f989dfe90db8a12f77012d777b04a69548fd21f.architecture: Machine learning regression models using climate-phenomenon predictors; the model set is not reported in the available metadata.
9f989dfe90db8a12f77012d777b04a69548fd21f.data: Not reported in the available metadata; title implies historical reservoir inflow records with climate indices (e.g., ENSO-related) as predictors.
9f989dfe90db8a12f77012d777b04a69548fd21f.result: Not reported in the available metadata; the title suggests climate-index information improves monthly inflow forecasts.
9f989dfe90db8a12f77012d777b04a69548fd21f.open_work: Extend to longer lead times and probabilistic forecasts usable for reservoir operation decisions.
9f989dfe90db8a12f77012d777b04a69548fd21f.issues: Abstract unavailable, so data, region and quantitative skill could not be verified; monthly data give small samples, and teleconnection-based predictability varies by region and season.

fcea0250f90d0732365a2ae88c35d8799d36e3fe.goal: Compares machine learning methods for monthly streamflow simulation not only on accuracy but also on interpretability and uncertainty, which matter for planning and management.
fcea0250f90d0732365a2ae88c35d8799d36e3fe.architecture: Comparison of multiple regression and machine learning methods: generalized additive models, multivariate adaptive regression splines, artificial neural networks (MLP), random forests and M5 cubist models.
fcea0250f90d0732365a2ae88c35d8799d36e3fe.data: Monthly streamflow and climate data for five highly seasonal rivers in the Ethiopian highlands (Blue Nile region); compared with physical models developed for the region.
fcea0250f90d0732365a2ae88c35d8799d36e3fe.result: Data-driven models reduce errors relative to regional physical models, with relative ranking varying by basin; random forests and GAMs aid interpretation, but GAMs and MARS become highly variable under high temperatures.
fcea0250f90d0732365a2ae88c35d8799d36e3fe.open_work: Evaluate robustness of empirical models under climate change and extreme conditions before using them for planning.
fcea0250f90d0732365a2ae88c35d8799d36e3fe.issues: Monthly data in few basins limit generality; extrapolation under unprecedented climate (high temperatures) is unreliable; empirical models lack process representation.

961a0e3f7ad066edf5fd9b236769021ccbff671e.goal: Shows that differentiable, learnable process-based hydrologic models can approach LSTM accuracy for streamflow while remaining interpretable and predicting untrained physical variables.
961a0e3f7ad066edf5fd9b236769021ccbff671e.architecture: Differentiable (δ) model: the HBV conceptual hydrologic model implemented in a differentiable programming framework with embedded neural networks (LSTM/MLP) that regionalize parameters and enhance or replace process modules.
961a0e3f7ad066edf5fd9b236769021ccbff671e.data: 671 CAMELS basins across the contiguous USA with Daymet and a second forcing dataset (Maurer/NLDAS); simulated evapotranspiration and baseflow compared with alternative estimates.
961a0e3f7ad066edf5fd9b236769021ccbff671e.result: Median Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.732 versus 0.748 for a state-of-the-art LSTM with Daymet (0.715 vs 0.722 with another forcing), while also outputting soil and groundwater storage, snowpack, ET and baseflow.
961a0e3f7ad066edf5fd9b236769021ccbff671e.open_work: Apply to models with more process complexity, constrain with multi-variable observations, and use the framework to learn physics from big data.
961a0e3f7ad066edf5fd9b236769021ccbff671e.issues: Still slightly below LSTM for streamflow; untrained internal states are only loosely validated; evaluated on CAMELS basins with limited human influence.

2f1e753d139ddfdd26786a65363c4e1d70d1de53.goal: Describes Google's operational riverine flood forecasting and warning system, aiming to deliver accurate real-time flood alerts for large gauged rivers.
2f1e753d139ddfdd26786a65363c4e1d70d1de53.architecture: Operational system with four subsystems; stage forecasting uses Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and linear models, and inundation uses a Thresholding model and a new machine-learning Manifold model as an alternative to hydraulic modeling.
2f1e753d139ddfdd26786a65363c4e1d70d1de53.data: Historical river stage gauge data and inundation information for flood-prone rivers in India and Bangladesh; operational evaluation during the 2021 monsoon season.
2f1e753d139ddfdd26786a65363c4e1d70d1de53.result: All models meet operational performance thresholds; LSTM beats the linear model; Thresholding and Manifold are similar for extent. In 2021 the system covered 287,000 km² and over 350M people, sending more than 100M alerts.
2f1e753d139ddfdd26786a65363c4e1d70d1de53.open_work: Extend coverage to more flood-prone and ungauged locations and improve modeling skill and accuracy.
2f1e753d139ddfdd26786a65363c4e1d70d1de53.issues: Limited to large gauged rivers; evaluation on historical data with operational-metric framing rather than independent benchmarks; inundation depth validation is limited.

71e6e9ec2217aa508f89f2c676e84ec0390910af.goal: Predicts photovoltaic energy generation from weather forecasts to support microgrid control and day-ahead/intra-day energy market bidding.
71e6e9ec2217aa508f89f2c676e84ec0390910af.architecture: Artificial neural network (MLP) developed in MATLAB, mapping forecast weather parameters to solar energy production.
71e6e9ec2217aa508f89f2c676e84ec0390910af.data: Weather forecast and PV generation data for a solar installation (site details not given in the abstract); validation on days outside the training database.
71e6e9ec2217aa508f89f2c676e84ec0390910af.result: Difference between produced and predicted energy is about 0.5–9%, judged sufficient for operational use in systems with integrated solar generation.
71e6e9ec2217aa508f89f2c676e84ec0390910af.open_work: Integrate the predictor into real microgrid controllers and test with more sites and seasons.
71e6e9ec2217aa508f89f2c676e84ec0390910af.issues: Single-site, small-dataset study; simple ANN without comparison to strong baselines; accuracy depends on weather forecast quality; no uncertainty estimates.

14db6dc7432d4aa9f85ce7540dc9bdabfe136150.goal: Evaluates deep learning for estimating daily reference evapotranspiration (ETo) from limited meteorological inputs and tests transferability beyond training stations.
14db6dc7432d4aa9f85ce7540dc9bdabfe136150.architecture: Comparison of deep neural network (MLP), temporal convolutional network (TCN) and LSTM with support vector machine and random forest, against temperature-, radiation- and humidity-based empirical equations; K-means clustering groups stations.
14db6dc7432d4aa9f85ce7540dc9bdabfe136150.data: Weather station data from the Northeast Plain, China, with FAO-56 Penman–Monteith ETo as target; local per-station and cross-station (leave-station-out within clusters) strategies.
14db6dc7432d4aa9f85ce7540dc9bdabfe136150.result: TCN and RF beat modified Hargreaves locally (RMSE lower by ~0.10 and ~0.07 mm/d); across stations TCN and LSTM performed best with temperature inputs, and all ML models beat radiation- and humidity-based equations.
14db6dc7432d4aa9f85ce7540dc9bdabfe136150.open_work: Test in other climates and with other input combinations, and assess operational use with forecast inputs.
14db6dc7432d4aa9f85ce7540dc9bdabfe136150.issues: Single region; target is computed Penman–Monteith ETo rather than lysimeter measurements; improvements over empirical formulas are modest in absolute terms.

7d57d79e9900e9525e1dfbf11d73621a412ae372.goal: Estimates reference evapotranspiration when only temperature data are available, a common situation at weather stations in data-scarce regions.
7d57d79e9900e9525e1dfbf11d73621a412ae372.architecture: Extreme learning machine (ELM, single-hidden-layer feedforward network) and generalized regression neural network (GRNN), compared with temperature-based empirical equations such as Hargreaves.
7d57d79e9900e9525e1dfbf11d73621a412ae372.data: Not reported in the available metadata; likely daily temperature records from weather stations in China with FAO-56 Penman–Monteith ETo as target.
7d57d79e9900e9525e1dfbf11d73621a412ae372.result: Not reported in the available metadata; the title implies both ML models give acceptable ETo estimates from temperature alone, likely outperforming empirical formulas.
7d57d79e9900e9525e1dfbf11d73621a412ae372.open_work: Assess spatial transferability to stations not used in training and in other climates.
7d57d79e9900e9525e1dfbf11d73621a412ae372.issues: Abstract unavailable, so data and numbers could not be verified; temperature-only inputs cannot capture radiation, humidity and wind effects, limiting accuracy in some climates.

df2f6f00d610ba4379ac25d2a995224a7c99791a.goal: Develops high-resolution meteorological drought forecasts for ungauged areas where no station observations exist.
df2f6f00d610ba4379ac25d2a995224a7c99791a.architecture: Machine learning models (extremely randomized trees and others such as random forest and boosted regression trees) using remote-sensing drought variables, compared with Kriging spatial interpolation; long-range climate forecasts versus climatology as future inputs.
df2f6f00d610ba4379ac25d2a995224a7c99791a.data: SPI and SPEI at 3-, 6-, 9- and 12-month scales forecast at 1–6 month leads on a 0.05° grid; remote sensing products (e.g., MODIS, TRMM) and long-range climate forecasts (South Korea, per reliable knowledge).
df2f6f00d610ba4379ac25d2a995224a7c99791a.result: Extremely randomized trees achieve the best producer's drought accuracy (up to 64%), while Kriging gives better user's accuracy (up to 44%); long-range forecast inputs add little, though reducing precipitation forecast error improves drought forecasts.
df2f6f00d610ba4379ac25d2a995224a7c99791a.open_work: Improve forecast skill through better long-range climate forecasts and more sophisticated downscaling.
df2f6f00d610ba4379ac25d2a995224a7c99791a.issues: Modest accuracy for drought classes; contribution of climate forecasts not significant; class-based metrics; single regional setting.

6c90357522b6031178583b3acc0aee32c0ec9e5d.goal: Builds a fast, easy-to-use ML-based hydrological model for daily streamflow in large, data-limited watersheds while handling spatial variability and extreme flows.
6c90357522b6031178583b3acc0aee32c0ec9e5d.architecture: Artificial neural network (MLP) trained on synthetic data from the physically based distributed GBHM model and a stochastic rainfall generator, with a categorization approach for high flows and local-binary-pattern computer vision features for spatial rainfall patterns.
6c90357522b6031178583b3acc0aee32c0ec9e5d.data: Synthetic case studies from GBHM simulations plus real data from the upper Chao Phraya Basin, Thailand.
6c90357522b6031178583b3acc0aee32c0ec9e5d.result: The combined GBHM-ANN-CA-CV model greatly improves accuracy in data-limited basins; computer-vision spatial features improve robustness and categorization greatly improves high-flow simulation.
6c90357522b6031178583b3acc0aee32c0ec9e5d.open_work: Apply to other basins and to changing-environment scenarios for water resource management.
6c90357522b6031178583b3acc0aee32c0ec9e5d.issues: Relies on the physical model's synthetic data so inherits its biases; single real-world basin; hand-crafted CV features rather than learned spatial representations.

8d5ba785089077bd5f849fb353ef8b61268930bb.goal: Tests whether LSTM networks predict continuous streamflow in ungauged basins better than regionalized conceptual hydrological models.
8d5ba785089077bd5f849fb353ef8b61268930bb.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network trained regionally, compared with state-of-the-art hydrological-model-dependent regionalization methods (spatial proximity, physical similarity, etc.).
8d5ba785089077bd5f849fb353ef8b61268930bb.data: 148 catchments in northeast North America (Quebec region) with the same meteorological and geophysical descriptor data as the hydrological models; leave-one-out cross-validation.
8d5ba785089077bd5f849fb353ef8b61268930bb.result: LSTM outperforms regionalized hydrological models in 93–97% of catchments and beats models calibrated on the target catchment in up to 78% of cases, robust to hyperparameter changes.
8d5ba785089077bd5f849fb353ef8b61268930bb.open_work: Use LSTM-based regionalization as a new baseline and explore larger, more diverse regions.
8d5ba785089077bd5f849fb353ef8b61268930bb.issues: Regional study with relatively dense gauging; leave-one-out may overstate transfer to truly remote ungauged areas; no interpretation of internal states.

70def1c9bdf053b526f5798935508cbb1ef1c214.goal: Reviews hybrid hydroclimatic forecasting that blends dynamical weather/climate model predictions with statistical or AI methods to improve forecast skill.
70def1c9bdf053b526f5798935508cbb1ef1c214.architecture: Review of hybrid forecasting systems that use machine learning and statistical post-processing to integrate outputs of numerical weather prediction, climate, land, hydrology and Earth system models.
70def1c9bdf053b526f5798935508cbb1ef1c214.data: Review of literature covering subseasonal-to-decadal predictions of rainfall, temperature, streamflow, floods, droughts, tropical cyclones and atmospheric rivers.
70def1c9bdf053b526f5798935508cbb1ef1c214.result: Hybrid systems can reduce dynamical model biases, avoid running costly land models, and combine sources of predictability across horizons, and are attracting growing attention.
70def1c9bdf053b526f5798935508cbb1ef1c214.open_work: Physically explainable results, assimilating human influences, new ensemble techniques, seamless short-to-long lead prediction, land/ocean/ice initial conditions, spatial variability and operational uptake.
70def1c9bdf053b526f5798935508cbb1ef1c214.issues: As a review it offers no new quantitative benchmark; hybrid approaches depend on stationarity of learned relationships and on the quality of dynamical inputs.

f581ce59ead3cd97f8ddfad937c714c79cacda0e.goal: Assesses how climate change will directly affect groundwater levels in Germany during the 21st century.
f581ce59ead3cd97f8ddfad937c714c79cacda0e.architecture: Convolutional neural network (1D CNN) groundwater level models driven only by meteorological inputs, applied to climate projections.
f581ce59ead3cd97f8ddfad937c714c79cacda0e.data: Groundwater level records at 118 sites across Germany; meteorological inputs (precipitation, temperature) from observations for training and regional climate projections under RCP2.6, 4.5 and 8.5.
f581ce59ead3cd97f8ddfad937c714c79cacda0e.result: Significant declining trends at most sites under RCP8.5, strongest in northern and eastern Germany, with greater variability and longer low-level periods; much weaker effects under RCP2.6 and 4.5.
f581ce59ead3cd97f8ddfad937c714c79cacda0e.open_work: Include anthropogenic factors such as extraction and land-use change, and extend to other regions.
f581ce59ead3cd97f8ddfad937c714c79cacda0e.issues: Excludes groundwater abstraction; extrapolation of data-driven models to future climates is uncertain; inherits climate-model biases.

2317685962197cf55363b2fd9353e5c80ccd8f6e.goal: Provides fast predictions of 2D maximum water depth maps for urban pluvial floods at locations and rain events not seen in training.
2317685962197cf55363b2fd9353e5c80ccd8f6e.architecture: U-Net convolutional neural network (image segmentation architecture) taking hyetograph patterns and topographic inputs, with systematic input selection and hyperparameter tuning (97k to 260M parameters).
2317685962197cf55363b2fd9353e5c80ccd8f6e.data: Hydrodynamic flood simulations for an urban area (Denmark) driven by natural rain events, with terrain and imperviousness rasters; evaluation on unseen locations and events.
2317685962197cf55363b2fd9353e5c80ccd8f6e.result: Five terrain-shape and imperviousness inputs are optimal; a 28M-parameter model works best; performance is similar to existing screening approaches with predictions in seconds.
2317685962197cf55363b2fd9353e5c80ccd8f6e.open_work: Balance temporal and spatial rainfall patterns in training data, improve spatial inputs, and couple U-FLOOD to dynamic sewer system models.
2317685962197cf55363b2fd9353e5c80ccd8f6e.issues: Predicts only maximum depth, not flood dynamics; trained on simulated data so inherits simulator assumptions; sewer system effects not represented.

9f48bb4aae59e1c6a6a1d9d420c721dd0d27ff4b.goal: Forecasts wind speed and wind energy for wind power planning and grid integration.
9f48bb4aae59e1c6a6a1d9d420c721dd0d27ff4b.architecture: Transformer-based deep neural network combined with wavelet transform decomposition of the input time series.
9f48bb4aae59e1c6a6a1d9d420c721dd0d27ff4b.data: Not reported in the available metadata; likely measured wind speed time series from sites in Brazil.
9f48bb4aae59e1c6a6a1d9d420c721dd0d27ff4b.result: Not reported in the available metadata; the title implies the wavelet-transformer improves wind speed and energy forecasts over baselines.
9f48bb4aae59e1c6a6a1d9d420c721dd0d27ff4b.open_work: Test across more sites and horizons and add probabilistic forecasts.
9f48bb4aae59e1c6a6a1d9d420c721dd0d27ff4b.issues: Abstract unavailable, so data, horizon and skill could not be verified; wavelet decomposition can leak future information if applied to the full series before splitting.

a2842566701213c2fbdf96be255820eace553c45.goal: Predicts soybean yield across multiple environments by combining genotype information and weather, to support breeding under diverse climatic conditions.
a2842566701213c2fbdf96be255820eace553c45.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network with a temporal attention mechanism for interpretability, using pedigree relatedness measures plus weekly weather.
a2842566701213c2fbdf96be255820eace553c45.data: Uniform Soybean Tests (UST) performance records in North America with weekly weather parameters over the growing season.
a2842566701213c2fbdf96be255820eace553c45.result: Outperforms SVR with RBF kernel, LASSO regression and the data-driven USDA yield model; attention identifies important time windows in the season.
a2842566701213c2fbdf96be255820eace553c45.open_work: Incorporate genomic markers and soil/management data, and extend to other crops and breeding programs.
a2842566701213c2fbdf96be255820eace553c45.issues: Pedigree-based relatedness is a coarse genotype representation; weekly weather aggregation may miss extremes; results tied to trial-plot conditions.

83f940e2a024c666769a6237d0e1f1e73f4bc9cd.goal: Assesses which environmental variables, observation frequencies and algorithms best predict county-level maize yield in the US Midwest.
83f940e2a024c666769a6237d0e1f1e73f4bc9cd.architecture: Comparison of Lasso, support vector regression, random forest, XGBoost (gradient boosting), LSTM and convolutional neural network (CNN).
83f940e2a024c666769a6237d0e1f1e73f4bc9cd.data: County-level maize yields with features from satellite observations, weather data, land surface model outputs, soil maps and crop progress reports (hundreds of features).
83f940e2a024c666769a6237d0e1f1e73f4bc9cd.result: XGBoost is most accurate and stable while LSTM and CNN are not advantageous; best setup improves accuracy by 5% over a Lasso baseline; reasonable forecasts from early June and better than USDA WASDE early in the season.
83f940e2a024c666769a6237d0e1f1e73f4bc9cd.open_work: Extend to other crops and regions and to in-season operational forecasting.
83f940e2a024c666769a6237d0e1f1e73f4bc9cd.issues: County-level aggregation; results specific to the US Midwest; deep models may be data-limited; feature importance is correlational.

07a040f140b3b3a6e19fad63ca1b031ab554f938.goal: Establishes benchmarking for uncertainty estimation in deep learning rainfall-runoff models, since actionable hydrological forecasts require reliable uncertainty.
07a040f140b3b3a6e19fad63ca1b031ab554f938.architecture: LSTM-based baselines: three Mixture Density Network variants (Gaussian, countable mixture of asymmetric Laplacians, uncountable mixture) and Monte Carlo dropout, plus a benchmarking procedure.
07a040f140b3b3a6e19fad63ca1b031ab554f938.data: CAMELS US basins (531 basins, daily streamflow with meteorological forcing).
07a040f140b3b3a6e19fad63ca1b031ab554f938.result: Mixture Density Network baselines give accurate, well-calibrated uncertainty and outperform Monte Carlo dropout; post-hoc analysis reveals nuanced learned behaviors.
07a040f140b3b3a6e19fad63ca1b031ab554f938.open_work: Standardize uncertainty benchmarks across the community and extend to forecasting with input uncertainty and ungauged basins.
07a040f140b3b3a6e19fad63ca1b031ab554f938.issues: Evaluated in simulation mode with observed forcing; covers mainly aleatoric/total predictive uncertainty; limited to CAMELS US.

55a1a8448150a386f179f12224efc65d9139b7d1.goal: Uses interpretive deep learning to extract scientific insight about flood-generating mechanisms across the contiguous United States.
55a1a8448150a386f179f12224efc65d9139b7d1.architecture: LSTM runoff models interpreted with the expected gradients method and an additive decomposition method.
55a1a8448150a386f179f12224efc65d9139b7d1.data: 160 representative catchments across CONUS (CAMELS-based) with daily meteorological forcing and streamflow; 20,908 identified flow peaks.
55a1a8448150a386f179f12224efc65d9139b7d1.result: Three mechanisms emerge: snowmelt (10.1% of peaks), recent rainfall (60.9%) and historical rainfall (29.0%); single mechanisms dominate 70.7% of catchments; LSTM memory retention differs by flood type.
55a1a8448150a386f179f12224efc65d9139b7d1.open_work: Use interpretive DL more broadly for AI-assisted scientific discovery of hydrological processes and extremes.
55a1a8448150a386f179f12224efc65d9139b7d1.issues: Mechanism attribution depends on the interpretation method and the model's learned structure; limited to available catchments and inputs.

f0e5515aadba86407e6672d17b79390083b04f92.goal: Accelerates urban pluvial flood prediction by emulating physically based simulations of maximum water depth.
f0e5515aadba86407e6672d17b79390083b04f92.architecture: Deep convolutional neural network framed as image-to-image translation (encoder-decoder CNN) generating water depth rasters.
f0e5515aadba86407e6672d17b79390083b04f92.data: Flood simulation data from three urban catchments and 18 hyetographs; tests with design and real hyetographs.
f0e5515aadba86407e6672d17b79390083b04f92.result: Predictions take about 0.5% of the time of physically based models with promising accuracy and generalizability.
f0e5515aadba86407e6672d17b79390083b04f92.open_work: Apply to flood-safe urban layout planning and related urban flood analysis tasks.
f0e5515aadba86407e6672d17b79390083b04f92.issues: Trained on simulator output so inherits its assumptions; few catchments and hyetographs; only maximum depth is predicted.

22c9f508f13d6dbc689ca3b0397f9e7355866286.goal: Estimates daily reference evapotranspiration when only limited climate variables are available.
22c9f508f13d6dbc689ca3b0397f9e7355866286.architecture: Artificial neural network (MLP) compared with empirical equations (e.g., temperature- and radiation-based formulas) using reduced input sets.
22c9f508f13d6dbc689ca3b0397f9e7355866286.data: Not reported in the available metadata; likely daily weather station data with Penman–Monteith ETo as target (possibly in Greece).
22c9f508f13d6dbc689ca3b0397f9e7355866286.result: Not reported in the available metadata; the title implies ANNs give competitive or better ETo estimates than empirical equations with limited inputs.
22c9f508f13d6dbc689ca3b0397f9e7355866286.open_work: Test spatial transferability and other input combinations.
22c9f508f13d6dbc689ca3b0397f9e7355866286.issues: Abstract unavailable, so data and numbers could not be verified; limited-input estimation is inherently less accurate in some climates.

fa89464e9db2cae14cca93a2a0b81a5d8324d978.goal: Improves land surface model terrestrial water storage simulations by learning their mismatch with GRACE, addressing missing processes such as groundwater depletion.
fa89464e9db2cae14cca93a2a0b81a5d8324d978.architecture: Deep convolutional neural network (CNN) learning spatiotemporal patterns of the mismatch between GRACE and NOAH-simulated TWS anomalies, used to correct NOAH output.
fa89464e9db2cae14cca93a2a0b81a5d8324d978.data: GRACE TWS anomalies and NOAH land surface model simulations over India, with in situ groundwater storage observations for validation.
fa89464e9db2cae14cca93a2a0b81a5d8324d978.result: CNN correction raises country-average correlation to 0.94 and NSE to 0.87 (14% and 52% improvements over NOAH); learned mismatch correlates well with in situ groundwater anomalies.
fa89464e9db2cae14cca93a2a0b81a5d8324d978.open_work: Fill the GRACE to GRACE-FO data gap and apply mismatch learning to other regions and models.
fa89464e9db2cae14cca93a2a0b81a5d8324d978.issues: Correction is statistical and not process-based; single region; coarse GRACE resolution limits local applicability.

57c8593df274053520c4dfd8a80e1318f8130abb.goal: Improves one-hour-ahead solar irradiance forecasting for photovoltaic integration by using multivariate inputs and multi-branch hybrid deep networks.
57c8593df274053520c4dfd8a80e1318f8130abb.architecture: WPD-CNN-LSTM-MLP: wavelet packet decomposition with convolutional neural network, LSTM and multi-layer perceptron (MLP) branches.
57c8593df274053520c4dfd8a80e1318f8130abb.data: Hourly irradiance, temperature, relative humidity and wind speed from Denver, Clark and Folsom, USA.
57c8593df274053520c4dfd8a80e1318f8130abb.result: Outperforms BPNN, SVM, RNN, LSTM, climatology–persistence and ablated hybrids in hourly irradiance forecasting.
57c8593df274053520c4dfd8a80e1318f8130abb.open_work: Extend to longer horizons and probabilistic forecasting.
57c8593df274053520c4dfd8a80e1318f8130abb.issues: Only one-hour-ahead deterministic forecasts; three sites; wavelet decomposition can leak information if not applied causally.

b874ade5deea29a03cd195225b193b0cf3115cbe.goal: Forecasts solar irradiance at ultra-short-term horizons (minutes) using sky images to anticipate cloud-driven fluctuations in PV output.
b874ade5deea29a03cd195225b193b0cf3115cbe.architecture: Transformer-based multimodal learning framework fusing ground-based sky images with irradiance/meteorological time series.
b874ade5deea29a03cd195225b193b0cf3115cbe.data: Not reported in the available metadata; likely a public sky-image and irradiance dataset from a ground station.
b874ade5deea29a03cd195225b193b0cf3115cbe.result: Not reported in the available metadata; the title implies improved ultra-short-term accuracy over single-modality baselines.
b874ade5deea29a03cd195225b193b0cf3115cbe.open_work: Test generalization across sites and cameras and extend to probabilistic forecasts.
b874ade5deea29a03cd195225b193b0cf3115cbe.issues: Abstract unavailable, so data and skill could not be verified; sky-camera approaches are site-specific and limited to very short horizons.

bf319b9790163415d927980bc8d4eaf589b469b5.goal: Estimates wheat yield while explaining the drivers of yield variability, combining predictive deep learning with interpretability.
bf319b9790163415d927980bc8d4eaf589b469b5.architecture: Deep neural network (1D convolutional neural network) on multivariate time series, interpreted with regression activation maps; compared with ridge regression and random forest.
bf319b9790163415d927980bc8d4eaf589b469b5.data: Vegetation (satellite, e.g., MODIS-derived) and meteorological time series with district-level wheat yields in the Indian Wheat Belt.
bf319b9790163415d927980bc8d4eaf589b469b5.result: The DL model beats ridge regression and random forest; learned features relate to growing-season length and temperature and light conditions (e.g., high 2012 yields linked to cool, sunny conditions).
bf319b9790163415d927980bc8d4eaf589b469b5.open_work: Apply the approach to other crops and regions.
bf319b9790163415d927980bc8d4eaf589b469b5.issues: Limited years of yield data; interpretation via activation maps is qualitative; regional scope.

a50026dcc51a5f02f2b2f7e0a76617d614709d4b.goal: Tests whether an LSTM can boost medium-range river streamflow forecasts over physics-based systems in the western United States.
a50026dcc51a5f02f2b2f7e0a76617d614709d4b.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network in a hybrid system driven by meteorological forecasts; compared with raw and bias-corrected GloFAS.
a50026dcc51a5f02f2b2f7e0a76617d614709d4b.data: ERA5 and GloFAS-ERA5 reanalysis catchment means plus streamflow at ten western US gauges; testing June 2019–June 2020 with ERA5; operational phase September 2020–October 2021 with ECMWF IFS forecasts up to 10 days.
a50026dcc51a5f02f2b2f7e0a76617d614709d4b.result: LSTM is best in testing (skilful at nine stations, six highly skilful) and beats raw and bias-corrected GloFAS operationally, with skilful 5-day forecasts at nine stations.
a50026dcc51a5f02f2b2f7e0a76617d614709d4b.open_work: Expand to more stations, ensemble IFS inputs and longer lead times.
a50026dcc51a5f02f2b2f7e0a76617d614709d4b.issues: Only ten stations; short evaluation periods; trained on reanalysis but driven by forecasts, causing distribution shift; deterministic forecasts.

ad1cf326c0f8d7cbb7a8203ed90daffb73c1562d.goal: Estimates daily reference evapotranspiration from limited hourly sensor data (temperature and humidity, or temperature only).
ad1cf326c0f8d7cbb7a8203ed90daffb73c1562d.architecture: Random forest, XGBoost, artificial neural network (MLP) and convolutional neural network (CNN), with different daily vs hourly input strategies.
ad1cf326c0f8d7cbb7a8203ed90daffb73c1562d.data: 53 weather stations in Minas Gerais, Brazil; targets from daily and summed-hourly ASCE Penman–Monteith ETo; regional and local scenarios.
ad1cf326c0f8d7cbb7a8203ed90daffb73c1562d.result: Using 24 h hourly data directly is best; CNN with hourly data plus hourly Ra is best overall, reducing RMSE by up to 28.2% (0.71 to 0.51) regionally and 22.4% locally.
ad1cf326c0f8d7cbb7a8203ed90daffb73c1562d.open_work: Test in other climates and with low-cost sensor networks.
ad1cf326c0f8d7cbb7a8203ed90daffb73c1562d.issues: Single Brazilian state; targets are computed ETo rather than measured; temperature-only inputs limit accuracy.

7919790ed3b0213c4ba84e06e171cb1c9918edc2.goal: Provides real-time street-scale pluvial flood prediction for an urban coastal city, where physics-based 1-D pipe/2-D overland flow models are too slow for operational decision support.
7919790ed3b0213c4ba84e06e171cb1c9918edc2.architecture: Random forest surrogate model trained to emulate hourly water depths from a high-fidelity 1-D/2-D physics-based urban flood model, using topographic and environmental features.
7919790ed3b0213c4ba84e06e171cb1c9918edc2.data: Hourly water depths simulated by a high-resolution 1-D/2-D physics-based model at 16,914 road segments in Norfolk, Virginia, USA; two training scenarios (flood-prone streets only vs. all segments).
7919790ed3b0213c4ba84e06e171cb1c9918edc2.result: The random forest achieves high predictive skill, best when trained only on the most flood-prone streets, and cuts run time by a factor of about 3,000 relative to the physics-based model.
7919790ed3b0213c4ba84e06e171cb1c9918edc2.open_work: Testing on additional storms and cities, adding forecast rainfall and tide inputs for operational use, and quantifying surrogate uncertainty.
7919790ed3b0213c4ba84e06e171cb1c9918edc2.issues: Learns from simulated rather than observed depths, so it inherits the physics model's errors; single city; skill drops when trained on all segments; no uncertainty estimate.

cbd319e889e76964fb1ead203bb23a6ed374663d.goal: Tests whether differentiable, physics-informed hydrologic models can extrapolate to ungauged regions and credibly predict decadal streamflow trends for climate change impact assessment.
cbd319e889e76964fb1ead203bb23a6ed374663d.architecture: Differentiable process-based hydrologic model (delta model) whose parameters are produced by a regionalized deep neural network (LSTM-based parameterization pipeline), compared against a pure LSTM.
cbd319e889e76964fb1ead203bb23a6ed374663d.data: CAMELS basins in the contiguous US with several meteorological forcings (e.g. Daymet, Maurer, NLDAS); random ungauged-basin (PUB) and regional holdout (PUR) cross-validation, plus decadal trend evaluation.
cbd319e889e76964fb1ead203bb23a6ed374663d.result: Delta models approach or beat LSTM in PUB and clearly beat it in PUR on daily metrics and mean/high-flow trends, though low-flow trends are worse; untrained evapotranspiration keeps good seasonality and parameter fields stay spatially stable.
cbd319e889e76964fb1ead203bb23a6ed374663d.open_work: Applying delta models to regional and global simulations, improving low-flow processes, and assimilating multi-source observations for climate impact studies.
cbd319e889e76964fb1ead203bb23a6ed374663d.issues: Low-flow trend skill lags LSTM; performance depends on forcing product; evaluated on US basins only, and trend credibility is judged on historical decades rather than true future climates.

0bde8f0da2dff6f8087f2245466cdb1b49118d2d.goal: Improves short-term solar irradiance forecasting to support integration of photovoltaic generation into the grid.
0bde8f0da2dff6f8087f2245466cdb1b49118d2d.architecture: Wavelet neural network with mixed wavelet activation functions in the hidden layer, a neural network variant combining wavelet decomposition ideas with an MLP.
0bde8f0da2dff6f8087f2245466cdb1b49118d2d.data: Not reported in the abstract; presumably measured solar irradiance time series from ground stations.
0bde8f0da2dff6f8087f2245466cdb1b49118d2d.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title implies the mixed wavelet network improves short-term forecasts over conventional benchmarks.
0bde8f0da2dff6f8087f2245466cdb1b49118d2d.open_work: Testing across more climates and forecast horizons and combining with sky imagery or NWP inputs.
0bde8f0da2dff6f8087f2245466cdb1b49118d2d.issues: Abstract unavailable, so data, horizon and gains could not be verified; univariate time-series models typically struggle with sudden cloud-driven ramps.

0cd10de0a5b92032fbf960003a295ae9f4f5ded4.goal: Forecasts solar irradiance for photovoltaic systems to reduce uncertainty in PV power output.
0cd10de0a5b92032fbf960003a295ae9f4f5ded4.architecture: Machine learning forecasting methods for irradiance; the specific algorithms are not reported in the available metadata.
0cd10de0a5b92032fbf960003a295ae9f4f5ded4.data: Not reported in the abstract; presumably measured irradiance and meteorological observations at PV sites.
0cd10de0a5b92032fbf960003a295ae9f4f5ded4.result: Not reported in the abstract; the paper presumably shows machine learning outperforms simple reference forecasts.
0cd10de0a5b92032fbf960003a295ae9f4f5ded4.open_work: Extending to longer horizons and different climates, and linking irradiance forecasts directly to PV power prediction.
0cd10de0a5b92032fbf960003a295ae9f4f5ded4.issues: Abstract unavailable, so methods, data and skill could not be verified; summary is based on the title only.

3884733586fdf9b2ef9f00c12285c272ae640aa1.goal: Extends machine-learning model induction from lumped to semi-distributed rainfall-runoff models, because lumped models lose meaning in large catchments with heterogeneous forcing and properties.
3884733586fdf9b2ef9f00c12285c272ae640aa1.architecture: Genetic programming (evolutionary computation) framework, MIKA-SHA, that automatically assembles interpretable semi-distributed conceptual rainfall-runoff models from FUSE and SUPERFLEX building blocks.
3884733586fdf9b2ef9f00c12285c272ae640aa1.data: Rainfall-runoff data for the Red Creek catchment near Vestry, Mississippi, USA.
3884733586fdf9b2ef9f00c12285c272ae640aa1.result: Induced model architectures agree with previous research and fieldwork insights on the watershed and are readily interpretable by hydrologists; quantitative skill is not given in the abstract.
3884733586fdf9b2ef9f00c12285c272ae640aa1.open_work: Coupling the framework with other building-block libraries and testing on more and larger catchments.
3884733586fdf9b2ef9f00c12285c272ae640aa1.issues: Single test catchment; computationally intensive search; no quantitative comparison with data-driven models such as LSTM reported in the abstract.

aa310958f482c7bd64ad5430b3fd279a626452e3.goal: Shows that a deep learning rainfall-runoff model can exploit multiple meteorological forcing products together rather than relying on a single product.
aa310958f482c7bd64ad5430b3fd279a626452e3.architecture: Long short-term memory network (LSTM) taking several precipitation and meteorological forcing products simultaneously as input.
aa310958f482c7bd64ad5430b3fd279a626452e3.data: CAMELS basins in the continental US with forcings from NLDAS, Maurer and Daymet.
aa310958f482c7bd64ad5430b3fd279a626452e3.result: Combining forcing products in a single LSTM significantly improves streamflow simulation accuracy over any individual product; the LSTM blends precipitation products differently by location and by hydrograph part.
aa310958f482c7bd64ad5430b3fd279a626452e3.open_work: Extending to more forcing products and regions, and to operational forecasting with forecast inputs.
aa310958f482c7bd64ad5430b3fd279a626452e3.issues: US-only with gridded products that are themselves correlated; benefit relies on all products being available at prediction time.

da67128bdfadc25e420a37d3e78197a46bca1b13.goal: Systematically compares deep learning architectures for soil moisture prediction to identify network design principles and understand how models use data.
da67128bdfadc25e420a37d3e78197a46bca1b13.architecture: Ten deep learning structures (three basic feature extractors such as LSTM, CNN-type and MLP-type networks, plus seven hybrids including feature-attention LSTM and GAN-based LSTM), interpreted with SHAP and t-SNE; three classical ML baselines.
da67128bdfadc25e420a37d3e78197a46bca1b13.data: Soil moisture observations across different soil textures and depths with meteorological drivers; specific sites and products not reported in the abstract.
da67128bdfadc25e420a37d3e78197a46bca1b13.result: LSTM's temporal modelling suits soil moisture forecasting; feature-attention LSTM and GAN-LSTM further improve accuracy, showing benefits of attention and adversarial training. Code for 13 models is open source.
da67128bdfadc25e420a37d3e78197a46bca1b13.open_work: Applying the design principles to other hydrology problems and testing transfer across regions.
da67128bdfadc25e420a37d3e78197a46bca1b13.issues: Site and dataset details are not given in the abstract; skill gains are modest and interpretability analyses are qualitative.

970e8f35dba8f6571a4b608780952adc7f429f10.goal: Predicts county-level crop yields across the US by exploiting both geospatial and temporal information, as climate change raises food-security concerns.
970e8f35dba8f6571a4b608780952adc7f429f10.architecture: Graph neural network combined with a recurrent neural network (GNN-RNN), where counties are graph nodes and the RNN models year-to-year dynamics.
970e8f35dba8f6571a4b608780952adc7f429f10.data: Over 2,000 counties in 41 US states, 1981–2019, with weather, land surface and soil features.
970e8f35dba8f6571a4b608780952adc7f429f10.result: The GNN-RNN consistently outperforms linear, tree-based and deep learning baselines on multiple metrics, presented as the first nationwide county-level ML yield model embedding geographical knowledge.
970e8f35dba8f6571a4b608780952adc7f429f10.open_work: Extending to other crops and countries, and to projections under climate change scenarios.
970e8f35dba8f6571a4b608780952adc7f429f10.issues: US-only; yield trends from technology and management may be confounded with weather signal; interpretability of learned spatial relations is limited.

d22335a6a04c5d243b66e2803675945c13288007.goal: Quantifies uncertainty in projected global crop yields from both climate models and crop models under climate change.
d22335a6a04c5d243b66e2803675945c13288007.architecture: Statistical crop model emulators of nine process-based global gridded crop models (GGCMI), used to run a large ensemble; not a deep learning method.
d22335a6a04c5d243b66e2803675945c13288007.data: Up to 45 CMIP5 and 34 CMIP6 climate projections under three forcing scenarios, for maize, spring and winter wheat, rice and soybean.
d22335a6a04c5d243b66e2803675945c13288007.result: Climate and crop models contribute roughly equally to uncertainty; median caloric production impact is more negative under CMIP6 (+1% to -19%) than CMIP5 (+5% to -13%); wheat and maize are dominated by crop-model spread, soybean and rice by climate.
d22335a6a04c5d243b66e2803675945c13288007.open_work: Developing consistent, process-level crop model testing and weighting ensembles by plausibility.
d22335a6a04c5d243b66e2803675945c13288007.issues: Unbalanced crop model ensemble with an equal-plausibility assumption; emulators simplify process-model behaviour.

1d4c3613608045c1a6219cd8b00da738dc6bff4f.goal: Combines conceptual hydrological models and machine learning so streamflow predictions are both skilful and physically consistent.
1d4c3613608045c1a6219cd8b00da738dc6bff4f.architecture: Physics-informed machine learning hybrid in which the abcd conceptual water-balance model structure is coupled with ML regressors that predict intermediate (evapotranspiration) and target (streamflow) variables.
1d4c3613608045c1a6219cd8b00da738dc6bff4f.data: Monthly streamflow and actual evapotranspiration for the Narmada river basin, India.
1d4c3613608045c1a6219cd8b00da738dc6bff4f.result: The PIML model outperforms both the purely conceptual abcd model and standalone ML algorithms while preserving water-balance consistency.
1d4c3613608045c1a6219cd8b00da738dc6bff4f.open_work: Extending to daily time steps, more basins and flood risk assessment applications.
1d4c3613608045c1a6219cd8b00da738dc6bff4f.issues: Single basin at monthly resolution; specific ML algorithms and quantitative gains not detailed in the abstract.

45f0476e46bbfa995c594c2588604541cf0123ca.goal: Evaluates random forests for 1-day-ahead streamflow forecasting in watersheds driven by both rainfall and snowmelt, beyond the usual rainfall-dominated settings.
45f0476e46bbfa995c594c2588604541cf0123ca.architecture: Random forest regression benchmarked against naive persistence and multiple linear regression.
45f0476e46bbfa995c594c2588604541cf0123ca.data: 86 watersheds in the Pacific Northwest, classified as rainfall-dominated, transient or snowmelt-dominated.
45f0476e46bbfa995c594c2588604541cf0123ca.result: Random forests perform better in snowmelt-driven watersheds, but improvements over benchmarks are largest in rainfall-driven ones; skill degrades with steeper slopes and sandier soils.
45f0476e46bbfa995c594c2588604541cf0123ca.open_work: Jointly considering variable importance measures with physical processes and testing longer lead times.
45f0476e46bbfa995c594c2588604541cf0123ca.issues: Only 1-day lead time; two variable importance measures disagree, limiting inference; regional study.

df0506f225bcd6840f709439b1cd10264734c1ea.goal: Forecasts daily global solar irradiance to support solar power generation planning.
df0506f225bcd6840f709439b1cd10264734c1ea.architecture: Machine learning forecasting methods for daily irradiance; the specific algorithms are not reported in the available metadata.
df0506f225bcd6840f709439b1cd10264734c1ea.data: Not reported in the abstract; presumably ground-measured irradiance and meteorological data.
df0506f225bcd6840f709439b1cd10264734c1ea.open_work: Testing at more sites and horizons and comparing with NWP-based forecasts.
df0506f225bcd6840f709439b1cd10264734c1ea.issues: Abstract unavailable, so methods, data and skill could not be verified; summary is based on the title only.

2311ab7fb495d82defa6156bf0b04e38fcb5046e.goal: Improves surface solar irradiance forecasts for the Brazilian Northeastern region to support solar energy integration.
2311ab7fb495d82defa6156bf0b04e38fcb5046e.architecture: Numerical weather prediction model forecasts post-processed with artificial neural networks (MLP) for bias correction or refinement.
2311ab7fb495d82defa6156bf0b04e38fcb5046e.data: NWP irradiance forecasts and ground measurements in Northeastern Brazil; specific model configuration and period not reported in the available metadata.
2311ab7fb495d82defa6156bf0b04e38fcb5046e.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title implies ANN post-processing improves NWP irradiance forecasts.
2311ab7fb495d82defa6156bf0b04e38fcb5046e.open_work: Extending to more stations and using additional predictors or satellite data.
2311ab7fb495d82defa6156bf0b04e38fcb5046e.issues: Abstract unavailable, so details and skill could not be verified; regional study.

bc4df5fd48434d1a38f501dbb5522bf1363bf634.goal: Evaluates global hydrological model flood simulations and improves them with machine learning, since GHM-based flood estimates are too inaccurate for most applications.
bc4df5fd48434d1a38f501dbb5522bf1363bf634.architecture: Hybrid physics-ML approach: LSTM post-processor taking basin-averaged meteorology and simulated discharge from GHM-CaMa-Flood chains as inputs to predict observed discharge.
bc4df5fd48434d1a38f501dbb5522bf1363bf634.data: Five GHMs under the ISIMIP2a protocol, 1971–2010, evaluated against 1,032 gauges from the Global Streamflow Indices and Metadata Archive (GSIM).
bc4df5fd48434d1a38f501dbb5522bf1363bf634.result: GHMs capture peak amplitude reasonably but timing poorly, with large differences across climate zones; the LSTM drastically improves global flood simulations, especially peak magnitude.
bc4df5fd48434d1a38f501dbb5522bf1363bf634.open_work: Using hybrid GHM-ML approaches for robust flood risk assessment and projections.
bc4df5fd48434d1a38f501dbb5522bf1363bf634.issues: Post-processing requires gauges and may not transfer to ungauged basins or future climates; inherits forcing biases.

0bf7d48ad5531966568d81ba2da4df49559dcede.goal: Examines whether pooling data from heterogeneous regions helps deep learning hydrologic models, challenging the practice of stratified regional models.
0bf7d48ad5531966568d81ba2da4df49559dcede.architecture: Time-series deep learning models, LSTM networks, trained on pooled versus region-stratified data.
0bf7d48ad5531966568d81ba2da4df49559dcede.data: Two hydrologic examples: soil moisture (SMAP-based) and streamflow (CAMELS) across the contiguous US.
0bf7d48ad5531966568d81ba2da4df49559dcede.result: Models improve when data from characteristically different regions are pooled (data synergy); modest diversity beats homogeneous training sets of similar size.
0bf7d48ad5531966568d81ba2da4df49559dcede.open_work: Promoting data sharing and building large diverse datasets to better represent extremes and future scenarios.
0bf7d48ad5531966568d81ba2da4df49559dcede.issues: Demonstrated for US datasets and LSTM only; mechanisms of synergy are not fully explained.

58b56ea65726b9f3c19a7409841c3b0632a890b8.goal: Investigates how future climate and land use changes alter flood susceptibility in the Tajan watershed, Iran.
58b56ea65726b9f3c19a7409841c3b0632a890b8.architecture: Random forest and Bayesian generalized linear model for flood susceptibility mapping, with land change modeler (LCM) for land use projection and LARS-WG weather generator for downscaled climate.
58b56ea65726b9f3c19a7409841c3b0632a890b8.data: 262 historical flood locations and 12 conditioning factors; land use 1990–2019 projected to 2040; climate 1990–2015 projected to 2020–2040 under RCP2.6 and RCP8.5.
58b56ea65726b9f3c19a7409841c3b0632a890b8.result: Random forest (AUC 0.91) beats GLMbayes (0.847); elevation, distance from river, land use, slope and rainfall dominate; projected forest and rangeland loss and rainfall increase raise flood probability downstream.
