58b56ea65726b9f3c19a7409841c3b0632a890b8.open_work: Using ensembles of climate models and dynamic hydrological modelling to refine projections.
58b56ea65726b9f3c19a7409841c3b0632a890b8.issues: Susceptibility is static and presence-based; single weather generator downscaling; future factor changes assumed to apply directly to a statistically trained model.

0b1b1bfe7129ad9a906217ffe273ebc8cf2b7efe.goal: Assesses whether data-driven machine learning models can match or replace process-based hydrologic models for streamflow simulation.
0b1b1bfe7129ad9a906217ffe273ebc8cf2b7efe.architecture: Comparison of an artificial neural network (MLP) and an LSTM against process models SAC-SMA, Xinanjiang and the distributed CREST model.
0b1b1bfe7129ad9a906217ffe273ebc8cf2b7efe.data: Four watersheds across the CONUS with different hydro-climatic conditions and input scenarios, including delayed inputs.
0b1b1bfe7129ad9a906217ffe273ebc8cf2b7efe.result: ML models are biased with baseline inputs but reach high accuracy with delayed inputs; ANN excels where rainfall drives runoff; ML is better for high flows, process models for low flows.
0b1b1bfe7129ad9a906217ffe273ebc8cf2b7efe.open_work: Large-scale tests of transferability and scalability, e.g. in the style of the Distributed Model Intercomparison Projects.
0b1b1bfe7129ad9a906217ffe273ebc8cf2b7efe.issues: Only four watersheds; results depend on input lag design; limited generalization claims.

246f3eec18cf23dd69b996ad9294dfe44384a4b5.goal: Improves long-term forecasting of stream water level using climate mode indices, rainfall and periodicity for water resources planning.
246f3eec18cf23dd69b996ad9294dfe44384a4b5.architecture: Hybrid deep learning: LSTM and gated recurrent unit (GRU) networks with Boruta random forest feature selection (BRF-LSTM) applied to lagged predictors.
246f3eec18cf23dd69b996ad9294dfe44384a4b5.data: Six gauging stations in the Murray-Darling Basin, Australia, with lagged climate mode indices, rainfall and a monthly periodicity factor.
246f3eec18cf23dd69b996ad9294dfe44384a4b5.result: BRF-LSTM outperforms benchmarks, with over 98% of errors within ±0.015 m and RRMSE about 1.30%; periodicity improves skill at four stations.
246f3eec18cf23dd69b996ad9294dfe44384a4b5.open_work: Applying the approach to other hydrological variables influenced by low-frequency climate variability.
246f3eec18cf23dd69b996ad9294dfe44384a4b5.issues: Few stations; very low errors may partly reflect water-level persistence; risk of selection bias from feature screening.

837e9281f85b56dd22aaeab39ce2bfcdfb64cb7e.goal: Exploits spatial and temporal dependencies across many basins to improve streamflow forecasting in gauged and ungauged basins.
837e9281f85b56dd22aaeab39ce2bfcdfb64cb7e.architecture: Graph neural networks (ChebNet, graph convolutional network, GraphWaveNet) with basins as nodes, compared with an LSTM baseline.
837e9281f85b56dd22aaeab39ce2bfcdfb64cb7e.data: CAMELS large-sample hydrology dataset, with transductive (fixed graph) and inductive (variable graph, ungauged basins) settings.
837e9281f85b56dd22aaeab39ce2bfcdfb64cb7e.result: GNNs are robust and computationally efficient, matching or beating the LSTM baseline; edge- and node-level analysis interprets learned relations.
837e9281f85b56dd22aaeab39ce2bfcdfb64cb7e.open_work: Incorporating river network topology and more data sources into graph learning.
837e9281f85b56dd22aaeab39ce2bfcdfb64cb7e.issues: Graphs built from basin similarity rather than physical connectivity; US-only; gains over LSTM are modest.

f206e21ba8dc8677062714837020a790dc674aa9.goal: Simulates and predicts suprapermafrost groundwater level variation in response to climate change in a permafrost region.
f206e21ba8dc8677062714837020a790dc674aa9.architecture: Artificial neural network relating climate drivers to groundwater level; the network design is not reported in the available metadata.
f206e21ba8dc8677062714837020a790dc674aa9.data: Not reported in the abstract; presumably observed groundwater levels and meteorological data at a permafrost site, likely on the Tibetan Plateau.
f206e21ba8dc8677062714837020a790dc674aa9.open_work: Projecting groundwater response under future climate scenarios and linking to active-layer dynamics.
f206e21ba8dc8677062714837020a790dc674aa9.issues: Abstract unavailable; study region, data and skill could not be verified; statistical models may not extrapolate under permafrost degradation.

806a27e12d1d6f6056031a452dfb9a57648ca329.goal: Develops and benchmarks machine learning models for daily river water temperature prediction to support water management under climate change.
806a27e12d1d6f6056031a452dfb9a57648ca329.architecture: Six models: stepwise linear regression, random forest, XGBoost, feed-forward neural networks (MLP) and two recurrent neural networks, tuned by Bayesian optimization, versus linear regression and air2stream.
806a27e12d1d6f6056031a452dfb9a57648ca329.data: 10 Austrian catchments (200 to 96,000 km2) with daily air temperature, runoff, precipitation and global radiation.
806a27e12d1d6f6056031a452dfb9a57648ca329.result: Mean RMSE of 0.55 °C versus 1.55 °C for linear regression and 0.98 °C for air2stream; FNN and XGBoost each best in 4 of 10 catchments, RNNs best in the largest.
806a27e12d1d6f6056031a452dfb9a57648ca329.open_work: Regional multi-catchment models and applications to future climate; R package wateRtemp released.
806a27e12d1d6f6056031a452dfb9a57648ca329.issues: High sensitivity to hyperparameters (FNN RMSE standard deviation 1.60 °C); single-catchment models; Austrian setting only.

d218f0e2713e7e03c0980866d42a0917a4ee8925.goal: Automates the construction of physically meaningful rainfall-runoff models from flexible modelling frameworks, avoiding time-consuming manual trial of configurations.
d218f0e2713e7e03c0980866d42a0917a4ee8925.architecture: Genetic programming (evolutionary computation) model induction toolkit (ML-RR-MI) that searches SUPERFLEX and FUSE building blocks to build lumped conceptual models.
d218f0e2713e7e03c0980866d42a0917a4ee8925.data: Rainfall-runoff data for the Blackwater River basin, Alabama, USA.
d218f0e2713e7e03c0980866d42a0917a4ee8925.result: Evolved model configurations are consistent with fieldwork and previous research findings; quantitative skill is not reported in the abstract.
d218f0e2713e7e03c0980866d42a0917a4ee8925.open_work: Extending to semi-distributed models (later done in MIKA-SHA) and other building-block libraries.
d218f0e2713e7e03c0980866d42a0917a4ee8925.issues: Single basin; computational cost of the search; no comparison with deep learning in the abstract.

496e280220841ac4461285c62178dd8fbd54f15c.goal: Tests whether machine learning models can be used for hydrological inference, not just prediction, using flood events across Germany.
496e280220841ac4461285c62178dd8fbd54f15c.architecture: Artificial neural networks (MLP) and random forest compared with multiple linear regression, interpreted using permuted feature importance.
496e280220841ac4461285c62178dd8fbd54f15c.data: Large dataset of flood events across Germany with catchment and event predictors.
496e280220841ac4461285c62178dd8fbd54f15c.result: ML models beat linear regression and reflect basic hydrological principles, but feature importances differ across algorithms, revealing equifinality that hampers inference.
496e280220841ac4461285c62178dd8fbd54f15c.open_work: Using multiple algorithms and interpretation methods within cross-validation when doing ML-based inference.
496e280220841ac4461285c62178dd8fbd54f15c.issues: Inference conclusions depend on chosen algorithms; correlated predictors complicate importance estimates.

ee0b4d9f02f0f271f41976c9582daaaefb8e645a.goal: Fills the roughly 1-year gap between GRACE and GRACE-FO total water storage records to maintain data continuity.
ee0b4d9f02f0f271f41976c9582daaaefb8e645a.architecture: Automated machine learning (AutoML) workflow selecting and tuning six ML model types (including tree ensembles and neural networks) per grid cell, with model combination.
ee0b4d9f02f0f271f41976c9582daaaefb8e645a.data: GRACE/GRACE-FO total water storage anomalies over CONUS with meteorological and climatic predictors.
ee0b4d9f02f0f271f41976c9582daaaefb8e645a.result: Mean gridwise NSE about 0.85, correlation about 0.95 and normalized RMSE about 0.09 on test data; skill holds in the mission gap and GRACE-FO period; no single algorithm is best everywhere.
ee0b4d9f02f0f271f41976c9582daaaefb8e645a.open_work: Applying AutoML to larger-scale hydrological prediction systems and global reconstructions.
ee0b4d9f02f0f271f41976c9582daaaefb8e645a.issues: Gridwise models ignore spatial dependence; reconstruction in the gap cannot be directly verified; CONUS only.

f31ba7550737dda8103dba465c389f158e93924f.goal: Evaluates neural network models for site-specific solar PV power forecasting using NWP output and local weather observations.
f31ba7550737dda8103dba465c389f158e93924f.architecture: Neural network models using NWP and observation inputs; the network designs are not reported in the available metadata.
f31ba7550737dda8103dba465c389f158e93924f.data: Not reported in the abstract; NWP forecast data and weather/PV observations at specific sites, likely in Finland given the authors.
f31ba7550737dda8103dba465c389f158e93924f.open_work: Testing across more sites and seasons and combining NWP with satellite nowcasts.
f31ba7550737dda8103dba465c389f158e93924f.issues: Abstract unavailable; data, horizons and skill could not be verified; high-latitude conditions (snow, low sun) may limit transferability.

de172ff1f381189723068ce17f5177f5b9d694a3.goal: Benchmarks deep learning models for very short-term solar irradiance forecasting from sky images, to support grid and plant operations.
de172ff1f381189723068ce17f5177f5b9d694a3.architecture: Four common deep learning architectures (convolutional neural network, CNN-LSTM, 3D CNN and ConvLSTM-type spatiotemporal models) fed with hemispherical sky image sequences and exogenous variables.
de172ff1f381189723068ce17f5177f5b9d694a3.data: Sequences of hemispherical sky images with irradiance measurements from a single site; one year held out for testing.
de172ff1f381189723068ce17f5177f5b9d694a3.result: Encoding spatiotemporal image sequences helps, with 10-min-ahead forecast skill of 20.4% versus smart persistence, but models behave like a very smart persistence and miss events such as clouds obscuring the sun.
de172ff1f381189723068ce17f5177f5b9d694a3.open_work: Shifting from reactive to anticipatory forecasting that predicts large irradiance ramps.
de172ff1f381189723068ce17f5177f5b9d694a3.issues: Single site; models lag ramps; evaluation limited to short horizons.

698f1acf1974926b6e7ef020652ac76cb195c942.goal: Interprets LSTM rainfall-runoff models to address the opacity that limits their acceptance in environmental sciences.
698f1acf1974926b6e7ef020652ac76cb195c942.architecture: Long short-term memory network (LSTM) analysed by inspecting internal memory cell states and gradients.
698f1acf1974926b6e7ef020652ac76cb195c942.data: Two catchments, one snow-influenced and one without, from the CAMELS US dataset.
698f1acf1974926b6e7ef020652ac76cb195c942.result: The trained LSTM internally learns patterns consistent with hydrological understanding, e.g. cell states resembling snow storage and dynamic reservoirs.
698f1acf1974926b6e7ef020652ac76cb195c942.open_work: Systematic interpretability tools for larger samples of basins and other hydrologic variables.
698f1acf1974926b6e7ef020652ac76cb195c942.issues: Only two catchments; qualitative interpretation; links between cells and physical stores are not unique.

049c95ca128fe891f197cd84ca35e15b055c7682.goal: Improves crop evapotranspiration prediction for agricultural water management by accounting for dynamic crop coefficients and precipitation.
049c95ca128fe891f197cd84ca35e15b055c7682.architecture: Three-layer back-propagation neural network (MLP, 4-10-1) trained with Levenberg-Marquardt, compared with multiple linear regression.
049c95ca128fe891f197cd84ca35e15b055c7682.data: Eddy covariance measured crop evapotranspiration with meteorological data (max/min air temperature, sunshine hours, precipitation) and crop coefficients.
049c95ca128fe891f197cd84ca35e15b055c7682.result: BP network reaches R2 0.87 and 91.44% accuracy versus 0.79 and 82.96% for regression; dynamic Kc improves accuracy by 19% over FAO-56 Kc, exceeding 95% with precipitation.
049c95ca128fe891f197cd84ca35e15b055c7682.open_work: Applying to other crops, sites and seasons and to irrigation scheduling.
049c95ca128fe891f197cd84ca35e15b055c7682.issues: Single site and crop details unspecified in the abstract; small network and dataset limit generalization.

1ee64baf0fed552ede42ab8416908279afddd5fc.goal: Assesses whether deep learning hydrologic models produce physically realistic streamflow projections under warming.
1ee64baf0fed552ede42ab8416908279afddd5fc.architecture: Regional LSTM benchmarked against process models HYMOD, SAC-SMA and VIC; hybrid variants with process-model outputs as extra targets (multi-output LSTM) or input features.
1ee64baf0fed552ede42ab8416908279afddd5fc.data: Daily streamflow in 15 California watersheds forced with warming scenarios, plus an LSTM trained on over 500 US watersheds.
1ee64baf0fed552ede42ab8416908279afddd5fc.result: LSTM reproduces hydrograph shifts but in some basins unrealistically increases the runoff ratio; SAC-SMA ET as input fixes this, but not with VIC or HYMOD; the 500-basin LSTM gives more realistic responses.
1ee64baf0fed552ede42ab8416908279afddd5fc.open_work: Hybrid modelling and large diverse training sets to make LSTM climate projections trustworthy.
1ee64baf0fed552ede42ab8416908279afddd5fc.issues: Synthetic warming scenarios rather than full climate projections; hybrid benefit depends on process model fidelity.

569bcc4081cae71935b367d773b6f8254091a72b.goal: Combines deep learning accuracy with physical mechanisms in distributed hydrological modelling for very large basins.
569bcc4081cae71935b367d773b6f8254091a72b.architecture: Differentiable framework encoding the HydroPy process model as a neural network, plus a parameterization neural network from watershed attributes and NN replacement modules (e.g. for potential evapotranspiration).
569bcc4081cae71935b367d773b6f8254091a72b.data: Amazon Basin (about 6 million km2), trained jointly on streamflow observations and GRACE total water storage.
569bcc4081cae71935b367d773b6f8254091a72b.result: Median NSE of 0.83 for streamflow and 0.77 for total water storage, 41% and 35% higher than original HydroPy; NN replacement for Penman-Monteith yields more plausible PET.
569bcc4081cae71935b367d773b6f8254091a72b.open_work: Applying the framework to other basins and global modelling, and further interpreting learned parameters.
569bcc4081cae71935b367d773b6f8254091a72b.issues: Single basin; process replacements reduce interpretability; dependent on GRACE resolution.

f793143eec39b2ed685fca44a7cd29948c2a39d2.goal: Reduces uncertainty in snow water equivalent (SWE) mapping from aerial lidar snow depth, which lacks spatially explicit snow density, in semiarid Arizona mountain forests that supply surface water.
f793143eec39b2ed685fca44a7cd29948c2a39d2.architecture: Artificial neural network (MLP) that distributes field snow density measurements spatially; density maps are combined with bias-corrected lidar snow depth to produce SWE maps.
f793143eec39b2ed685fca44a7cd29948c2a39d2.data: About 300 field snow density measurements, aerial lidar snow depth bias-corrected with ~4,000 geolocated field depth observations, two sites on Arizona's Mogollon Rim, February and March 2017; SNOTEL comparison.
f793143eec39b2ed685fca44a7cd29948c2a39d2.result: Snow density varies less spatially than depth in late winter; the lidar-ANN SWE estimates differ by up to 30% from SWE computed with SNOTEL density, and point-station representativeness changes between midwinter and late winter.
f793143eec39b2ed685fca44a7cd29948c2a39d2.open_work: Extending the approach to more sites, years and snow conditions, and testing transfer of density models without dense field surveys.
f793143eec39b2ed685fca44a7cd29948c2a39d2.issues: Two sites and two survey dates only; relies on intensive field campaigns; no independent SWE validation beyond field data; generalization untested.

12ff9b26f3053246983edac4a30eab13ef752fa2.goal: Quantifies the probability that meteorological drought propagates into ecological (vegetation) drought of different magnitudes in northwestern China, to support ecological conservation.
12ff9b26f3053246983edac4a30eab13ef752fa2.architecture: Hybrid of machine learning classifiers and a four-dimensional C-vine copula; 11 classifiers compared, with quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA) best; drought events identified with a three-dimensional spatiotemporal clustering method.
12ff9b26f3053246983edac4a30eab13ef752fa2.data: Meteorological and ecological drought indices over northwestern China, 1982–2020; 130 meteorological and 184 ecological drought events, 46 paired propagation events. Specific input products not reported in the abstract.
12ff9b26f3053246983edac4a30eab13ef752fa2.result: QDA performs best among 11 models; ecological droughts last longer but have smaller area and severity than meteorological droughts; the hybrid method handles large regions better than traditional propagation methods.
12ff9b26f3053246983edac4a30eab13ef752fa2.open_work: Applying the framework to other regions and drought types, and to future climate scenarios to project propagation risk.
12ff9b26f3053246983edac4a30eab13ef752fa2.issues: Only 46 paired propagation events for training; results depend on the event-pairing overlap rule and drought index choices; skill metrics not given in the abstract.

efe6e287e46878b1e59e52935407c393e3297e40.goal: Evaluates how well artificial intelligence models forecast floods and droughts in contrasting arid and tropical climate regions.
efe6e287e46878b1e59e52935407c393e3297e40.architecture: Comparison of several AI/machine learning forecasting models (neural network-based); exact model set not reported here (abstract unavailable).
efe6e287e46878b1e59e52935407c393e3297e40.data: Hydrometeorological observations from arid and tropical study catchments; specific datasets not reported.
efe6e287e46878b1e59e52935407c393e3297e40.result: Not available from the abstract; the study compares model skill for flood and drought forecasting across the two climate settings.
efe6e287e46878b1e59e52935407c393e3297e40.open_work: Testing across more catchments and climates and on longer lead times.
efe6e287e46878b1e59e52935407c393e3297e40.issues: Abstract missing; details of models, data and results not verified.

42a22f8126c63dc4ae990e7ffa7dfbf89da1227e.goal: Assesses LSTM streamflow prediction in poorly monitored, data-scarce watersheds and addresses overfitting, uncertainty quantification and out-of-distribution prediction.
42a22f8126c63dc4ae990e7ffa7dfbf89da1227e.architecture: LSTM networks with L2 and dropout regularization, a Bayesian LSTM for uncertainty quantification, and a physics-informed hybrid LSTM coupled with a hydrologic model for out-of-distribution prediction.
42a22f8126c63dc4ae990e7ffa7dfbf89da1227e.data: Daily streamflow in two diverse sets of catchments with and without snow influence, with calibration records as short as two years.
42a22f8126c63dc4ae990e7ffa7dfbf89da1227e.result: With similar hydrologic variability, LSTM reaches NSE above 0.8 from two years of data; under shifted variability the hybrid model generalizes better; Bayesian and hybrid LSTMs do not overfit and the Bayesian LSTM gives useful uncertainty.
42a22f8126c63dc4ae990e7ffa7dfbf89da1227e.open_work: Applying the approaches to more data-scarce regions and combining Bayesian and physics-informed components.
42a22f8126c63dc4ae990e7ffa7dfbf89da1227e.issues: Small number of case-study catchments; out-of-distribution skill depends on the process model in the hybrid; quantitative uncertainty calibration not reported in the abstract.

27c54a8c6b6ca248295a3ce813a2fe7b2f5ecd92.goal: Determines which dam-influenced basins can be modeled by deep learning for continental-scale daily streamflow prediction using readily available information.
27c54a8c6b6ca248295a3ce813a2fe7b2f5ecd92.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) networks trained on basin groups defined by reservoir degree of regulation (dor), purpose and diversion, in a divide-and-conquer strategy.
27c54a8c6b6ca248295a3ce813a2fe7b2f5ecd92.data: 3,557 basins over the contiguous United States (83% dammed), extending reference-basin datasets with reservoir attributes (e.g. GAGES-II-type information).
27c54a8c6b6ca248295a3ce813a2fe7b2f5ecd92.result: Training on all basins gives median NSE 0.74; pooled training yields median NSE 0.73, 0.78 and 0.71 for zero-, small- and large-dor basins; reference-trained models transfer poorly and migrating models between dor groups fails.
27c54a8c6b6ca248295a3ce813a2fe7b2f5ecd92.open_work: Separately modeling reservoirs for irrigation, fire protection, hydropower and flood control, and explicit representation of large-dor reservoirs.
27c54a8c6b6ca248295a3ce813a2fe7b2f5ecd92.issues: Large-dor basins with irrigation dams remain poorly simulated; no explicit reservoir operation data; dammed basins must be in the training set.

cc228fab0cfbac8d326bf1082f434ebf946b2f33.goal: Develops a fast basin-scale river network model for streamflow forecasting, since high-resolution vector-based river network models are computationally demanding.
cc228fab0cfbac8d326bf1082f434ebf946b2f33.architecture: Multistage physics-guided graph neural network (GNN) pretrained to emulate a vector-based river routing model, fine-tuned on gauge observations, with graph-based data fusion for bias correction and graph coarsening for scalability.
cc228fab0cfbac8d326bf1082f434ebf946b2f33.data: Outputs of a high-resolution vector-based river network model and streamflow gauge observations in a snow-dominated western US watershed and a larger basin.
cc228fab0cfbac8d326bf1082f434ebf946b2f33.result: The GNN surrogate reproduces the process model with median KGE above 0.97; data fusion improves KGE by up to 50% at cross-validation gauges; coarsened graphs give comparable skill at a fraction of training cost.
cc228fab0cfbac8d326bf1082f434ebf946b2f33.open_work: Scaling to continental river networks and determining the degree of physical realism needed in large-scale GNN river models.
cc228fab0cfbac8d326bf1082f434ebf946b2f33.issues: Surrogate inherits biases of the process-based model; tested in a limited number of basins; forecasting skill under extremes not detailed.

5f885290a10e45351f8cba536d7f574f63ec3f78.goal: Projects future streamflow in the Himalayan Sutlej River basin under climate change for water resource planning.
5f885290a10e45351f8cba536d7f574f63ec3f78.architecture: Comparison of Gaussian linear regression, generalized additive model, MARS, artificial neural network (MLP), random forest and a 1D convolutional neural network; random forest selected for projections.
5f885290a10e45351f8cba536d7f574f63ec3f78.data: Daily data 1979–2009 at Kasol for training; bias-corrected CMIP6 output from six GCMs downscaled to 0.25° under SSP245 and SSP585 for 2041–2070 and 2071–2100.
5f885290a10e45351f8cba536d7f574f63ec3f78.result: Random forest performs best (test R2 0.78, NSE 0.71, KGE 0.82); mean annual streamflow rises about 0.8–1.4%, monsoon flow increases ~10–13%, while pre-monsoon and winter flows decline (winter ~-22%).
5f885290a10e45351f8cba536d7f574f63ec3f78.open_work: Incorporating glacier and snowmelt dynamics and land-use change, and assessing downstream agricultural water impacts.
5f885290a10e45351f8cba536d7f574f63ec3f78.issues: Statistical models trained on historical relationships may not hold under future climate; GCM and downscaling uncertainty; glacier retreat not explicitly modeled.

c4515857baf4481227ecf203bf7570ca6457f2e1.goal: Nowcasts urban flood inundation during extreme weather events by combining physics-based and human-sensed data to improve situational awareness.
c4515857baf4481227ecf203bf7570ca6457f2e1.architecture: Attention-based spatial-temporal graph convolution network (ASTGCN), a graph neural network with spatial and temporal graph convolution modules and attention.
c4515857baf4481227ecf203bf7570ca6457f2e1.data: Harris County, Texas, census tracts during Hurricane Harvey 2017: static spatial features, rainfall intensity and water elevation, and human-sensed data (flood reports, human activity fluctuations).
c4515857baf4481227ecf203bf7570ca6457f2e1.result: ASTGCN achieves precision 0.808 and recall 0.891 for census-tract flood status, outperforming other models; adding human-sensed features improves performance.
c4515857baf4481227ecf203bf7570ca6457f2e1.open_work: Training and testing on more historical flood events to build an operational predictive tool for responders.
c4515857baf4481227ecf203bf7570ca6457f2e1.issues: Single event and single region; human-sensed data availability and biases vary; nowcasting rather than lead-time forecasting.

0a3fc7ca59f8713e003ece5c47cb757c83dbf3ca.goal: Assesses future coastal flooding risk in South Korea under climate change to support integrated coastal zone management.
0a3fc7ca59f8713e003ece5c47cb757c83dbf3ca.architecture: Multiple machine learning classifiers compared, with k-nearest neighbor performing best, producing risk probability maps.
0a3fc7ca59f8713e003ece5c47cb757c83dbf3ca.data: Coastal flood hazard data with RCP scenarios from regional climate models and sea level rise ratios; projections for the 2030s to 2080s.
0a3fc7ca59f8713e003ece5c47cb757c83dbf3ca.result: Average ROC AUC of 0.946 with k-NN; southern coastal areas show higher compound flood risk (high tide plus heavy rainfall) than eastern and western coasts.
0a3fc7ca59f8713e003ece5c47cb757c83dbf3ca.open_work: Incorporating socioeconomic vulnerability and dynamic coastal processes into the risk probability approach.
0a3fc7ca59f8713e003ece5c47cb757c83dbf3ca.issues: Statistical classification may not extrapolate to future climates; climate model and sea level rise uncertainties; details of training labels not given in the abstract.

a2cfb24796fb240aa02ff2b4e178951a7782938b.goal: Automates irrigation control that keeps soil moisture safe while reducing water use under uncertain evapotranspiration and precipitation forecasts.
a2cfb24796fb240aa02ff2b4e178951a7782938b.architecture: Data-driven robust model predictive control combining a mechanistic soil moisture model with uncertainty sets learned from historical forecast errors (support vector clustering for evapotranspiration, tailored set for precipitation) and affine decision rules.
a2cfb24796fb240aa02ff2b4e178951a7782938b.data: Historical evapotranspiration and precipitation forecasts and observations used for real-data case studies; specific products not reported in the abstract.
a2cfb24796fb240aa02ff2b4e178951a7782938b.result: Maintains soil moisture above safety levels and cuts total water consumption by 40% relative to tuned open-loop control, outperforming rule-based and certainty-equivalent MPC.
a2cfb24796fb240aa02ff2b4e178951a7782938b.open_work: Field deployment and extension to multiple fields, crops and longer weather-forecast horizons.
a2cfb24796fb240aa02ff2b4e178951a7782938b.issues: Simulation case studies rather than field trials; performance depends on representativeness of historical forecast errors.

bb70a8354b634b7f9d35ca9c0beb6d881b79c7db.goal: Builds a fast, generalizable surrogate for spatio-temporal flood simulation, as numerical shallow water solvers are computationally expensive.
bb70a8354b634b7f9d35ca9c0beb6d881b79c7db.architecture: SWE-GNN: a hydraulics-inspired graph neural network mirroring finite-volume shallow water equation solvers, with learned inter-cell fluxes, stacked layers, multi-step-ahead loss and curriculum learning.
bb70a8354b634b7f9d35ca9c0beb6d881b79c7db.data: Two-dimensional dike-breach flood simulations over randomly generated digital elevation models produced with a high-fidelity numerical solver.
bb70a8354b634b7f9d35ca9c0beb6d881b79c7db.result: Mean errors of 0.04 m for water depth and 0.004 m2/s for unit discharge on unseen topographies; generalizes to new breach locations, larger domains and longer periods; up to 100x faster than the solver.
bb70a8354b634b7f9d35ca9c0beb6d881b79c7db.open_work: Applying to real topographies and uncertainty-aware, time-sensitive flood applications.
bb70a8354b634b7f9d35ca9c0beb6d881b79c7db.issues: Trained and tested on synthetic terrain and simulated floods only; no real event validation; dike-breach scenarios only.

0dd75d1b2b21f2dfc70dee1722fe3fd258c86c7d.goal: Surveys deep learning methods for very short-term solar irradiance forecasting, important for grid integration of photovoltaic power.
0dd75d1b2b21f2dfc70dee1722fe3fd258c86c7d.architecture: Review of deep learning approaches (e.g. convolutional neural networks, recurrent networks/LSTM and hybrids) for intra-hour solar irradiance forecasting.
0dd75d1b2b21f2dfc70dee1722fe3fd258c86c7d.data: Covers studies using inputs such as ground-based sky images, irradiance time series and satellite data; specific datasets not reported here (abstract unavailable).
0dd75d1b2b21f2dfc70dee1722fe3fd258c86c7d.result: Not available from the abstract; the survey organizes and compares deep learning methods for very short-term forecasting.
0dd75d1b2b21f2dfc70dee1722fe3fd258c86c7d.open_work: Standardized benchmarks and datasets, and better handling of rapid cloud-induced ramps.
0dd75d1b2b21f2dfc70dee1722fe3fd258c86c7d.issues: Abstract missing; scope and conclusions not verified.

5a5e459db1110a9a4d8558fae7b16a659c63fc38.goal: Estimates land subsidence and associated groundwater storage loss across the western United States, where physical models and InSAR are costly or incomplete.
5a5e459db1110a9a4d8558fae7b16a659c63fc38.architecture: Machine learning regression (tree-based model type not specified in the abstract) relating widely available predictors to land subsidence.
5a5e459db1110a9a4d8558fae7b16a659c63fc38.data: Evapotranspiration, land use, sediment thickness and other ancillary data, with InSAR/GPS subsidence observations for training; western US, 2015–2016.
5a5e459db1110a9a4d8558fae7b16a659c63fc38.result: Estimates ~2.0 km3/yr groundwater storage loss from pumping-induced compaction in 2015–2016; California accounts for 75% of subsidence, concentrated in the Central Valley.
5a5e459db1110a9a4d8558fae7b16a659c63fc38.open_work: Extending to other periods and regions and linking to groundwater management.
5a5e459db1110a9a4d8558fae7b16a659c63fc38.issues: Short period; relies on training labels from InSAR with atmospheric errors; ML relationships are correlative rather than mechanistic.

1cb6eeac1b8b22ca429d7c315c71369baede4d76.goal: Produces global high-resolution total water storage anomalies (TWSA) to better resolve the terrestrial water cycle beyond coarse GRACE resolution.
1cb6eeac1b8b22ca429d7c315c71369baede4d76.architecture: Self-supervised deep learning data assimilation model with a new loss function combining hydrological simulations and satellite gravimetry.
1cb6eeac1b8b22ca429d7c315c71369baede4d76.data: GRACE and GRACE-FO measurements and hydrological model simulations; global 0.5° output.
1cb6eeac1b8b22ca429d7c315c71369baede4d76.result: The product closes the water balance in small basins while preserving large-scale GRACE accuracy, supporting local hazard monitoring.
1cb6eeac1b8b22ca429d7c315c71369baede4d76.open_work: Applying the approach to other TWSA data sources and using the product for natural and anthropogenic water cycle impact studies.
1cb6eeac1b8b22ca429d7c315c71369baede4d76.issues: Fine-scale information depends on hydrological simulations; validation in small basins relies on water balance closure; limited quantitative metrics in the abstract.

1b3d2ec66bc229cf67737b5268e22a343cecff1a.goal: Improves streamflow simulation and flood prediction in India, hampered by hydrological model and meteorological forecast errors.
1b3d2ec66bc229cf67737b5268e22a343cecff1a.architecture: Post-processing of five hydrological models (VIC, H08, CWatM, Noah-MP, CLM) with multiple linear regression, random forest, XGBoost and LSTM, including ML-based multi-model ensembles.
1b3d2ec66bc229cf67737b5268e22a343cecff1a.data: IMD observed meteorological forcing and GEFS forecasts driving the hydrological models; observed streamflow and flood inundation in Indian basins.
1b3d2ec66bc229cf67737b5268e22a343cecff1a.result: ML post-processing significantly improves overall streamflow simulation and the ML multi-model ensemble beats individual models, but improvement in high flows is limited; accounting for dams is crucial.
1b3d2ec66bc229cf67737b5268e22a343cecff1a.open_work: Developing operational multi-model ML flood early warning systems for India.
1b3d2ec66bc229cf67737b5268e22a343cecff1a.issues: Limited gains for high flows that matter most for floods; skill depends on forecast quality and dam representation.

38b348d71981685e624956f4f3183ccb5d700149.goal: Predicts global horizontal irradiance 1–5 minutes ahead from sky images to help balance PV electricity supply and demand.
38b348d71981685e624956f4f3183ccb5d700149.architecture: Two artificial neural network (MLP) methodologies using color information at a limited number of sampling points in sky images, without explicit cloud detection.
38b348d71981685e624956f4f3183ccb5d700149.data: Ground-based sky images and measured global horizontal irradiance at a single site; dataset details not reported in the abstract.
38b348d71981685e624956f4f3183ccb5d700149.result: Captures fluctuating irradiance trends with minimum RMSE of 143 W/m2, comparable to existing methods while using far less image data.
38b348d71981685e624956f4f3183ccb5d700149.open_work: Testing at other sites and climates and extending forecast horizons.
38b348d71981685e624956f4f3183ccb5d700149.issues: High absolute RMSE; single-site evaluation; limited image information may miss complex cloud dynamics.

5f6522bc1ac2475917c2ad7d0b735fe62c14fbf0.goal: Constructs high-resolution groundwater drought information in the Indus Basin by downscaling coarse GRACE observations.
5f6522bc1ac2475917c2ad7d0b735fe62c14fbf0.architecture: Machine learning downscaling of GRACE groundwater storage anomalies (specific model not reported here; abstract unavailable), followed by drought index calculation.
5f6522bc1ac2475917c2ad7d0b735fe62c14fbf0.data: GRACE satellite data with hydrometeorological predictors over the Indus Basin; details not reported.
5f6522bc1ac2475917c2ad7d0b735fe62c14fbf0.result: Not available from the abstract; the study produces spatio-temporal high-resolution groundwater drought maps.
5f6522bc1ac2475917c2ad7d0b735fe62c14fbf0.open_work: Validation with more in situ wells and extension to GRACE-FO period and other basins.
5f6522bc1ac2475917c2ad7d0b735fe62c14fbf0.issues: Abstract missing; method and results not verified; downscaled products depend on predictor relationships and sparse wells.

8fdb881e079cbfcbc983f900e8dd3b7a82fb7829.goal: Characterizes how maize, sorghum and soybean yields depend on climate in crop-specific developmental phases, to understand climate change impacts on food systems.
8fdb881e079cbfcbc983f900e8dd3b7a82fb7829.architecture: Random forest used as a diagnostic tool with phase-specific climate variables and a time trend for technology.
8fdb881e079cbfcbc983f900e8dd3b7a82fb7829.data: County yields and climate variables for the US plains, 1980–2016, aggregated by establishment, critical window and grain-filling phases.
8fdb881e079cbfcbc983f900e8dd3b7a82fb7829.result: Random forest explains 71–86% of yield variance; yields fall sharply above ~29°C (maize) and 30°C (soybean) maximum temperature, while sorghum tolerates up to 32.5°C; maize is sensitive to low humidity during flowering.
8fdb881e079cbfcbc983f900e8dd3b7a82fb7829.open_work: Projecting shifts in optimal growing regions under warming with soil productivity and adaptation included.
8fdb881e079cbfcbc983f900e8dd3b7a82fb7829.issues: Correlative county-level analysis; technology represented only by a time trend; extrapolation to future warming is uncertain.

2d6f805285d15177e59035b035cb4dca93dd713b.goal: Identifies river flooding mechanisms in Europe and detects their changes, needed for flood forecasting and projection under climate change.
2d6f805285d15177e59035b035cb4dca93dd713b.architecture: Explainable machine learning (LSTM-based discharge model with interpretation) combined with cluster analysis to attribute annual maximum discharge events to drivers.
2d6f805285d15177e59035b035cb4dca93dd713b.data: 53,968 annual maximum discharge events in about a thousand European catchments with meteorological drivers over roughly 70 years.
2d6f805285d15177e59035b035cb4dca93dd713b.result: Three mechanisms emerge: recent precipitation, antecedent precipitation (excess soil moisture) and snowmelt; over half of catchments have mixed mechanisms; snowmelt floods decreased and recent-precipitation floods increased.
2d6f805285d15177e59035b035cb4dca93dd713b.open_work: Extending to other regions and linking mechanism changes to flood seasonality and magnitude projections.
2d6f805285d15177e59035b035cb4dca93dd713b.issues: Attribution depends on the interpretation method and model; observational record limits trend detection; catchment selection bias.

e6f486f5d42c4c26196e3595beaad522a2741463.goal: Improves hourly ensemble streamflow forecasts in a cascade reservoir catchment where upstream releases and rainfall-runoff both control flow.
e6f486f5d42c4c26196e3595beaad522a2741463.architecture: Hydrometeorological ensemble forecasting (bias-corrected meteorological forecasts driving a land surface hydrological model) combined with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network.
e6f486f5d42c4c26196e3595beaad522a2741463.data: Yantan catchment, China; hourly streamflow hindcasts during rainy seasons 2013–2017 with ensemble meteorological forecasts and upstream reservoir release data.
e6f486f5d42c4c26196e3595beaad522a2741463.result: The hydrometeorological approach reduces probabilistic error by 10% and deterministic error by 6% versus ESP over 7 days; adding LSTM cuts deterministic error another 6% in the first 72 hours; LSTM with observations only degrades after 24 hours.
e6f486f5d42c4c26196e3595beaad522a2741463.open_work: Better integration of reservoir operation information and extension to other regulated catchments.
e6f486f5d42c4c26196e3595beaad522a2741463.issues: Single catchment; short hindcast period; gains of ML limited to short leads.

464ca36196e9f9b7f1455bd04e7e5db16a72ab96.goal: Improves urban flood prediction by jointly modeling spatial and temporal features with diverse inputs, faster than physically based models.
464ca36196e9f9b7f1455bd04e7e5db16a72ab96.architecture: CNN-RNN hybrid feature fusion: combinations of FCN, U-Net, SegNet, DeepLabv3+ with LSTM, BiLSTM and GRU, with Bayesian optimization for factor selection; LSTM-DeepLabv3+ is best.
464ca36196e9f9b7f1455bd04e7e5db16a72ab96.data: Urban flood simulations from a physically based model under various rainfall inputs with seven selected flood-driving factors; study area details not reported in the abstract.
464ca36196e9f9b7f1455bd04e7e5db16a72ab96.result: LSTM-DeepLabv3+ achieves MAE 0.007, RMSE 0.025, NSE 0.973, KGE 0.755, with inference of 1.158 s, about 1/125 of physical model computation time.
464ca36196e9f9b7f1455bd04e7e5db16a72ab96.open_work: Testing with observed flood events and transfer to other urban areas.
464ca36196e9f9b7f1455bd04e7e5db16a72ab96.issues: Trained on simulated floods so inherits physical model errors; single urban case; no uncertainty estimates.

d530a65ad6d603be858c211b91a18839789af863.goal: Builds a data-driven high-temporal-resolution rainfall-runoff model for flood risk management in a flood-prone Houston watershed.
d530a65ad6d603be858c211b91a18839789af863.architecture: Sequence-to-sequence long short-term memory (LSTM) network emulating rainfall-runoff at 15-minute resolution, compared with the process-based GSSHA model.
d530a65ad6d603be858c211b91a18839789af863.data: Ten years of precipitation from 153 rain gauges and river channel discharge (over 5.3 million data points) in a Houston, Texas watershed.
d530a65ad6d603be858c211b91a18839789af863.result: LSTM predicts discharge efficiently and is more robust than GSSHA; test NSE rises from 0.666 to 0.942 when a selected subset of gauges is used as input.
d530a65ad6d603be858c211b91a18839789af863.open_work: Exploring physical consistency further and applying to other watersheds and forecasting with predicted rainfall.
d530a65ad6d603be858c211b91a18839789af863.issues: Single watershed; input gauge selection based on performance risks overfitting; relies on observed rainfall rather than forecasts.

31af782e58f5aba479a4a4a79b2ff71ee68b047f.goal: Estimates county-level corn yield from meteorological conditions while capturing temporal cumulative effects and spatial heterogeneity.
31af782e58f5aba479a4a4a79b2ff71ee68b047f.architecture: DeepCropNet: attention-based long short-term memory (LSTM) for temporal features with multi-task learning output layers for regional spatial features.
31af782e58f5aba479a4a4a79b2ff71ee68b047f.data: US Corn Belt county yields 1981–2016 with growing degree days, killing degree days and precipitation time series.
31af782e58f5aba479a4a4a79b2ff71ee68b047f.result: RMSE of 0.82 Mg/ha versus 1.14 for LASSO and 1.05 for random forest; attention reveals consistent cumulative temporal patterns.
31af782e58f5aba479a4a4a79b2ff71ee68b047f.open_work: Adding soil, management and remote-sensing inputs and testing under future climate.
31af782e58f5aba479a4a4a79b2ff71ee68b047f.issues: Only three meteorological inputs; no explicit technology or management variables; spatial generalization outside the Corn Belt untested.

2d04f4a5c1610fa6cdd3886707bff6e1a807e894.goal: Improves solar PV power output forecasting by combining ground observations with satellite observations.
2d04f4a5c1610fa6cdd3886707bff6e1a807e894.architecture: Deep learning forecasting model fusing ground and satellite inputs (specific network not reported here; abstract unavailable).
2d04f4a5c1610fa6cdd3886707bff6e1a807e894.data: Ground-based PV/irradiance measurements and satellite observations; specific products not reported.
2d04f4a5c1610fa6cdd3886707bff6e1a807e894.result: Not available from the abstract; integration of satellite data is expected to improve forecasts over ground-only inputs.
2d04f4a5c1610fa6cdd3886707bff6e1a807e894.open_work: Testing across more plants, climates and lead times.
2d04f4a5c1610fa6cdd3886707bff6e1a807e894.issues: Abstract missing; architecture, data and skill not verified.

deac03f5b600a249b5ea3d7aac470075ac91cab0.goal: Produces short-term probabilistic flood forecasts as probability density functions to quantify forecast uncertainty.
deac03f5b600a249b5ea3d7aac470075ac91cab0.architecture: Conceptual hydrological model coupled with machine learning techniques for probability density forecasting (specific methods not reported here; abstract unavailable).
deac03f5b600a249b5ea3d7aac470075ac91cab0.data: Flood events in one or more study catchments; data not reported.
deac03f5b600a249b5ea3d7aac470075ac91cab0.open_work: Testing in more catchments and with forecast rainfall inputs.
deac03f5b600a249b5ea3d7aac470075ac91cab0.issues: Abstract missing; methods and results not verified.

0e1a3086370892529f5e6e1b1fd29f585db99381.goal: Provides accurate and rapid urban flood prediction in time and space to support flood management decisions.
0e1a3086370892529f5e6e1b1fd29f585db99381.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) network with Bayesian optimization and transfer learning, compared with ANN and convolutional neural network baselines.
0e1a3086370892529f5e6e1b1fd29f585db99381.data: Simulations from a physically based hydrodynamic model for various hyetographs in a northern China urban case study, plus a second case for transfer learning.
0e1a3086370892529f5e6e1b1fd29f585db99381.result: Predicts maximum water depths and flood time series 19,585 times faster than the hydrodynamic model with mean relative error 9.5%; transfer learning generalizes to a new case.
0e1a3086370892529f5e6e1b1fd29f585db99381.open_work: Using the model for real-time control, optimization and emergency planning.
0e1a3086370892529f5e6e1b1fd29f585db99381.issues: Trained on synthetic hydrodynamic outputs; limited validation with observed floods; only design hyetographs tested.

72316c2ddd54c0a336d4e12db24cfa373559debc.goal: Provides scalable urban surface flooding data by extracting flood level trends from existing surveillance cameras.
72316c2ddd54c0a336d4e12db24cfa373559debc.architecture: Deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) for floodwater segmentation in video frames, producing a static observer flooding index (SOFI).
72316c2ddd54c0a336d4e12db24cfa373559debc.data: 1,218 flooding images collected from the Internet for training; six surveillance videos with different flooding and lighting conditions for testing.
72316c2ddd54c0a336d4e12db24cfa373559debc.result: SOFI correlates 75% on average with actual water level fluctuations, rising to 85% after retraining with a few frames per video.
72316c2ddd54c0a336d4e12db24cfa373559debc.open_work: Deploying at scale across camera networks and integrating with flood models.
72316c2ddd54c0a336d4e12db24cfa373559debc.issues: Qualitative trend only, not absolute water level; only six test videos; performance depends on lighting and viewpoint.

6eb563f4ca868210e1c959fc524db05b3f1aedef.goal: Predicts property damage from flash floods in the Southeast US to support proactive disaster management.
6eb563f4ca868210e1c959fc524db05b3f1aedef.architecture: Random forest classifier and regressor with variable selection, using hazard, vulnerability and exposure features.
6eb563f4ca868210e1c959fc524db05b3f1aedef.data: More than 14,000 flash flood events with mesoscale hydrometeorological and socioeconomic data from multiple sources.
6eb563f4ca868210e1c959fc524db05b3f1aedef.result: Classifies damaging events with 81% accuracy and predicts damage amounts in good agreement with observed property damage.
6eb563f4ca868210e1c959fc524db05b3f1aedef.open_work: Extending to real-time damage forecasting and other regions.
6eb563f4ca868210e1c959fc524db05b3f1aedef.issues: Damage reports are noisy and incomplete; regression skill not quantified in the abstract.

91ebffe254a055395e7c647a37fe5cbbf63b35fb.goal: Develops forecasts of direct normal solar irradiance (DNI), important for concentrating solar power, using operational numerical weather prediction outputs.
91ebffe254a055395e7c647a37fe5cbbf63b35fb.architecture: Artificial neural network (MLP) models post-processing operational NWP forecast variables to predict DNI.
91ebffe254a055395e7c647a37fe5cbbf63b35fb.data: Operational NWP forecast data and ground DNI measurements; specific model and site not reported here (abstract unavailable).
91ebffe254a055395e7c647a37fe5cbbf63b35fb.result: Not available from the abstract; ANN models are assessed against NWP-based DNI forecasts.
91ebffe254a055395e7c647a37fe5cbbf63b35fb.open_work: Testing at more sites and climates and with probabilistic outputs.
91ebffe254a055395e7c647a37fe5cbbf63b35fb.issues: Abstract missing; details not verified; skill depends on NWP quality and aerosol representation.

d96ef705419e09c1130147a0fc7b38d479bd37d2.goal: Improves hydrologic flood routing in large heterogeneous river basins by learning routing parameters with differentiable modeling.
d96ef705419e09c1130147a0fc7b38d479bd37d2.architecture: Differentiable Muskingum-Cunge routing model over a river network with an embedded neural network (MLP) inferring Manning's n and channel geometry from reach attributes, trained only on downstream hydrographs.
d96ef705419e09c1130147a0fc7b38d479bd37d2.data: Synthetic experiments plus real Juniata River basin data with reach-scale attributes, runoff inputs and gauge hydrographs.
d96ef705419e09c1130147a0fc7b38d479bd37d2.result: Manning's n is identifiable with moderate precision but channel geometry is not; the model beats ML and summed-runoff baselines for subbasins above 2,000 km2, including untrained inner gauges.
d96ef705419e09c1130147a0fc7b38d479bd37d2.open_work: Coupling the learned n parameterization with national-scale hydrologic models for flood simulation.
d96ef705419e09c1130147a0fc7b38d479bd37d2.issues: Absolute n values vary with training period; channel geometry unidentifiable; single basin demonstration.

0e37c06ac593f9d5108f49efe6df3a4b6c404c62.goal: Forecasts monthly photovoltaic power at a regional level by integrating meteorological and geographical (topographic) features, to identify suitable regions for new solar plants.
0e37c06ac593f9d5108f49efe6df3a4b6c404c62.architecture: Multi-channel convolutional neural network (CNN) that ingests raster maps of elevation, solar irradiation, temperature, wind speed and precipitation as separate input channels.
0e37c06ac593f9d5108f49efe6df3a4b6c404c62.data: Gridded raster maps of elevation and meteorological variables paired with monthly PV power outputs from 164 sites; product names and region details are not reported in the abstract.
0e37c06ac593f9d5108f49efe6df3a4b6c404c62.result: Reaches a mean absolute percentage error of 8.639%, versus 16.187% for multiple linear regression and 15.991% for a standard artificial neural network, and transfers to regions not used in training.
0e37c06ac593f9d5108f49efe6df3a4b6c404c62.open_work: Extending to finer temporal resolution (daily or hourly) and testing transfer to other climates and larger areas are natural next steps.
0e37c06ac593f9d5108f49efe6df3a4b6c404c62.issues: Monthly resolution only, a modest number of sites, and no uncertainty quantification; the source and resolution of meteorological inputs are not detailed in the abstract.

cbce86bef2379505d327cbe35d419c6efedae23c.goal: Short-term electrical load forecasting for a large-scale power system using neural networks with climate information taken from global climate models.
cbce86bef2379505d327cbe35d419c6efedae23c.architecture: Neural network models (exact family not known from the available metadata) that use climate-model variables as predictors of electricity load.
cbce86bef2379505d327cbe35d419c6efedae23c.data: Historical load data from a large-scale electrical power system (likely Brazilian, given the authors) and global climate model outputs; details are not available because the abstract is missing.
cbce86bef2379505d327cbe35d419c6efedae23c.result: Not reported; the abstract is unavailable.
cbce86bef2379505d327cbe35d419c6efedae23c.open_work: Testing other network architectures and climate drivers and quantifying forecast uncertainty would follow naturally.
cbce86bef2379505d327cbe35d419c6efedae23c.issues: Abstract missing, so data, horizons and skill cannot be verified; the card is based on the title only.

1ebf51a73e645b48bbecf396efdae48c9de39477.goal: Rainfall-runoff forecasting in large-scale basins with a spatiotemporal deep learning model that uses remote sensing precipitation products as forcing.
1ebf51a73e645b48bbecf396efdae48c9de39477.architecture: Spatiotemporal deep learning model combined with remote-sensing precipitation; the exact architecture is not available.
1ebf51a73e645b48bbecf396efdae48c9de39477.data: Satellite remote sensing precipitation products and observed streamflow for large basins; specific products and basins are not available because the abstract is missing.
1ebf51a73e645b48bbecf396efdae48c9de39477.result: Not reported; the abstract is unavailable.
1ebf51a73e645b48bbecf396efdae48c9de39477.open_work: Comparison across precipitation products and transfer to other large basins would follow naturally.
1ebf51a73e645b48bbecf396efdae48c9de39477.issues: Abstract missing, so the card is based on the title only; satellite precipitation errors propagate into runoff forecasts.

10e58b5e394845627e9b52a439f0b9aba3f44d04.goal: Forecasts runoff at three hydrological stations for flood warning while accounting for meteorological drivers beyond precipitation and making the model interpretable.
10e58b5e394845627e9b52a439f0b9aba3f44d04.architecture: Decomposition-ensemble pipeline: TVF-EMD and robust local mean decomposition of runoff, bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) and extreme learning machine sub-models, combined nonlinearly by a random forest; SHAP for explanation.
10e58b5e394845627e9b52a439f0b9aba3f44d04.data: Runoff series from three hydrological stations with meteorological variables selected by the Relief algorithm and variance inflation factor; station locations and periods not reported in the abstract.
10e58b5e394845627e9b52a439f0b9aba3f44d04.result: Outperforms comparison models on various evaluation metrics, and SHAP quantifies each meteorological variable's contribution to the long-term runoff trend; no specific numbers are given in the abstract.
10e58b5e394845627e9b52a439f0b9aba3f44d04.open_work: Testing on more basins and longer lead times, and checking whether the decomposition is applied without future information leakage, are natural next steps.
10e58b5e394845627e9b52a439f0b9aba3f44d04.issues: Very complex multi-stage pipeline with risk of overfitting and decomposition leakage in operational use; only three stations evaluated.

b837af3a1a92760da3804580ddede9ff0e95ba70.goal: Short-term forecasting of solar irradiance fields from satellite-derived irradiance, to support solar energy integration.
b837af3a1a92760da3804580ddede9ff0e95ba70.architecture: Spatiotemporal deep learning model (IrradianceNet) based on convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) layers that predicts future irradiance maps from past maps.
b837af3a1a92760da3804580ddede9ff0e95ba70.data: Satellite-derived surface solar irradiance fields (to our knowledge the CM SAF SARAH-2 product over Europe); details are not confirmed because the abstract is missing.
b837af3a1a92760da3804580ddede9ff0e95ba70.result: Not reported in the available metadata; the model is presented as improving on persistence and optical-flow style baselines for short lead times.
b837af3a1a92760da3804580ddede9ff0e95ba70.open_work: Longer lead times, inclusion of NWP inputs and probabilistic forecasts would follow naturally.
b837af3a1a92760da3804580ddede9ff0e95ba70.issues: Abstract missing; deterministic deep forecasts tend to blur cloud structures at longer leads, and satellite-derived irradiance carries retrieval errors.

b8f1e41ead77f16b9dda18ccd96ead521b13a989.goal: Evaluates whether the transformer improves forecasts of karst spring discharge up to 4 days ahead for drinking-water management.
b8f1e41ead77f16b9dda18ccd96ead521b13a989.architecture: Transformer compared with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network and a common baseline model, in discharge-based and non-discharge-based input scenarios, with uncertainty analysis.
b8f1e41ead77f16b9dda18ccd96ead521b13a989.data: Extensive hourly database for an Austrian karst spring (LKAS2) plus two further karst springs with diverse discharge characteristics; inputs include rainfall, electrical conductivity and temporal information.
b8f1e41ead77f16b9dda18ccd96ead521b13a989.result: Transformer beats the LSTM by 9% mean difference for the spring with the longest response time but is 4% worse for the shortest; both reach NSE 0.64-0.92 and sMAPE 10.8-28.7% at LKAS2 and the transformer better captures snowmelt.
b8f1e41ead77f16b9dda18ccd96ead521b13a989.open_work: Testing on more springs and longer horizons, and exploiting attention for process understanding, are natural next steps.
b8f1e41ead77f16b9dda18ccd96ead521b13a989.issues: Only three springs; performance depends on spring response time; prediction intervals are widest during snowmelt.

aab9777b97f0b8518772540dac65242fcc93c2cc.goal: Predicts meteorological drought robustly by exploiting the full antecedent global sea surface temperature fluctuation pattern rather than signals from a few ocean regions.
aab9777b97f0b8518772540dac65242fcc93c2cc.architecture: Antecedent SST fluctuation pattern (ASFP) predictors fed to support vector regression, random forest and extreme learning machine models for ensemble, probabilistic and deterministic predictions.
aab9777b97f0b8518772540dac65242fcc93c2cc.data: Antecedent global SST fields and the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI) at 1°x1° for the Colorado, Danube, Orange and Pearl River basins; SST product not reported in the abstract.
aab9777b97f0b8518772540dac65242fcc93c2cc.result: ASFP-ELM effectively predicts the space-time evolution of drought events at 1- and 3-month lead times and outperforms ASFP-SVR and ASFP-RF; no skill numbers in the abstract.
aab9777b97f0b8518772540dac65242fcc93c2cc.open_work: Extending to longer leads and more basins, and integrating into drought early warning systems, are suggested.
aab9777b97f0b8518772540dac65242fcc93c2cc.issues: Short lead times only; SST-only predictors ignore land-surface memory; skill numbers and physical interpretation are not given in the abstract.

adbc9bc320cf68c70e1920fa77d81b1d6343597f.goal: Simulates streamflow in data-scarce regions, including ungauged internal sub-basins, where large-sample deep learning and transfer learning generalize poorly.
adbc9bc320cf68c70e1920fa77d81b1d6343597f.architecture: Distributed physics-informed deep learning model: differentiable hydrological models for each sub-basin with neural network parameterization, coupled with a differentiable Muskingum channel routing scheme.
adbc9bc320cf68c70e1920fa77d81b1d6343597f.data: Streamflow from the downstream-most gauge for training and upstream held-out stations for testing, with meteorological forcing; basin and data products are not reported in the abstract.
adbc9bc320cf68c70e1920fa77d81b1d6343597f.result: Trained only on the outlet station, it outperforms a distributed hydrological model at both training and held-out upstream stations, and beats transfer-learning models while needing fewer gauges.
adbc9bc320cf68c70e1920fa77d81b1d6343597f.open_work: Testing in more regions with distinct hydrological processes and adding further process modules are natural extensions.
adbc9bc320cf68c70e1920fa77d81b1d6343597f.issues: Equifinality in sub-basin parameters when constrained only by outlet flow; no quantitative scores in the abstract; evaluated on a limited number of basins.

cf7b44884a62b71b5491cf286ab1d96abea4c861.goal: Reviews the flash drought concept, the sources of uncertainty in its prediction, and the potential of machine learning and deep learning to improve it.
cf7b44884a62b71b5491cf286ab1d96abea4c861.architecture: Review of 121 articles covering flash drought definitions, key indicators, characteristics, and monitoring, prediction and impact-assessment methods, including ML and DL approaches.
cf7b44884a62b71b5491cf286ab1d96abea4c861.data: Literature corpus of 121 relevant articles; no new data.
cf7b44884a62b71b5491cf286ab1d96abea4c861.result: Flash drought prediction is limited by inconsistent definitions and indicators, low subseasonal-to-seasonal predictability, input-data errors, parameter uncertainty and nonlinear, non-stationary indicator interactions; combining traditional methods and multisource data with ML/DL shows promise.
cf7b44884a62b71b5491cf286ab1d96abea4c861.open_work: Calls for consistent definitions, better physical understanding, and ML/DL models that fuse multisource data for S2S flash drought prediction.
cf7b44884a62b71b5491cf286ab1d96abea4c861.issues: A review, so no new quantitative evaluation; conclusions about ML potential are largely prospective.

e0ea43088b2b8cac9ce8e58ef07b434da5ff09a2.goal: Models karst spring discharge where few climate stations exist in the catchment, by learning directly from gridded meteorological data.
e0ea43088b2b8cac9ce8e58ef07b434da5ff09a2.architecture: 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) processing gridded meteorological inputs followed by a 1D CNN for discharge simulation, compared with 1D models using station data; spatial input sensitivity analysis.
e0ea43088b2b8cac9ce8e58ef07b434da5ff09a2.data: Gridded meteorological data (product not named in the abstract) and discharge for three karst spring catchments in the Alpine and Mediterranean regions.
e0ea43088b2b8cac9ce8e58ef07b434da5ff09a2.result: The 2D models simulate karst spring discharge excellently, rivalling existing modeling studies in the regions, and the sensitivity analysis highlights relevant input areas useful for catchment delineation.
e0ea43088b2b8cac9ce8e58ef07b434da5ff09a2.open_work: Using spatial sensitivity to localize and delineate karst catchments and testing more springs are suggested directions.
e0ea43088b2b8cac9ce8e58ef07b434da5ff09a2.issues: Only three catchments; no quantitative scores in the abstract; performance tied to the quality of gridded meteorological products.

abf5468211f0fd28ecdc3293eaf635985f898b39.goal: Short-term solar irradiance forecasting at arbitrary locations without local ground measurements, to support grid integration of dispersed solar generators.
abf5468211f0fd28ecdc3293eaf635985f898b39.architecture: Deep neural network (feed-forward DNN) trained on a subset of sites that uses satellite-based irradiance measurements and weather forecasts to generalize across locations.
abf5468211f0fd28ecdc3293eaf635985f898b39.data: Satellite-based irradiance measurements and NWP weather forecasts with ground measurements at 25 locations in the Netherlands.
abf5468211f0fd28ecdc3293eaf635985f898b39.result: The general model averages 31.31% rRMSE across locations and horizons, equal to or better than the best local model trained with ground data (32.01% rRMSE).
abf5468211f0fd28ecdc3293eaf635985f898b39.open_work: Extending to other climates and larger regions and to probabilistic forecasts would follow naturally.
abf5468211f0fd28ecdc3293eaf635985f898b39.issues: Tested only in the Netherlands with relatively homogeneous climate; deterministic forecasts with no uncertainty.

97023584a339643fa906c1d3b555f6bf0e6b53f7.goal: Day-ahead forecasting of total rooftop PV generation in a region by jointly using aggregated and site-level generation series together with weather data.
97023584a339643fa906c1d3b555f6bf0e6b53f7.architecture: Two hierarchical temporal convolutional neural network (HTCNN) architectures, applied either as a single regional model or as separate models for weather-based sub-regions whose forecasts are summed.
97023584a339643fa906c1d3b555f6bf0e6b53f7.data: One year of solar generation and weather time series from 101 locations across Western Australia.
97023584a339643fa906c1d3b555f6bf0e6b53f7.result: The sub-region HTCNN needs fewer networks and reaches a forecast skill score of 40.2%, reducing error by a statistically significant 6.5% versus the best alternative.
97023584a339643fa906c1d3b555f6bf0e6b53f7.open_work: Testing over multiple years and other regions and adding probabilistic outputs are natural next steps.
97023584a339643fa906c1d3b555f6bf0e6b53f7.issues: Only one year of data, one region, and deterministic forecasts; source of weather data (observed or forecast) is not clear from the abstract.

b388eadaa34fb39d931a2ae72e56da123f9677da.goal: Short-term (6-hour and daily) electricity demand forecasting using climate predictors to support energy security in southeast Queensland.
b388eadaa34fb39d931a2ae72e56da123f9677da.architecture: Artificial neural network (MLP) benchmarked against MARS, multiple linear regression and ARIMA; a hybrid ANN combines ANN, MARS and MLR forecasts, with bootstrap for uncertainty.
b388eadaa34fb39d931a2ae72e56da123f9677da.data: Energex demand data at 8 stations in southeast Queensland, six SILO climate variables and 51 ECMWF reanalysis variables, with lagged cross-correlation predictor selection.
b388eadaa34fb39d931a2ae72e56da123f9677da.result: The ANN beats ARIMA, MARS and MLR, and the hybrid ANN is best, e.g. RRMSE of 3.85% (6-h) and 4.37% (daily) at Redcliffe.
b388eadaa34fb39d931a2ae72e56da123f9677da.open_work: Testing in other regions and with forecast rather than reanalysis predictors would be needed for operational use.
b388eadaa34fb39d931a2ae72e56da123f9677da.issues: Uses reanalysis predictors, which are not available in real time; single region; shallow network.

4f9e13873f86acde3deb87244b418b4a32fbf81a.goal: Tests whether jointly modeling daily streamflow and stream water temperature with multi-task deep learning improves predictions of interdependent hydrologic variables.
4f9e13873f86acde3deb87244b418b4a32fbf81a.architecture: Multi-task deep learning with an LSTM (recurrent) network and a scaling factor weighting the auxiliary variable's loss; single-site and multi-site models.
4f9e13873f86acde3deb87244b418b4a32fbf81a.data: Paired daily streamflow and stream temperature at 101 sites across the conterminous United States, with meteorological forcing.
4f9e13873f86acde3deb87244b418b4a32fbf81a.result: Multi-task single-site models beat single-task models for 56 of 101 sites in streamflow NSE; the multi-site model improves only 17 sites, and naive scaling-factor choices degrade 3 and 47 of 53 sites.
4f9e13873f86acde3deb87244b418b4a32fbf81a.open_work: Better selection of the multi-task scaling factor and understanding where multi-task benefits arise are open questions.
4f9e13873f86acde3deb87244b418b4a32fbf81a.issues: Benefits are site- and configuration-dependent; sensitivity to the scaling-factor hyperparameter limits robustness.

034f9b8b3cb7a3fe8434a45e6cf336b5e3e8b59c.goal: Builds a fast, resolution-invariant, geometry-adaptive large-scale flood modeling and forecasting framework to overcome costly fixed-grid hydrodynamic models.
034f9b8b3cb7a3fe8434a45e6cf336b5e3e8b59c.architecture: FloodCast: multi-satellite observation module with unsupervised change detection plus a geometry-adaptive physics-informed neural solver (GeoPINS) combining PINNs with Fourier neural operators, extended to sequence-to-sequence modeling.
034f9b8b3cb7a3fe8434a45e6cf336b5e3e8b59c.data: Benchmark dataset for the 2022 Pakistan flood built from a finite-difference hydrodynamic solution, with SAR-based flood extent and depth, optical remote sensing imagery and satellite rainfall.
034f9b8b3cb7a3fe8434a45e6cf336b5e3e8b59c.result: Achieves an average MAPE of 14.93% and MAE of 0.0610 m for 14-day water depth simulations, outperforming traditional hydrodynamics against SAR-based depth data.
034f9b8b3cb7a3fe8434a45e6cf336b5e3e8b59c.open_work: Real-time flood hazard forecasting with reliable precipitation forecasts and transfer to other basins are the stated directions.
034f9b8b3cb7a3fe8434a45e6cf336b5e3e8b59c.issues: Evaluated on a single flood event; forecast skill depends on precipitation input quality; validation depth data from SAR is itself uncertain.

e1698d91240a6c5002a661e37a05364b62334e13.goal: Fills spatial gaps in the 3-km SMAP/Sentinel-1 soil moisture product caused by the narrow swath and low revisit of Sentinel-1 radar.
e1698d91240a6c5002a661e37a05364b62334e13.architecture: Two-layer machine learning framework that first predicts brightness temperature and then soil moisture in gap areas, using historical radar backscatter (30-day average); specific learner not named in the abstract.
e1698d91240a6c5002a661e37a05364b62334e13.data: SMAP/Sentinel-1 L2_SM_SP 3-km soil moisture, SMAP radiometer and Sentinel-1 radar observations over Arizona, Oklahoma, Iowa and Arkansas; validated against holdouts, airborne and in situ networks.
e1698d91240a6c5002a661e37a05364b62334e13.result: Reconstructs 3-km soil moisture with mean R improvements of 47%/35%/20%/80% and unbiased RMSE improvements of 20%/10%/7%/26% over the 33-km SMAP product at the four sites.
e1698d91240a6c5002a661e37a05364b62334e13.open_work: Applying the framework globally and to areas where radiometer observations are also missing would follow.
e1698d91240a6c5002a661e37a05364b62334e13.issues: Requires concurrent radiometer data; validated in only four regions; inherits errors of the SMAP/Sentinel-1 retrieval it imitates.

4f9019ea4d09386f1595f1d3e82c72c1ff2dcf53.goal: Estimates conditional extreme quantiles beyond the range of historical data for flood risk forecasting with complex predictor dependence.
4f9019ea4d09386f1595f1d3e82c72c1ff2dcf53.architecture: Extreme quantile regression neural network (EQRN) combining neural networks with extreme value theory (generalized Pareto tail), including a recurrent (LSTM-type) version for time series.
4f9019ea4d09386f1595f1d3e82c72c1ff2dcf53.data: Discharge and covariates in space and time for the Swiss Aare catchment; specific data products not reported in the abstract.
4f9019ea4d09386f1595f1d3e82c72c1ff2dcf53.result: Provides one-day-ahead predictions of return levels and exceedance probabilities that complement static extreme value analysis and adapt to distributional shifts.
4f9019ea4d09386f1595f1d3e82c72c1ff2dcf53.open_work: Extending to longer lead times and multivariate or spatial extremes are natural next steps.
4f9019ea4d09386f1595f1d3e82c72c1ff2dcf53.issues: Single catchment application; extrapolation to very high quantiles remains uncertain; no quantitative skill figures in the abstract.

84781a8c9f6af8eed17d4c1529bfb64457c43fbc.goal: Simulates runoff response to climate change in permafrost-affected alpine catchments, where cryosphere degradation alters runoff regimes.
84781a8c9f6af8eed17d4c1529bfb64457c43fbc.architecture: Physics-informed deep learning model hybridizing neural networks with dominant hydrological process physics, including neural network-based soil freeze-thaw coupling inspired by the Stefan equation.
84781a8c9f6af8eed17d4c1529bfb64457c43fbc.data: Streamflow and meteorological forcing for the source region of the Yellow River; specific products and periods not reported in the abstract.
84781a8c9f6af8eed17d4c1529bfb64457c43fbc.result: Including freeze-thaw physics better captures interannual streamflow and baseflow recession under +1°C warming, and the model beats lumped, distributed physical and standard DL models.
84781a8c9f6af8eed17d4c1529bfb64457c43fbc.open_work: Applying to other permafrost catchments and to full climate projections is a natural extension.
84781a8c9f6af8eed17d4c1529bfb64457c43fbc.issues: Single basin; warming tests are sensitivity experiments without observational verification of future responses.

66e8e1fa4c43e78b72f9629fbadcc92e92841a1c.goal: Investigates whether deep learning rainfall-runoff models learn physically meaningful input-output relationships.
66e8e1fa4c43e78b72f9629fbadcc92e92841a1c.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) network with daily precipitation and mean air temperature as inputs, probed with hypothetical input experiments.
66e8e1fa4c43e78b72f9629fbadcc92e92841a1c.data: Daily precipitation, air temperature and discharge from a snow-dominated watershed (Japan, per the authors' affiliation); details not given in the abstract.
66e8e1fa4c43e78b72f9629fbadcc92e92841a1c.result: The trained LSTM produces discharge even without precipitation and conserves only 17-39% of snow-period precipitation mass in annual flow, despite strong goodness-of-fit.
66e8e1fa4c43e78b72f9629fbadcc92e92841a1c.open_work: Motivates physical constraints such as mass conservation in DL hydrological models.
66e8e1fa4c43e78b72f9629fbadcc92e92841a1c.issues: Single watershed and minimal inputs; hypothetical experiments are out-of-distribution by design.

b6822ce6b7b3a5279c6458881bc88a3d1f624c14.goal: Intra-day forecasting of global horizontal irradiance at a PV plant location without real-time ground measurements.
b6822ce6b7b3a5279c6458881bc88a3d1f624c14.architecture: Deep neural network with convolutional and dense layers (CNN) using time series of satellite-derived irradiance estimates around the target plus secondary inputs.
b6822ce6b7b3a5279c6458881bc88a3d1f624c14.data: Satellite-derived irradiance estimates near the target location; benchmarked against ECMWF irradiance forecasts; satellite product not named in the abstract.
b6822ce6b7b3a5279c6458881bc88a3d1f624c14.result: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy compared with ECMWF forecasts and similar published approaches, without using irradiance measurements; no numbers in the abstract.
b6822ce6b7b3a5279c6458881bc88a3d1f624c14.open_work: Testing at more sites and adding probabilistic outputs would follow.
b6822ce6b7b3a5279c6458881bc88a3d1f624c14.issues: Single site; no quantitative scores in the abstract; inherits satellite retrieval errors.

7d29a972e902e3d296360966a8218c41cc565b7f.goal: Predicts farmland flood (waterlogging) disasters by coupling machine learning with weather forecasts, with a case study in the Yangtze River basin.
7d29a972e902e3d296360966a8218c41cc565b7f.architecture: Machine learning model coupled with weather forecast inputs; specific algorithm not known because the abstract is missing.
7d29a972e902e3d296360966a8218c41cc565b7f.data: Weather forecast data and farmland flood records in the Yangtze River basin; products not available.
7d29a972e902e3d296360966a8218c41cc565b7f.result: Not reported; the abstract is unavailable.
7d29a972e902e3d296360966a8218c41cc565b7f.open_work: Extending lead time and transferring to other agricultural regions would follow.
7d29a972e902e3d296360966a8218c41cc565b7f.issues: Abstract missing, so the card is based on the title only; skill depends on weather forecast accuracy.

6af7683484dae96c1080c2dd92f7be0959e4174f.goal: Models evapotranspiration (latent heat flux) by inferring stomatal and aerodynamic resistances, a key challenge across vegetation types.
6af7683484dae96c1080c2dd92f7be0959e4174f.architecture: Hybrid model: a feed-forward neural network (MLP) estimates surface and aerodynamic resistances that feed the Penman-Monteith equation end to end, constrained by theory-driven priors or multi-task learning of sensible heat.
6af7683484dae96c1080c2dd92f7be0959e4174f.data: Multi-year eddy-covariance flux measurements at forest and grassland sites from the FLUXNET database.
6af7683484dae96c1080c2dd92f7be0959e4174f.result: All hybrid models predict fluxes well (R2 0.82-0.89 grassland, 0.70-0.80 forest, mean diurnal); constrained models give physically consistent resistances while the under-constrained model is implausible.
6af7683484dae96c1080c2dd92f7be0959e4174f.open_work: Proposes testing the learned resistance parameterizations as replacements for ad hoc formulations in Earth system models.
6af7683484dae96c1080c2dd92f7be0959e4174f.issues: Equifinality when both resistances are estimated freely; limited to sites with flux data; not yet tested in an Earth system model.

e713b82f12a88093f2f52e177ad76df7c29c2158.goal: Tests whether catchment physical descriptors are necessary for regionalization in global deep learning streamflow models, given that they are uncertain or unavailable.
e713b82f12a88093f2f52e177ad76df7c29c2158.architecture: Deep learning global hydrologic model (LSTM-type recurrent networks, among other models) where catchment attributes are replaced by random vectors.
e713b82f12a88093f2f52e177ad76df7c29c2158.data: Gauged basins with weather forcing and catchment physical descriptors (CAMELS-type data, not named in the abstract).
e713b82f12a88093f2f52e177ad76df7c29c2158.result: Random vectors give predictive performance comparable to actual physical descriptors and are robust across data sparsity scenarios and model choices.
e713b82f12a88093f2f52e177ad76df7c29c2158.open_work: Extending to ungauged prediction scenarios, where random vectors cannot directly substitute descriptors, is an open question.
e713b82f12a88093f2f52e177ad76df7c29c2158.issues: Only valid for gauged-basin scenarios; random vectors provide no physical interpretability.

37990e5d54c22111fe8306c29b94f2976c465b69.goal: Bridges the performance gap of physically-based hydrology models by incorporating physical knowledge into machine learning for streamflow prediction with less data.
37990e5d54c22111fe8306c29b94f2976c465b69.architecture: Physics-guided LSTM architecture coupled with the SWAT hydrology model that models intermediate processes linking weather drivers to streamflow.
37990e5d54c22111fe8306c29b94f2976c465b69.data: Observed runoff for small catchments in the South Branch of the Root River Watershed, Minnesota, plus a 200-year synthetic dataset from SWAT for pretraining.
37990e5d54c22111fe8306c29b94f2976c465b69.result: Early-stage work; synthetic SWAT data improves performance and reduces convergence time, but no quantitative results are given.
37990e5d54c22111fe8306c29b94f2976c465b69.open_work: Plans to add complexity and spatial heterogeneity to generalize to more sophisticated cases.
37990e5d54c22111fe8306c29b94f2976c465b69.issues: Preliminary results only; small catchments in a single watershed; inherits SWAT structural biases via synthetic data.

b7e0b7192daf0fd8dda24ab0b080dce6ac8a00e3.goal: Assesses whether deep learning rainfall-runoff models produce physically plausible streamflow projections under warming and changes in potential evapotranspiration.
b7e0b7192daf0fd8dda24ab0b080dce6ac8a00e3.architecture: Sensitivity analysis comparing three conceptual process-based models with LSTM, mass-conserving LSTM (MC-LSTM) and a new MC-LSTM-PET variant, plus a national LSTM.
b7e0b7192daf0fd8dda24ab0b080dce6ac8a00e3.data: 212 watersheds in the Great Lakes basin and a national LSTM fit to 531 US watersheds (CAMELS); warming scenarios with Hamon and Priestley-Taylor PET.
b7e0b7192daf0fd8dda24ab0b080dce6ac8a00e3.result: DL models beat process models historically, but the LSTM shows unrealistic water losses under warming (-20% to -25%), whereas MC-LSTM-PET reproduces the expected PET-dependent responses of process models.
b7e0b7192daf0fd8dda24ab0b080dce6ac8a00e3.open_work: Physical constraints on architecture and inputs are needed for credible DL climate projections; further constraint designs are open.
b7e0b7192daf0fd8dda24ab0b080dce6ac8a00e3.issues: Sensitivity experiments with idealized scenarios; no ground truth for future responses; process models are used as the plausibility reference.

77911883798031618368989e4190ee1bf437a846.goal: Improves river hydrodynamic modeling with complex lake and uncontrolled downstream boundary conditions for flood management.
77911883798031618368989e4190ee1bf437a846.architecture: Coupled framework of a gated recurrent unit (GRU) network with a 1-D hydrodynamic model (GRU-HD), using ML-predicted water levels as downstream boundary conditions.
77911883798031618368989e4190ee1bf437a846.data: Water levels and streamflow on the middle and lower Yangtze River with Poyang and Dongting lakes; periods not reported in the abstract.
77911883798031618368989e4190ee1bf437a846.result: GRU-HD simulates water levels, streamflow and river-lake exchange with most KGE above 0.90, and ML boundary conditions beat the rating-curve approach.
77911883798031618368989e4190ee1bf437a846.open_work: Applying to other river-lake systems and to forecasting mode with predicted inflows would follow.
77911883798031618368989e4190ee1bf437a846.issues: Single river system; ML boundary predictions may not extrapolate to unprecedented floods.

87d6515b5b8950264d4046418d0348014ea6ba09.goal: Probabilistic day-ahead forecasting of wind power generation in complex Arctic terrain to handle uncertainty in electricity markets.
87d6515b5b8950264d4046418d0348014ea6ba09.architecture: Several deep learning models for probabilistic forecasting (recurrent and related networks producing prediction intervals), compared across covariate sets.
87d6515b5b8950264d4046418d0348014ea6ba09.data: Power generation from a wind power plant in Northern Norway with measured weather and numerical weather predictions (NWP) as covariates.
