87d6515b5b8950264d4046418d0348014ea6ba09.result: Prediction interval quality improves when both historical measured weather and NWP are included, allowing the model to correct systematic NWP biases; using either alone performs worse.
87d6515b5b8950264d4046418d0348014ea6ba09.open_work: Testing other sites and calibration methods for prediction intervals would follow.
87d6515b5b8950264d4046418d0348014ea6ba09.issues: Single wind farm; specific architectures and quantitative scores are not detailed in the abstract.

f68097ebb0a2c1ac73894fc43e41f109bc5b3a59.goal: Automates prediction of the expert-produced Canadian Drought Monitor (CDM) maps and explains drought dynamics in near real time.
f68097ebb0a2c1ac73894fc43e41f109bc5b3a59.architecture: Machine learning framework (tree-based gradient boosting type model, not named in the abstract) with SHAP variable importance for interpretation.
f68097ebb0a2c1ac73894fc43e41f109bc5b3a59.data: Nearly two decades of CDM expert analyses with climate, hydrological and remote sensing predictors including GRACE groundwater signals.
f68097ebb0a2c1ac73894fc43e41f109bc5b3a59.result: Effectively predicts CDM maps and drought evolution; SHAP links the 2015 Prairie drought to a strong El Nino and reduced groundwater detected by GRACE.
f68097ebb0a2c1ac73894fc43e41f109bc5b3a59.open_work: Streamlining CDM operations and retrospectively extending the CDM to evaluate drought events historically.
f68097ebb0a2c1ac73894fc43e41f109bc5b3a59.issues: Learns expert judgments, which embed subjectivity; skill metrics and model type are not detailed in the abstract.

9afb8bdee81b385b3bec9ac9c28c7d068b34b3c7.goal: Benchmarks attention-based models against LSTM across diverse hydrologic prediction tasks to guide model choice in the era of large models.
9afb8bdee81b385b3bec9ac9c28c7d068b34b3c7.architecture: Benchmark framework comparing 11 transformer architectures with an LSTM baseline, plus pretrained large language models and time series attention models for zero-shot forecasting.
9afb8bdee81b385b3bec9ac9c28c7d068b34b3c7.data: Multi-source datasets for daily runoff (including a global streamflow dataset), soil moisture, snow water equivalent and dissolved oxygen.
9afb8bdee81b385b3bec9ac9c28c7d068b34b3c7.result: LSTM is best for regression (median KGE 0.75 on global streamflow, 0.11 above the best transformer), while attention models overtake LSTM as tasks move to autoregression and zero-shot prediction.
9afb8bdee81b385b3bec9ac9c28c7d068b34b3c7.open_work: Provides a platform for developing large-scale hydrologic models; scaling foundation models for hydrology remains open.
9afb8bdee81b385b3bec9ac9c28c7d068b34b3c7.issues: Results depend on hyperparameter tuning per architecture; zero-shot evaluation of LLMs is limited.

474560dd04d4c07ac175d43e1f762eb0dbb49899.goal: Improves agricultural irrigation efficiency by accounting for future soil moisture loss driven by weather, soil and plants.
474560dd04d4c07ac175d43e1f762eb0dbb49899.architecture: Deep reinforcement learning control agent (DRLIC, neural network policy) with an irrigation reward function and a safety mechanism based on a soil moisture predictor.
474560dd04d4c07ac175d43e1f762eb0dbb49899.data: In-field testbed of six almond trees with sprinklers, soil moisture sensors and wireless control nodes; weather inputs not specified in the abstract.
474560dd04d4c07ac175d43e1f762eb0dbb49899.result: In a 15-day field experiment DRLIC saves up to 9.52% water compared with a widely used irrigation scheme.
474560dd04d4c07ac175d43e1f762eb0dbb49899.open_work: Longer, larger deployments and assessment of crop yield impacts would follow.
474560dd04d4c07ac175d43e1f762eb0dbb49899.issues: Very short and small experiment (15 days, six trees); no yield or plant-health outcomes reported.

4a6efc258088dd2c2245592e5366bf475f92e674.goal: Improves day-ahead station-level forecasting of global horizontal irradiance (GHI) by adding spatio-temporal cloud context from satellite imagery, aiding grid integration of solar power.
4a6efc258088dd2c2245592e5366bf475f92e674.architecture: Deep learning model (CrossViViT, a video vision transformer with cross-attention) fusing satellite image sequences with station time series, plus a method to output a predictive distribution per time step.
4a6efc258088dd2c2245592e5366bf475f92e674.data: New multi-modal dataset of satellite imagery over a large region paired with irradiance and related physical variables from multiple geographically diverse solar stations; held-out stations for zero-shot tests.
4a6efc258088dd2c2245592e5366bf475f92e674.result: Robust day-ahead GHI forecasts, including on difficult days with variable cloud and in zero-shot generalization to unobserved stations; a hard/easy test split exposes performance in critical cloudy conditions.
4a6efc258088dd2c2245592e5366bf475f92e674.open_work: Extending to more regions and stations, longer horizons, and coupling with NWP cloud forecasts or operational grid scheduling.
4a6efc258088dd2c2245592e5366bf475f92e674.issues: Station coverage and satellite domain are limited; uncertainty calibration and value for actual grid operations are not fully assessed.

1961e99e35e562a88d3c324c8519882dc4e2c16a.goal: Tests whether LSTM rainfall-runoff models can extrapolate to extreme precipitation beyond the training range, a key concern for flood design and climate change.
1961e99e35e562a88d3c324c8519882dc4e2c16a.architecture: Stand-alone LSTM compared with a hybrid model combining a conceptual hydrological model with an LSTM, probed with synthetic design precipitation events of increasing intensity and duration.
1961e99e35e562a88d3c324c8519882dc4e2c16a.data: 196 catchments in Switzerland for training; synthetic design storms of varying intensity and duration for the extrapolation experiments.
1961e99e35e562a88d3c324c8519882dc4e2c16a.result: The LSTM cannot predict discharge above a theoretical limit of 73 mm/d, below the 183 mm/d training maximum, and shows concave runoff response; gating, not only cell-state saturation, blocks new extreme information.
1961e99e35e562a88d3c324c8519882dc4e2c16a.open_work: More robust training strategies, larger and more diverse training sets, and architectures that preserve extrapolation capacity for extremes.
1961e99e35e562a88d3c324c8519882dc4e2c16a.issues: Synthetic design events rather than observed extremes; a single region; larger hidden states or more data do not guarantee better extrapolation.

5ae2db734e2a80ac483e7915322d710e45317361.goal: Identifies how catchment properties control the Budyko parameter omega (Fu's equation) governing long-term partitioning of precipitation into evapotranspiration and runoff.
5ae2db734e2a80ac483e7915322d710e45317361.architecture: Boosted regression tree and CUBIST rule-based regression models interpreted with feature importance, accumulated local effects (ALE) and LIME explainable AI methods.
5ae2db734e2a80ac483e7915322d710e45317361.data: 15 catchment properties for 443 Australian catchments; continental omega and evapotranspiration mapped at 0.05° resolution.
5ae2db734e2a80ac483e7915322d710e45317361.result: Root zone storage capacity, vapor pressure, vegetation coverage, precipitation depth, seasonality-asynchrony index and water use efficiency dominate omega, with nonlinear, non-monotonic and regionally varying effects.
5ae2db734e2a80ac483e7915322d710e45317361.open_work: Applying the interpretable parameterization to other continents and to nonstationary climate and land-cover conditions.
5ae2db734e2a80ac483e7915322d710e45317361.issues: Long-term static framework ignores temporal change; interpretation methods reflect model associations rather than causality; Australia-only.

4b3845213fb8e42cf90fd3cebda9f7d33f07619c.goal: Assesses how agrometeorological droughts drive winter wheat yield loss risk at regional scale in Pakistan, as implied by the title.
4b3845213fb8e42cf90fd3cebda9f7d33f07619c.architecture: Machine learning approach linking drought indices to wheat yield loss risk; specific algorithms are not reported in the available metadata.
4b3845213fb8e42cf90fd3cebda9f7d33f07619c.data: Not reported in the abstract (abstract unavailable); presumably regional wheat yield records and agrometeorological drought indices for Pakistan.
4b3845213fb8e42cf90fd3cebda9f7d33f07619c.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title suggests drought indices dynamically explain wheat yield loss risk regionally.
4b3845213fb8e42cf90fd3cebda9f7d33f07619c.open_work: Seasonal drought forecasting for early warning of yield loss and extension to other crops and regions.
4b3845213fb8e42cf90fd3cebda9f7d33f07619c.issues: Abstract unavailable, so methods, data and skill cannot be verified; likely limited yield record length and regional statistics.

5e87305cf35bff55b14446c6ea352069c2a8eb37.goal: Explains what drives machine learning predictions of soil moisture during drought events to assess reliability of AI-based drought modelling.
5e87305cf35bff55b14446c6ea352069c2a8eb37.architecture: Site-specific random forest models interpreted with permutation importance, accumulated local effects, SHAP, LIME and individual conditional expectation explainable AI tools.
5e87305cf35bff55b14446c6ea352069c2a8eb37.data: Observations from 30 flux sites covering 8 vegetation types (soil temperature, aridity, latent heat flux and related variables).
5e87305cf35bff55b14446c6ea352069c2a8eb37.result: Soil temperature, atmospheric aridity, time variables and latent heat flux dominate globally; grass sites depend more on temperature, aridity and latent heat, forest sites on time-dependent variables.
5e87305cf35bff55b14446c6ea352069c2a8eb37.open_work: Using interpretations to guide operational drought prediction, irrigation and water management, and extending to more sites.
5e87305cf35bff55b14446c6ea352069c2a8eb37.issues: Site-level models with limited samples; interpretations depend on correlated predictors; no explicit forecast lead time or uncertainty.

688197275fd874b6ac0bdf324f39dae6bea98f81.goal: Provides daily, field-scale seasonal forecasts of mean air temperature up to 90 days for agricultural decisions such as yield prediction and sowing timing.
688197275fd874b6ac0bdf324f39dae6bea98f81.architecture: Hybrid model coupling the GloSea5GC2 coupled global climate model with a regularized extreme learning machine (a single-hidden-layer neural network), testing 20 frameworks and output blending.
688197275fd874b6ac0bdf324f39dae6bea98f81.data: GloSea5GC2 forecasts and hindcasts with field-scale station temperature observations in Korea.
688197275fd874b6ac0bdf324f39dae6bea98f81.result: Hybrid model RMSE 1.02 to 3.35 versus climatology 1.61 to 3.37 at all leads; centering with hindcast data improves RMSE by 3 to 20%; output blending works when hindcasts are missing.
688197275fd874b6ac0bdf324f39dae6bea98f81.open_work: Extending to minimum and maximum temperature, humidity and other agro-climatic variables at field scale.
688197275fd874b6ac0bdf324f39dae6bea98f81.issues: Single variable and limited sites; modest gains over climatology at long leads; deterministic evaluation without probabilistic skill.

14f5eaf06f5ba2215b4d94ac73eb69b93410fb20.goal: Forecasts drought up to a year ahead for agricultural planning and insurance, a problem still unsolved with reasonable accuracy.
14f5eaf06f5ba2215b4d94ac73eb69b93410fb20.architecture: End-to-end spatio-temporal neural networks compared, including the EarthFormer transformer and convolutional LSTM, predicting the Palmer Drought Severity Index.
14f5eaf06f5ba2215b4d94ac73eb69b93410fb20.data: Open monthly gridded climate data as input; five distinct environmental regions as testbeds for PDSI prediction.
14f5eaf06f5ba2215b4d94ac73eb69b93410fb20.result: EarthFormer performs best for short-term forecasts up to six months, while ConvLSTM excels at longer-term PDSI forecasting.
14f5eaf06f5ba2215b4d94ac73eb69b93410fb20.open_work: Adding more predictors and probabilistic forecasting, and testing in more regions and for insurance use cases.
14f5eaf06f5ba2215b4d94ac73eb69b93410fb20.issues: PDSI is a derived index with its own biases; few regions; skill at 12-month leads is limited and uncertainty is not quantified.

59a9acf8329851a39671433ba57ed6811f99360b.goal: Quantifies how uncertainty from initial conditions, forcing, parameters and model structure cascades through compound flood modeling chains.
59a9acf8329851a39671433ba57ed6811f99360b.architecture: Linked process-based hydrodynamic model and machine learning model (PB-ML) compared with multiple linear regression to attribute uncertainty contributions over time.
59a9acf8329851a39671433ba57ed6811f99360b.data: Hydrodynamic model scenario ensembles for Hurricane Harvey in Galveston Bay, Texas, evaluated through maximum water level residuals.
59a9acf8329851a39671433ba57ed6811f99360b.result: The PB-ML model captures hidden nonlinear interactions and outperforms MLR; model structure and forcing are the main uncertainty sources, contributing 56% of variance reduction in maximum water level residuals.
59a9acf8329851a39671433ba57ed6811f99360b.open_work: Applying the framework to other compound events and coasts and using it to target uncertainty reduction in operational flood forecasting.
59a9acf8329851a39671433ba57ed6811f99360b.issues: Single event and location; ML component type and generalization not established; scenarios cover a finite set of perturbations.

2b8439660c70b2a10944df4ce599498abc48bb91.goal: Explains the causes of groundwater drought events across spatial scales using interpretable deep learning.
2b8439660c70b2a10944df4ce599498abc48bb91.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) groundwater models interpreted with expected gradients and additive decomposition.
2b8439660c70b2a10944df4ce599498abc48bb91.data: Groundwater and meteorological records for 16 regions in the southeastern United States at three spatial scales; 233 drought events identified with the standardized groundwater index.
2b8439660c70b2a10944df4ce599498abc48bb91.result: Temperature-related features drive large-scale groundwater droughts (importance rising from 56.1% to 63.1% approaching onset), while precipitation dominates in small catchments; temperature shows a trigger effect.
2b8439660c70b2a10944df4ce599498abc48bb91.open_work: Extending interpretable deep learning to other aquifers and hydrological processes and linking findings to physical mechanisms.
2b8439660c70b2a10944df4ce599498abc48bb91.issues: Attributions reflect learned correlations rather than causality; regional focus; results depend on LSTM accuracy and chosen interpretation methods.

2b9f1da2d0551f382ca92b32dd3258fb7833266b.goal: Develops a practical framework for using deep reinforcement learning to schedule irrigation adaptively from crop and soil sensor information.
2b9f1da2d0551f382ca92b32dd3258fb7833266b.architecture: Deep reinforcement learning policy (neural network) mapping nine state variables to a probabilistic choice among five daily irrigation amounts, trained in a crop-model environment.
2b9f1da2d0551f382ca92b32dd3258fb7833266b.data: APSIM-Wheat simulations at Goondiwindi, Australia, trained with 1981 to 2010 weather and tested on each year 2011 to 2020.
2b9f1da2d0551f382ca92b32dd3258fb7833266b.result: The learned rule improves profit over the conventional regional rule in every test year, with the largest gain of 17% in 2018.
2b9f1da2d0551f382ca92b32dd3258fb7833266b.open_work: Applying the framework to other cropping systems, real sensor data and field trials.
2b9f1da2d0551f382ca92b32dd3258fb7833266b.issues: Simulation-only with a crop model as environment; assumes perfect state observations; single site and crop.

ddbe8ac6d4f77ba262a67f3d24a1f288545b0826.goal: Improves predictive understanding of how ENSO and global sea surface temperatures drive river flows by opening up black-box deep learning.
ddbe8ac6d4f77ba262a67f3d24a1f288545b0826.architecture: Explainable deep learning with saliency maps on convolutional neural network SST predictors, combined with complex climate networks, with uncertainty estimation.
ddbe8ac6d4f77ba262a67f3d24a1f288545b0826.data: Global SST from observations, reanalysis and Earth system model simulations, paired with river flow records for selected major rivers.
ddbe8ac6d4f77ba262a67f3d24a1f288545b0826.result: Global SST holds predictive information beyond ENSO indices; saliency identifies relevant SST regions and dependencies, improving river flow prediction with uncertainty.
ddbe8ac6d4f77ba262a67f3d24a1f288545b0826.open_work: Using explainable DL for climate-informed water resource projections and coupling with Earth system models.
ddbe8ac6d4f77ba262a67f3d24a1f288545b0826.issues: Saliency maps can be noisy and model-dependent; few rivers; relies on Earth system model fidelity for projections.

153146f09d0621182db3cdd3a7f7e566bcf9cd09.goal: Downscales ERA5 wind speed to local scale for energy system modeling, such as small wind farms and community energy systems.
153146f09d0621182db3cdd3a7f7e566bcf9cd09.architecture: Statistical downscaling with machine learning regression applied per region class, after classifying regions into three classes by ERA5 quality, using topographic metrics.
153146f09d0621182db3cdd3a7f7e566bcf9cd09.data: ERA5 wind speed (about 31 km) downscaled to 1 km using weather station observations and topographic metrics; compared with COSMO-REA6 and independent validation datasets.
153146f09d0621182db3cdd3a7f7e566bcf9cd09.result: The approach significantly improves ERA5 wind speed performance in complex terrain, validated against COSMO-REA6 and independent observations.
153146f09d0621182db3cdd3a7f7e566bcf9cd09.open_work: Extending to hub-height winds, other regions and direct use in energy system models.
153146f09d0621182db3cdd3a7f7e566bcf9cd09.issues: Depends on station density; near-surface winds may differ from turbine hub height; specific regression method and numbers not given in the abstract.

4ebeda8b8aa7377d81f555cdd0d633ac4123a986.goal: Builds scalable, accurate hydrologic models that exploit river network structure, aiding flood warning with limited training data.
4ebeda8b8aa7377d81f555cdd0d633ac4123a986.architecture: HydroNets: a family of deep neural network models structured along the river network, combining basin-specific rainfall-runoff modules with upstream routing dynamics.
4ebeda8b8aa7377d81f555cdd0d633ac4123a986.data: Two large river basins in India with only a few years of data.
4ebeda8b8aa7377d81f555cdd0d633ac4123a986.result: Injecting river structure reduces sample complexity and improves predictions, especially at longer horizons, compared with structure-agnostic baselines.
4ebeda8b8aa7377d81f555cdd0d633ac4123a986.open_work: Scaling to more basins and global flood forecasting, and testing robustness to climate-driven distribution shift.
4ebeda8b8aa7377d81f555cdd0d633ac4123a986.issues: Only two basins evaluated; quantitative skill not reported in the abstract; short records limit extreme-event evaluation.

5cbbfa92ad68b8a0b61949fec2a3dc4adb554409.goal: Improves prediction of soil moisture in the unsaturated zone by adding physical mechanisms to data-driven deep learning.
5cbbfa92ad68b8a0b61949fec2a3dc4adb554409.architecture: Physics-informed deep learning (PIDL): LSTM-based network with a loss constrained by water balance, Richards equation and soil moisture boundary conditions.
5cbbfa92ad68b8a0b61949fec2a3dc4adb554409.data: Many in situ soil moisture observation sites in the field.
5cbbfa92ad68b8a0b61949fec2a3dc4adb554409.result: PIDL reduces soil moisture RMSE by 51.03% vs ordinary LSTM and 53.46% vs physical models, and performs better with sparse data, extremes and abrupt changes and over longer prediction periods.
5cbbfa92ad68b8a0b61949fec2a3dc4adb554409.open_work: Generalizing the hybrid approach to other hydrological prediction problems.
5cbbfa92ad68b8a0b61949fec2a3dc4adb554409.issues: Site-based tests; physical constraints rely on simplified Richards equation parameters; regional transferability not shown.

543c44b484e014507fa9e982997989be48e1eb7e.goal: Estimates flash drought intensification rate and detects flash droughts in China while examining their meteorological drivers.
543c44b484e014507fa9e982997989be48e1eb7e.architecture: Multiple linear regression, long short-term memory (LSTM) and random forest models relating rate of intensification to nine climate variables.
543c44b484e014507fa9e982997989be48e1eb7e.data: Global reanalysis soil moisture and climate variables, China, 1979 to 2016 (weekly soil moisture percentiles).
543c44b484e014507fa9e982997989be48e1eb7e.result: Random forest is best: average CC 0.90 and RMSE 2.6 percentile/week in southeastern China; flash drought POD 0.93, FAR 0.15, CSI 0.80; P deficit and PET excess act synergistically.
543c44b484e014507fa9e982997989be48e1eb7e.open_work: Using ML for operational flash drought monitoring and early warning and improving performance in arid regions such as Xinjiang.
543c44b484e014507fa9e982997989be48e1eb7e.issues: Relies on reanalysis soil moisture and its biases; poor performance in Xinjiang; diagnostic rather than predictive at lead time.

28a71d87c76b9bd25314dabc064b28985c30cb63.goal: Captures the state of multiple global climate signals to improve seasonal forecasts and inform reservoir operations in regions where ENSO teleconnections are unclear.
28a71d87c76b9bd25314dabc064b28985c30cb63.architecture: Climate State Intelligence framework: AI-based feature extraction from global SST and climate fields feeding seasonal forecast models, used as inputs to optimized lake operating policies.
28a71d87c76b9bd25314dabc064b28985c30cb63.data: Global SST anomalies and climate indices (ENSO, NAO) with hydrometeorological data for Lake Como basin, northern Italy.
28a71d87c76b9bd25314dabc064b28985c30cb63.result: Teleconnections from ENSO and NAO give skillful seasonal precipitation and inflow forecasts; forecast-informed operations improve system performance by 44% on average, 59% using preseason SST anomalies directly.
28a71d87c76b9bd25314dabc064b28985c30cb63.open_work: Applying the framework to other basins and integrating dynamical seasonal forecasts.
28a71d87c76b9bd25314dabc064b28985c30cb63.issues: Single regulated lake; teleconnection signals may be nonstationary; value depends on operating objectives.

f6f222e5d6932eee7052356df292b18803384986.goal: Evaluates whether machine learning improves estimation of crop yield response to climate change compared with linear regression.
f6f222e5d6932eee7052356df292b18803384986.architecture: Boosted regression trees compared with ordinary least squares linear regression (including quadratic and piece-wise linear specifications).
f6f222e5d6932eee7052356df292b18803384986.data: Synthetic climate and yield data for tests; historical district crop yields of rice, wheat and pearl millet with climate data in India.
f6f222e5d6932eee7052356df292b18803384986.result: BRTs predict better and find climate-yield break points and interactions, but estimate a considerably smaller negative climate change impact than LR, possibly by conflating time and climate.
f6f222e5d6932eee7052356df292b18803384986.open_work: Developing methods that keep ML flexibility while correctly separating trends from climate effects, and using multi-model analyses.
f6f222e5d6932eee7052356df292b18803384986.issues: Overly flexible models can confound time trends and climate; attribution sensitive to model choice; India-specific.

fc03b7cbe542c8471b7d4c9cd452eba253834410.goal: Improves medium-term photovoltaic and wind power forecasting under intermittency by using numerical weather predictions, as implied by the title.
fc03b7cbe542c8471b7d4c9cd452eba253834410.architecture: Hybrid xLSTM (extended long short-term memory) and temporal convolutional CNN (TCCNN) deep learning model driven by NWP inputs.
fc03b7cbe542c8471b7d4c9cd452eba253834410.data: Not reported in the abstract (abstract unavailable); presumably NWP forecasts and PV and wind farm power records.
fc03b7cbe542c8471b7d4c9cd452eba253834410.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title suggests improved handling of intermittency over baselines.
fc03b7cbe542c8471b7d4c9cd452eba253834410.open_work: Probabilistic forecasting and transfer to other plants and climates.
fc03b7cbe542c8471b7d4c9cd452eba253834410.issues: Abstract unavailable, so data, horizons and skill cannot be verified; likely site-specific evaluation.

4d6e80bd79393fd116e76e46df93351e65f87ad1.goal: Estimates global and direct solar irradiance from satellite observations for solar energy applications, as implied by the title.
4d6e80bd79393fd116e76e46df93351e65f87ad1.architecture: Deep learning model using selected spectral bands of satellite images; the network design is not available.
4d6e80bd79393fd116e76e46df93351e65f87ad1.data: Not reported in the abstract (abstract unavailable); presumably geostationary satellite spectral imagery with ground irradiance measurements.
4d6e80bd79393fd116e76e46df93351e65f87ad1.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title suggests selected spectral bands support accurate global and direct irradiance estimation.
4d6e80bd79393fd116e76e46df93351e65f87ad1.open_work: Extension to forecasting and other regions and satellites.
4d6e80bd79393fd116e76e46df93351e65f87ad1.issues: Abstract unavailable, so satellite, region and accuracy cannot be verified; direct irradiance is sensitive to aerosols and thin clouds.

8b46b03e1403cb6353a2d5c24678c46e9de22adc.goal: Tests whether LSTM deep learning matches conceptual models for monthly rainfall-runoff prediction in Australia's dry, variable climate.
8b46b03e1403cb6353a2d5c24678c46e9de22adc.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) networks compared with the WAPABA conceptual monthly rainfall-runoff model.
8b46b03e1403cb6353a2d5c24678c46e9de22adc.data: Almost 500 Australian catchments at monthly time step; study period with a wet phase followed by a prolonged drought (Millennium Drought).
8b46b03e1403cb6353a2d5c24678c46e9de22adc.result: LSTMs match or exceed WAPABA in over two-thirds of catchments, gain most in large catchments, and generalize better to new conditions; short records benefit neither.
8b46b03e1403cb6353a2d5c24678c46e9de22adc.open_work: Improving LSTM training with small monthly datasets and use for climate change water resources planning.
8b46b03e1403cb6353a2d5c24678c46e9de22adc.issues: Monthly data give small training sets; nonstationarity from drought challenges both models; limited interpretability.

8390a14b8f73d63dc25f2accec7f040926c9829e.goal: Segments floods in near real time from high-resolution satellite and aerial imagery without hand labels.
8390a14b8f73d63dc25f2accec7f040926c9829e.architecture: H2O-Net: self-supervised deep convolutional segmentation network with adversarial domain adaptation (GAN-style synthesis of water-correlated signals) and coarse-to-fine label refinement.
8390a14b8f73d63dc25f2accec7f040926c9829e.data: High-resolution commercial satellite imagery (PlanetScope) with Sentinel-2/Landsat-derived water indices for domain bridging; transfer test on drone imagery.
8390a14b8f73d63dc25f2accec7f040926c9829e.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art semantic segmentation for flood mapping by 10% pixel accuracy and 12% mIoU, and transfers to drone imagery.
8390a14b8f73d63dc25f2accec7f040926c9829e.open_work: Real-time deployment for flood alerts and broader sensor and geographic generalization.
8390a14b8f73d63dc25f2accec7f040926c9829e.issues: Optical imagery is blocked by clouds during floods; self-generated labels may carry index errors; limited event set.

c7701551acc26fcc7b620e08435913c4a353eaae.goal: Provides a standardized public benchmark dataset for sky-image-based short-term solar (PV) forecasting with deep learning.
c7701551acc26fcc7b620e08435913c4a353eaae.architecture: Benchmark dataset with code base for processing and baseline deep learning models (convolutional neural network) for PV nowcasting and forecasting.
c7701551acc26fcc7b620e08435913c4a353eaae.data: Three years (2017 to 2019) of quality-controlled sky images and PV power from Stanford University, downsampled 64x64 images plus high-resolution images and sky video.
c7701551acc26fcc7b620e08435913c4a353eaae.result: Releases ready-to-use sky image and PV data with baselines to enable model comparison and reproducibility.
c7701551acc26fcc7b620e08435913c4a353eaae.open_work: Adding more sites and climates, and benchmarking new architectures and probabilistic forecasts.
c7701551acc26fcc7b620e08435913c4a353eaae.issues: Single site and climate; short-term horizons only; downsampled images may lose cloud detail.

366e1374609a99480d96f2752fee6583d0670f22.goal: Improves rice crop yield prediction by fusing satellite remote sensing and meteorological data.
366e1374609a99480d96f2752fee6583d0670f22.architecture: RicEns-Net: deep ensemble combining multiple machine learning algorithms over 15 selected features from 5 modalities.
366e1374609a99480d96f2752fee6583d0670f22.data: Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3 optical data, surface temperature and rainfall; field yields from the EY Open Science Challenge 2023 (Vietnam rice).
366e1374609a99480d96f2752fee6583d0670f22.result: MAE of 341 kg/ha (about 5 to 6% of the lowest average regional yield), outperforming prior models including EY challenge entries.
366e1374609a99480d96f2752fee6583d0670f22.open_work: Testing on other crops and regions and with longer yield records.
366e1374609a99480d96f2752fee6583d0670f22.issues: Small single-region dataset; heavy feature engineering risks overfitting; no uncertainty quantification.

9f2c5afd75fcf9291abc6e7437078ecdbf945e23.goal: Attributes past and future European wheat yield shocks to climate drivers to inform food security under climate change.
9f2c5afd75fcf9291abc6e7437078ecdbf945e23.architecture: Data-driven attribution framework based on machine learning with game-theoretic Shapley values, predicting yield-shock probability.
9f2c5afd75fcf9291abc6e7437078ecdbf945e23.data: Subnational wheat yields across Europe 1980 to 2018 with climate data; RCP4.5 and RCP8.5 projections for 2070 to 2099; crop model ensemble yields for comparison.
9f2c5afd75fcf9291abc6e7437078ecdbf945e23.result: Water limitation drove 32% of past yield shocks; in 2070 to 2099 extreme warming dominates in 46% (RCP4.5) and 54% (RCP8.5) of areas; crop models miss excess-water impacts.
9f2c5afd75fcf9291abc6e7437078ecdbf945e23.open_work: Improving crop models to represent excess water and heat extremes, and including adaptation.
9f2c5afd75fcf9291abc6e7437078ecdbf945e23.issues: Statistical extrapolation to future climates beyond the training range; no adaptation or CO2 effects; attribution is associative.

beed60a1eb8775eba1ad18567972224309a91872.goal: Improves calibration and parameter regionalization of the U.S. National Water Model for high-resolution flood forecasting and water management.
beed60a1eb8775eba1ad18567972224309a91872.architecture: Differentiable hybrid models with neural network multiscale parameterization of process-based equations, with unit-hydrograph or Muskingum-Cunge river routing, trained end to end.
beed60a1eb8775eba1ad18567972224309a91872.data: 2,807 CONUS basins for training and 4,997 basins for evaluation at about 37 km2 resolution; compared with NWM 3.0.
beed60a1eb8775eba1ad18567972224309a91872.result: Median daily NSE improves to about 0.68 from 0.48 for NWM 3.0, with large gains in the western CONUS and Prairie Pothole Region; Muskingum-Cunge helps basins over 10,000 km2.
beed60a1eb8775eba1ad18567972224309a91872.open_work: Integration with the next-generation NWM via BMI and operational flood prediction; a released CONUS hydrologic dataset.
beed60a1eb8775eba1ad18567972224309a91872.issues: Process structure still simplified; computational cost of training; evaluation focuses on streamflow.

6feadd48e8d909cb2668e348cc5cf0b522e300ec.goal: Learns data-driven equivalents of hydrologic signatures from streamflow and climate to improve rainfall-runoff modeling in ungauged watersheds.
6feadd48e8d909cb2668e348cc5cf0b522e300ec.architecture: Encoder-decoder model: convolutional neural network encoder producing a low-dimensional signature encoding, and a process-informed decoder with stores and fluxes.
6feadd48e8d909cb2668e348cc5cf0b522e300ec.data: U.S. CAMELS watershed dataset (streamflow, climate forcing and attributes).
6feadd48e8d909cb2668e348cc5cf0b522e300ec.result: Learned signatures improve prediction over classical or no signatures and relate to seasonality, extremes, baseflow and recessions.
6feadd48e8d909cb2668e348cc5cf0b522e300ec.open_work: Replacing expert-selected signatures with learned ones in other hydrologic applications.
6feadd48e8d909cb2668e348cc5cf0b522e300ec.issues: Encodings are less directly interpretable; CAMELS-only; ungauged application still needs some flow data for encoding.

3935221db2083cc7529924311994f9edbb9635ee.goal: Enables implicit numerical schemes in differentiable hydrological models to avoid numerical errors from explicit operator-splitting schemes.
3935221db2083cc7529924311994f9edbb9635ee.architecture: Discretize-then-optimize adjoint method for gradients through implicit solvers in a differentiable model where neural networks parameterize a process-based hydrologic model (HBV-type).
3935221db2083cc7529924311994f9edbb9635ee.data: Large-sample US basins (CAMELS) streamflow and evapotranspiration data.
3935221db2083cc7529924311994f9edbb9635ee.result: Adjoint model moderately improves KGE, peak and low flows and ET over the explicit model; with capillary rise, low flows beat LSTM; spatial parameter patterns remain robust.
3935221db2083cc7529924311994f9edbb9635ee.open_work: Using implicit schemes to enrich differentiable models with more complex physics.
3935221db2083cc7529924311994f9edbb9635ee.issues: Higher computational cost with modest improvements; evaluation limited to selected basins and metrics.

a97fdba28c880476677bf94577cd293683f6a874.goal: Estimates current and future irrigation water use across China to inform water allocation under climate change.
a97fdba28c880476677bf94577cd293683f6a874.architecture: Machine learning framework (specific algorithm not named in the abstract) combining multiple datasets, forced with climate and socio-economic projections.
a97fdba28c880476677bf94577cd293683f6a874.data: Prefecture-level reported irrigation water use, multiple climate and socio-economic datasets, 11 cropland validation sites; future emission scenario projections.
a97fdba28c880476677bf94577cd293683f6a874.result: R2 0.86 to 0.91 and RMSE 0.261 to 0.361 km3/yr against prefecture data; IWU increases 8.5 to 17.1% by 2050s and 6.8 to 34.8% by 2100s, costing US$1.65 to 6.5 billion/year.
a97fdba28c880476677bf94577cd293683f6a874.open_work: Transferring the framework to other countries facing rising irrigation demand.
a97fdba28c880476677bf94577cd293683f6a874.issues: Future projections assume stable learned relationships; site validation R2 only 0.67; socio-economic uncertainty large.

f7f4dab5622801d1fc1894b015053bb0019fc429.goal: Extends near-surface ESA CCI satellite soil moisture to root-zone depth globally.
f7f4dab5622801d1fc1894b015053bb0019fc429.architecture: Soil Water Index calibration against in situ data, regionalized with machine learning using soil, vegetation and climate descriptors.
f7f4dab5622801d1fc1894b015053bb0019fc429.data: ESA CCI soil moisture, International Soil Moisture Network in situ data, global descriptors; 2001 to 2018; compared with ERA5-Land and FLDAS.
f7f4dab5622801d1fc1894b015053bb0019fc429.result: Root-zone soil moisture agrees well with ERA5-Land and FLDAS, mainly at mid-latitudes.
f7f4dab5622801d1fc1894b015053bb0019fc429.open_work: Wider exploitation of the product for large-scale soil moisture studies and improving high-latitude and tropical performance.
f7f4dab5622801d1fc1894b015053bb0019fc429.issues: Sparse in situ network limits calibration in many regions; weaker agreement outside mid-latitudes; ML method details not in abstract.

b2642685741f1b3c8f6b7088c45ae2e47896eae1.goal: Estimates design floods anywhere on the global river network, especially in ungauged areas.
b2642685741f1b3c8f6b7088c45ae2e47896eae1.architecture: Flood frequency fitting with Bayesian MCMC, K-means clustering of stations, and regional regression models including support vector machine regression.
b2642685741f1b3c8f6b7088c45ae2e47896eae1.data: 11,793 global gauging stations with twelve globally available catchment descriptors.
b2642685741f1b3c8f6b7088c45ae2e47896eae1.result: SVM regression performs best (normalized RMSE 0.708 for 100-year floods); average relative bias under 18% for 10 to 100 year floods, improving on the index-flood method.
b2642685741f1b3c8f6b7088c45ae2e47896eae1.open_work: Applying estimates to global flood hazard mapping and accounting for nonstationarity.
b2642685741f1b3c8f6b7088c45ae2e47896eae1.issues: Assumes stationary flood frequency; station distribution uneven across climates; ungauged accuracy limited by descriptors.

21f292bcd4150190a7718e6043ec29f4f51effac.goal: Provides an open, deep-learning-ready multi-modal dataset for county-level crop yield prediction that accounts for both growing-season weather and long-term climate change.
21f292bcd4150190a7718e6043ec29f4f51effac.architecture: Benchmark dataset (CropNet) with a Python package of three APIs for on-the-fly download; baselines use various deep learning models (CNN, LSTM, transformer-type) for yield prediction.
21f292bcd4150190a7718e6043ec29f4f51effac.data: Sentinel-2 imagery, WRF-HRRR computed meteorological data and USDA crop yield statistics for over 2200 contiguous US counties, 2017–2022; terabyte scale, released on Hugging Face.
21f292bcd4150190a7718e6043ec29f4f51effac.result: Experiments with several deep learning solutions show the dataset is generally applicable and effective for climate change-aware crop yield prediction; no single headline metric is reported in the abstract.
21f292bcd4150190a7718e6043ec29f4f51effac.open_work: Extending coverage beyond the US and beyond six years, adding further modalities, and using the data for climate-scenario yield projection.
21f292bcd4150190a7718e6043ec29f4f51effac.issues: Only six years of yields limit learning of long-term climate effects; county-level aggregation and HRRR-derived weather may carry model biases; US-only coverage.

a2c20521084a754bcf4171e824655441986d4ae6.goal: Fills gaps in daily ESA CCI satellite soil moisture caused by poor coverage, snow, frozen soil and radio-frequency interference, to provide spatiotemporally continuous data for hydrological and ecological research.
a2c20521084a754bcf4171e824655441986d4ae6.architecture: Spatiotemporal machine learning gap-filling approach combining satellite observations with model-driven knowledge (bias-corrected model diurnal temperature range) and a residual calibration step; tree-based ML regression.
a2c20521084a754bcf4171e824655441986d4ae6.data: ESA CCI soil moisture over China, satellite-derived and model-derived diurnal temperature range and other explanatory variables; validated against multiple in situ networks; long-term application 2005–2015.
a2c20521084a754bcf4171e824655441986d4ae6.result: In situ validation gives RMSE 0.09–0.14 and MAE 0.07–0.13 cm3/cm3; 10-fold cross-validation median R2 0.56, RMSE 0.025; long-term trend R2 0.49 versus 0.28 for the original CCI product.
a2c20521084a754bcf4171e824655441986d4ae6.open_work: Applying the approach to other regions and other gap-prone satellite variables, and improving accuracy where model-derived predictors replace satellite ones.
a2c20521084a754bcf4171e824655441986d4ae6.issues: Moderate R2; model-derived DTR yields lower accuracy than satellite DTR; performance drops sharply when any explanatory variable is removed; demonstrated only for China.

95d2c0cc173a2bea6746d1971add6cd469294560.goal: Overcomes the computational cost of running process-based agricultural system models at regional scale to support nitrogen and water management decisions under climate change.
95d2c0cc173a2bea6746d1971add6cd469294560.architecture: Machine learning emulators (surrogate models) trained to reproduce the APSIM crop model outputs of yield and soil organic carbon under many management scenarios; specific ML algorithms not named in the abstract.
95d2c0cc173a2bea6746d1971add6cd469294560.data: APSIM simulations for the Huang-Huai-Hai plain, China, over 101 years (1980–2080) under many nitrogen and irrigation scenarios with climate forcing.
95d2c0cc173a2bea6746d1971add6cd469294560.result: Emulators accurately and quickly reproduce APSIM yield and soil carbon predictions at different spatial resolutions with much less input data and identify optimal nitrogen management for yield and carbon sequestration.
95d2c0cc173a2bea6746d1971add6cd469294560.open_work: Extending emulation to other crop models, regions and complex systems, and using it in policy-relevant scenario analysis.
95d2c0cc173a2bea6746d1971add6cd469294560.issues: Emulators inherit APSIM structural and parameter uncertainty; evaluated against the model rather than observations; validity outside the training scenarios is uncertain.

e535916aabd5d89aa8617a68fb853fcaa774bbb5.goal: Improves surface soil moisture prediction by embedding causal relations among hydrometeorological variables into a deep learning model.
e535916aabd5d89aa8617a68fb853fcaa774bbb5.architecture: Causality-structured LSTM (CLSTM) that incorporates a causal graph learned from the data alongside temporal dependencies, compared with a standard LSTM.
e535916aabd5d89aa8617a68fb853fcaa774bbb5.data: Surface soil moisture and meteorological drivers at 64 FLUXNET sites worldwide.
e535916aabd5d89aa8617a68fb853fcaa774bbb5.result: CLSTM outperforms LSTM, with more than 67% of sites improving NSE by over 10%, better generalization under extreme conditions such as drought and precipitation events, and gains across lead times.
e535916aabd5d89aa8617a68fb853fcaa774bbb5.open_work: Applying causality-structured networks to other hydrometeorological variables and to drought prediction.
e535916aabd5d89aa8617a68fb853fcaa774bbb5.issues: Point-scale site evaluation only; causal discovery may be sensitive to method choices and data length; no gridded or operational test.

ca83ea33ea88f7d467515bb3240692b1a829bfff.goal: Addresses the lack of large annotated SAR datasets for deep learning flood segmentation needed for rapid global flood mapping.
ca83ea33ea88f7d467515bb3240692b1a829bfff.architecture: Benchmark dataset (Kuro Siwo) of manually annotated multi-temporal SAR flood maps plus a benchmark (BlackBench) of segmentation baselines such as U-Net-type CNNs and transformer models, with unlabeled data for self-supervised pretraining.
ca83ea33ea88f7d467515bb3240692b1a829bfff.data: Sentinel-1 SAR Ground Range Detected and Single Look Complex products for 43 flood events worldwide, covering over 338 billion m2 with 33 billion m2 flooded or permanent water, plus a large unlabeled SAR set.
ca83ea33ea88f7d467515bb3240692b1a829bfff.result: Provides strong baselines for flood events across Europe, America, Africa, Asia and Australia; specific scores are not reported in the abstract.
ca83ea33ea88f7d467515bb3240692b1a829bfff.open_work: Exploiting SAR phase information from SLC data, self-supervised pretraining at scale, and adding more events and regions.
ca83ea33ea88f7d467515bb3240692b1a829bfff.issues: 43 events may under-sample flood types such as urban or vegetated flooding where SAR is weak; manual labels can contain errors.

6a21dcdd1680932d83776039c1a6e58fd8b795ed.goal: Tests whether global entity-aware deep learning models, as used in rainfall-runoff modelling, can predict groundwater levels across many wells and generalize spatially.
6a21dcdd1680932d83776039c1a6e58fd8b795ed.architecture: Global deep learning model (sequence network) with static well features: environmental attributes, time-series-derived features, or random integer identifiers as a control.
6a21dcdd1680932d83776039c1a6e58fd8b795ed.data: Published dataset of 108 groundwater monitoring wells in Germany with meteorological inputs; in-sample (temporal) and out-of-sample (spatial) evaluation.
6a21dcdd1680932d83776039c1a6e58fd8b795ed.result: In-sample mean NSE above 0.8, comparable to single-well models, but out-of-sample NSE below 0.7; all static feature types, including random ones, perform equally, so the model uses them only as identifiers.
6a21dcdd1680932d83776039c1a6e58fd8b795ed.open_work: Larger well datasets and more meaningful static features to achieve genuine entity awareness and regionalization in hydrogeology.
6a21dcdd1680932d83776039c1a6e58fd8b795ed.issues: Small dataset of 108 wells; no real entity awareness learned; spatial generalization is poor.

cc0775c953564c6bf23b7a4b3c1ad96417fc3fdb.goal: Bridges machine learning and process-based hydrology by reviewing physics-aware machine learning approaches for water cycle prediction under climate change.
cc0775c953564c6bf23b7a4b3c1ad96417fc3fdb.architecture: Review of physics-aware ML in four classes: physical data-guided, physics-informed, physics-embedded and physics-aware hybrid learning, applied to rainfall-runoff and hydrodynamic processes; releases the HydroPML platform.
cc0775c953564c6bf23b7a4b3c1ad96417fc3fdb.data: Literature review; the HydroPML platform hosts hydrological methods and data, publicly available.
cc0775c953564c6bf23b7a4b3c1ad96417fc3fdb.result: Structures the field into a community of methods, identifies promising and challenging directions, and releases HydroPML as a foundation for hydrological applications.
cc0775c953564c6bf23b7a4b3c1ad96417fc3fdb.open_work: Developing explainable and causal ML for hydrology and progressing toward a digital water cycle.
cc0775c953564c6bf23b7a4b3c1ad96417fc3fdb.issues: Review framing is broad and somewhat promotional; platform maturity and benchmark coverage are not detailed in the abstract.

678b7cac4c3b9b643a6ef43b9c9340603b160953.goal: Enables real-time daily monitoring of rapidly developing flash droughts over the contiguous United States.
678b7cac4c3b9b643a6ef43b9c9340603b160953.architecture: Generative adversarial network (GAN) with a Markovian (PatchGAN) discriminator and a modified U-Net generator; four generator losses compared (MAE, adversarial, adversarial plus MSE, adversarial plus MAE).
678b7cac4c3b9b643a6ef43b9c9340603b160953.data: Daily NLDAS-2 forcing and land surface data with Standardized Soil Moisture Index (SSI) maps over CONUS.
678b7cac4c3b9b643a6ef43b9c9340603b160953.result: The GAN reproduces SSI better than U-Net and naive baselines and captures fine and coarse spatial drought patterns and abrupt temporal changes important for flash drought identification.
678b7cac4c3b9b643a6ef43b9c9340603b160953.open_work: Operational deployment, extension to other drought indices and regions, and uncertainty quantification.
678b7cac4c3b9b643a6ef43b9c9340603b160953.issues: Target SSI is model-derived from NLDAS-2, so it inherits land surface model biases; no probabilistic output; quantitative scores not given in the abstract.

d895e34407234027715751922f77c079d3f690ec.goal: Improves medium-lead streamflow forecast accuracy for flood warning in snow-fed Himalayan rivers through dynamic error correction.
d895e34407234027715751922f77c079d3f690ec.architecture: Hybrid physics-aware framework coupling the HBV conceptual hydrological model, a particle filter for data assimilation, and random forest error correction, producing an ensemble of streamflow.
d895e34407234027715751922f77c079d3f690ec.data: Observed streamflow and meteorological forcing for the Beas River (India) and Sunkoshi River (Nepal).
d895e34407234027715751922f77c079d3f690ec.result: For 7-day-ahead forecasts NSE reaches 0.94 and 0.98 in calibration and 0.95 and 0.99 in validation for Beas and Sunkoshi respectively.
d895e34407234027715751922f77c079d3f690ec.open_work: Testing in more basins, with forecast meteorological inputs, and for extreme flood events.
d895e34407234027715751922f77c079d3f690ec.issues: Only two basins; very high NSE may reflect error correction using recent observations; reliance on forecast forcing quality not discussed.

09c672f0e443169ce7d4cfa044277bf57af418f5.goal: Infers robust catchment characteristics from meteorological drivers and streamflow responses because existing basin attributes are noisy, uncertain or missing, harming broad-scale streamflow models.
09c672f0e443169ce7d4cfa044277bf57af418f5.architecture: Knowledge-guided self-supervised learning (KGSSL) inverse framework with an encoder that learns basin characteristics from driver-response sequences, coupled to an LSTM-type forward streamflow model.
09c672f0e443169ce7d4cfa044277bf57af418f5.data: CAMELS (Catchment Attributes and Meteorology for Large-sample Studies) US benchmark basins.
09c672f0e443169ce7d4cfa044277bf57af418f5.result: KGSSL outperforms baselines by 16% in predicting missing characteristics and gives a 35% improvement in forward streamflow modelling when static characteristics are unknown.
09c672f0e443169ce7d4cfa044277bf57af418f5.open_work: Extending to ungauged basins and other environmental systems where system characteristics are uncertain.
09c672f0e443169ce7d4cfa044277bf57af418f5.issues: Requires response data to infer characteristics, limiting use in ungauged basins; evaluated only on CAMELS.

9f2ce0d3bdc4b8a1acc2695ebd83ff2daf720277.goal: Develops a spatially distributed hybrid physics-AI hydrological model to improve high-resolution regional flood modelling and learn interpretable corrections to internal fluxes.
9f2ce0d3bdc4b8a1acc2695ebd83ff2daf720277.architecture: Differentiable process-based model with kinematic wave routing on a flow-direction grid, hybridized with a neural network (MLP) process-parameterization network correcting internal fluxes and a regionalization network estimating parameters, trained jointly.
9f2ce0d3bdc4b8a1acc2695ebd83ff2daf720277.data: Two high-resolution datasets (1 km, 1 h): 235 catchments in France for calibration and validation, and a multi-catchment flash-flood-prone setup for regionalization.
9f2ce0d3bdc4b8a1acc2695ebd83ff2daf720277.result: Hybrid models achieve higher accuracy and robustness than the classical GR-like model in both spatial and temporal validation, with interpretable parameter and flux patterns.
9f2ce0d3bdc4b8a1acc2695ebd83ff2daf720277.open_work: Using learned flux corrections to discover scale-relevant hydrological laws and extending to other regions and processes.
9f2ce0d3bdc4b8a1acc2695ebd83ff2daf720277.issues: Regional focus on France; interpretability of learned corrections remains partly qualitative; quantitative gains not stated in the abstract.

528bfb06f48b0885db59d52ba8605b56cfe625f6.goal: Uses interpretable deep learning to reveal how flood drivers vary in space and time under climate change rather than treating deep learning as a black box.
528bfb06f48b0885db59d52ba8605b56cfe625f6.architecture: Peak-sensitive Informer (transformer variant) compared with transformer and LSTM, combined with interpretability (attribution) techniques.
528bfb06f48b0885db59d52ba8605b56cfe625f6.data: 482 watersheds across the United States, 1981–2020, with precipitation, soil water and snowmelt drivers.
528bfb06f48b0885db59d52ba8605b56cfe625f6.result: Informer gives NSE above 0.6 in 70% of watersheds for peak flows; three flood-inducing patterns are identified (precipitation, excess soil water, snowmelt) and over 40% of watersheds show shifts in dominant drivers.
528bfb06f48b0885db59d52ba8605b56cfe625f6.open_work: Using interpretable deep learning for process discovery in other hydrological variables and regions.
528bfb06f48b0885db59d52ba8605b56cfe625f6.issues: Interpretations depend on attribution method reliability; NSE above 0.6 in only 70% of basins limits trust elsewhere; attribution of driver shifts to climate change is correlative.

de02efe6aeb6e701536b6941b928c36ee0b064d3.goal: Improves representation of land-atmosphere energy and water exchange in regional climate simulations by optimizing surface soil and vegetation conditions.
de02efe6aeb6e701536b6941b928c36ee0b064d3.architecture: Hybrid data assimilation and machine learning (DA-ML) framework implemented in the WRF model with land surface models, assimilating LAI and soil moisture; ML used to estimate evapotranspiration-related fields.
de02efe6aeb6e701536b6941b928c36ee0b064d3.data: Remotely sensed LAI, multi-source soil moisture observations, large aperture scintillometer flux observations and an ML-based ET map (ETMap) in the Heihe River basin, northwest China.
de02efe6aeb6e701536b6941b928c36ee0b064d3.result: WRF (DA-ML) agrees well with observed sensible and latent heat fluxes, improves ET versus open loop, reduces warm and dry biases especially in oases, and produces more realistic oasis-desert boundaries.
de02efe6aeb6e701536b6941b928c36ee0b064d3.open_work: Applying the framework to other basins with complex surfaces and longer climate simulations.
de02efe6aeb6e701536b6941b928c36ee0b064d3.issues: Single-basin case study; improvements described largely qualitatively in the abstract; computational cost of DA within WRF not discussed.

13d18b5b685b6431b3e0a4aba333857a51d5c80c.goal: Provides real-time street-level flood inundation forecasts, which high-resolution hydrodynamic models are too slow to deliver.
13d18b5b685b6431b3e0a4aba333857a51d5c80c.architecture: Fourier neural operator (FNO) surrogate of a hydrodynamic model for flood extent and depth, compared with a U-Net baseline.
13d18b5b685b6431b3e0a4aba333857a51d5c80c.data: Hydrodynamic simulations of water depth at 15-min intervals for six historical storm events over an urban area of Houston, Texas; two held-out events for testing.
13d18b5b685b6431b3e0a4aba333857a51d5c80c.result: FNO outperforms U-Net, maintains high predictability at lead times up to 3 h, and generalizes well to new sites.
13d18b5b685b6431b3e0a4aba333857a51d5c80c.open_work: Testing on more events and cities and coupling with rainfall forecasts for operational use.
13d18b5b685b6431b3e0a4aba333857a51d5c80c.issues: Trained and evaluated on simulated depths, so it inherits hydrodynamic model errors; only eight events in total.

b7d315be69bc002b8f9e7e1065b2d2e53f9039a6.goal: Uses a generative adversarial network as a multi-site stochastic weather generator to produce synthetic rainfall series for flood frequency estimation.
b7d315be69bc002b8f9e7e1065b2d2e53f9039a6.architecture: Generative adversarial network (GAN) trained to generate spatially correlated multi-site weather (rainfall) time series, which drive a hydrological model for flood frequency analysis.
b7d315be69bc002b8f9e7e1065b2d2e53f9039a6.data: Not reported (abstract unavailable); presumably multi-site station rainfall records from a study catchment.
b7d315be69bc002b8f9e7e1065b2d2e53f9039a6.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title implies the GAN generator yields synthetic weather suitable for estimating flood frequency.
b7d315be69bc002b8f9e7e1065b2d2e53f9039a6.open_work: Likely: comparison with conventional stochastic weather generators and extension to non-stationary climate.
b7d315be69bc002b8f9e7e1065b2d2e53f9039a6.issues: Abstract unavailable; GANs may under-represent rare extremes that dominate flood frequency, and training records are typically short.

2c8c48c80a26beac699d7c81fcc22586adca74c9.goal: Assesses flood predictability for Hurricane Harvey by driving a coupled hydrologic-hydraulic model with high-resolution precipitation forecasts and deep learning nowcasts.
2c8c48c80a26beac699d7c81fcc22586adca74c9.architecture: Non-ML CREST-iMAP coupled hydrologic and inundation model forced by quantitative precipitation forecasts and U-Net deep learning precipitation nowcasts.
2c8c48c80a26beac699d7c81fcc22586adca74c9.data: Not reported (abstract unavailable); likely radar-based precipitation (e.g., MRMS) and NWP quantitative precipitation forecasts for the Houston area during Harvey 2017.
2c8c48c80a26beac699d7c81fcc22586adca74c9.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title implies a comparison of flood forecast skill from QPF versus U-Net nowcast forcing.
2c8c48c80a26beac699d7c81fcc22586adca74c9.open_work: Likely: blending nowcasts and NWP forecasts and testing on more events.
2c8c48c80a26beac699d7c81fcc22586adca74c9.issues: Abstract unavailable; single-event case study; U-Net nowcasts typically blur and underestimate intense rainfall at longer leads.

9f2a6036ab5e8ec4e5c555c65276f5c048e051f8.goal: Produces nationwide 100 m maps of climate change impacts on shallow groundwater table depth in Denmark where running the 100 m hydrological model for a full climate ensemble is infeasible.
9f2a6036ab5e8ec4e5c555c65276f5c048e051f8.architecture: Hybrid downscaling with random forest trained on 100 m hydrological model impact signals, applied to 500 m national model outputs.
9f2a6036ab5e8ec4e5c555c65276f5c048e051f8.data: Danish national integrated surface-subsurface hydrological model (500 m) with a climate model ensemble; 100 m submodels for five subcatchments covering about 9% of Denmark for training; one held-out validation submodel.
9f2a6036ab5e8ec4e5c555c65276f5c048e051f8.result: Downscaled 100 m impact maps validate successfully against the held-out 100 m submodel and are consistent with the 500 m model signals across Denmark.
9f2a6036ab5e8ec4e5c555c65276f5c048e051f8.open_work: Applying the downscaling to other hydrological model outputs and other regions with computational limits.
9f2a6036ab5e8ec4e5c555c65276f5c048e051f8.issues: Validated against model output, not observations; training subcatchments cover only 9% of the country; uses a reduced climate ensemble for training.

580ec7dcb0368b951a6250cc71995503e8dbda5e.goal: Improves the skill and reliability of medium-range (1–7 day) ensemble streamflow forecasts for water management.
580ec7dcb0368b951a6250cc71995503e8dbda5e.architecture: Machine learning postprocessor applied to ensemble streamflow from NWP-forced distributed hydrological model, compared with a neural network and simple baselines; the ML algorithm is not named in the abstract.
580ec7dcb0368b951a6250cc71995503e8dbda5e.data: NWP ensemble forecasts driving a distributed hydrological model in the Upper Susquehanna River basin, eastern United States.
580ec7dcb0368b951a6250cc71995503e8dbda5e.result: The postprocessor beats climatology, persistence, raw hydrometeorological forecasts and a neural network, with larger gains at medium-range leads, high flows and warm season.
580ec7dcb0368b951a6250cc71995503e8dbda5e.open_work: Testing in other basins and with other postprocessing algorithms and forecast systems.
580ec7dcb0368b951a6250cc71995503e8dbda5e.issues: Single basin; gains smaller at short leads and for low-moderate flows; quantitative metrics not given in the abstract.

f30d27bfebe4f32ba2310d043ec62db24e6fae61.goal: Predicts photovoltaic power production 24 and 48 h ahead from numerical weather predictions to reduce reliance on idling backup plants.
f30d27bfebe4f32ba2310d043ec62db24e6fae61.architecture: Long-term recurrent convolutional network (LRCN), combining CNN and LSTM, using spatio-temporal NWP fields over the area of interest.
f30d27bfebe4f32ba2310d043ec62db24e6fae61.data: NOAA numerical weather prediction data (likely GFS) and spatially aggregated PV production in Germany.
f30d27bfebe4f32ba2310d043ec62db24e6fae61.result: The model is compared with persistence and state-of-the-art methods; the abstract does not report numbers beyond claiming competitive performance.
f30d27bfebe4f32ba2310d043ec62db24e6fae61.open_work: Probabilistic forecasting and extension to other regions and finer spatial targets.
f30d27bfebe4f32ba2310d043ec62db24e6fae61.issues: Only aggregated national production predicted; coarse NWP input; quantitative improvements not reported in the abstract.

776f70d2fc19a2d2428cb1af8b69e1f4641cfacd.goal: Assesses the reliability of hydrological models for predicting responses to changed forcings beyond observed conditions, such as climate change, where observations cannot validate them.
776f70d2fc19a2d2428cb1af8b69e1f4641cfacd.architecture: Metamorphic testing with a multi-model approach and sensitivity analysis to training and calibration options, applied to conceptual hydrological models and machine learning models (e.g., LSTM).
776f70d2fc19a2d2428cb1af8b69e1f4641cfacd.data: Selected basins from the CAMELS data set.
776f70d2fc19a2d2428cb1af8b69e1f4641cfacd.result: ML models fit better than conceptual models in calibration and validation, but their response to modified inputs can violate expectations, and its magnitude and even sign depend on training data.
776f70d2fc19a2d2428cb1af8b69e1f4641cfacd.open_work: Using metamorphic tests routinely to diagnose models and to develop models with physically consistent responses.
776f70d2fc19a2d2428cb1af8b69e1f4641cfacd.issues: Expected responses are qualitative and somewhat subjective; limited set of basins and models; does not establish which model is correct for future climates.

705211da5e6e7ce8cf8cd8024f369721be169f1c.goal: Predicts daily streamflow in watersheds that only have monthly aggregated or intermittent observations due to limited monitoring.
705211da5e6e7ce8cf8cd8024f369721be169f1c.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) network trained with aggregated or intermittent targets.
705211da5e6e7ce8cf8cd8024f369721be169f1c.data: Near-natural and human-influenced watersheds with daily data degraded to monthly aggregates and monthly or weekly intermittent samples.
705211da5e6e7ce8cf8cd8024f369721be169f1c.result: Median NSE 0.61 (near-natural) and 0.48 (human-influenced) from monthly aggregates, and 0.70 and 0.55 from intermittent observations; median bias within ±5% except in arid regions.
705211da5e6e7ce8cf8cd8024f369721be169f1c.open_work: Applying the approach in truly data-scarce regions and improving performance in arid and human-influenced basins.
705211da5e6e7ce8cf8cd8024f369721be169f1c.issues: Tested by synthetically degrading observed daily data; weaker in arid and human-influenced watersheds; relies on wet-season data.

147716d862c66d288fffac038d5d0203c1a59568.goal: Improves sub-seasonal (up to 30 day) joint precipitation and streamflow ensemble forecasts for water management in the source region of the Yangtze River.
147716d862c66d288fffac038d5d0203c1a59568.architecture: Ensemble of convolutional neural networks with ResNet blocks and a specialized loss for statistical downscaling of precipitation, coupled to a hybrid Xin'anjiang conceptual model plus LSTM (XAJ-LSTM).
147716d862c66d288fffac038d5d0203c1a59568.data: ECMWF sub-seasonal ensemble precipitation forecasts, observed precipitation and streamflow in the source region of the Yangtze River.
147716d862c66d288fffac038d5d0203c1a59568.result: CNN downscaling cuts RMSE by about 34% vs raw ECMWF and 26% vs quantile mapping; streamflow driven by it has 16–33% lower relative errors and 20–31% lower RMSE, while standalone XAJ gains little.
147716d862c66d288fffac038d5d0203c1a59568.open_work: Extending to other basins and operational sub-seasonal forecasting chains, and understanding hydrologic model sensitivity to forcing improvements.
147716d862c66d288fffac038d5d0203c1a59568.issues: Single basin; heavy-precipitation gains are smaller (6–10%); benefits depend on the hydrological model used.

5c10a40ae24d6ca5549e54e1cd8668d9cfcba310.goal: Develops adaptive coastal flood protection strategies under deep uncertainty in sea-level rise that update as observations accrue.
5c10a40ae24d6ca5549e54e1cd8668d9cfcba310.architecture: Reinforcement learning (deep RL) policy optimization for sequential adaptation decisions, compared with conventional numerical optimization methods.
5c10a40ae24d6ca5549e54e1cd8668d9cfcba310.data: Sea-level rise projections and coastal flood and economic loss models for Manhattan, New York City; specific products not reported in the abstract.
5c10a40ae24d6ca5549e54e1cd8668d9cfcba310.result: RL-based designs substantially reduce costs compared with conventional methods and handle complex policies, extreme losses and potential expert misjudgment.
5c10a40ae24d6ca5549e54e1cd8668d9cfcba310.open_work: Applying RL to broader climate adaptation decisions and other regions and hazards.
5c10a40ae24d6ca5549e54e1cd8668d9cfcba310.issues: Results depend on the assumed sea-level rise and damage models; single case study; RL policy interpretability for decision-makers is a concern.

c95a89bf9603ead29489412c7b57aa9660fddd5b.goal: Improves streamflow prediction in human-regulated catchments by representing anthropogenic disturbance through river-reach attributes.
c95a89bf9603ead29489412c7b57aa9660fddd5b.architecture: Multiscale LSTM and a differentiable parameter learning (DPL) hybrid model, both using combined river-reach and catchment static attributes.
c95a89bf9603ead29489412c7b57aa9660fddd5b.data: 95 human-regulated catchments in the USA and 24 in the Yellow River Basin, China; river attributes such as degree of regulation and dams plus SWOT River Database (SWORD) width, slope and elevation.
c95a89bf9603ead29489412c7b57aa9660fddd5b.result: Median KGE 0.78 (Multiscale LSTM) and 0.71 (DPL) in the USA, and 0.58 and 0.24 in the Yellow River; river-scale attributes dominate and the training period choice is the strongest factor.
c95a89bf9603ead29489412c7b57aa9660fddd5b.open_work: Improving models in heavily regulated basins such as the Yellow River and incorporating more satellite-derived human-influence data.
c95a89bf9603ead29489412c7b57aa9660fddd5b.issues: Much weaker performance in China, especially for DPL; static attributes cannot capture time-varying reservoir operations.

29b7d89323d2e7b27e85f586d46eb830b0786814.goal: Projects climate change impacts on streamflow in the Konya Closed basin, Turkey, using bias-corrected CMIP6 GCM outputs and machine learning.
29b7d89323d2e7b27e85f586d46eb830b0786814.architecture: Comparison of LSTM, bidirectional LSTM, AdaBoost, gradient boosting, regression tree and random forest for bias correction and streamflow modelling.
29b7d89323d2e7b27e85f586d46eb830b0786814.data: CMIP6 GCMs under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, Climate Prediction Center data for the historical period, and observed streamflow in the Konya Closed basin.
29b7d89323d2e7b27e85f586d46eb830b0786814.result: Random forest consistently outperforms other models; projections show a significant decline in river flow in coming decades.
29b7d89323d2e7b27e85f586d46eb830b0786814.open_work: Using projections to plan climate-resilient water infrastructure and drought early warning.
29b7d89323d2e7b27e85f586d46eb830b0786814.issues: Single basin; statistical models trained on historical relationships may not hold under future climate; GCM selection and uncertainty not detailed.

d3d16174cae649971bbe8846cacc5b0012fed404.goal: Enables accurate deep learning PV power forecasting for sites with little observational data.
d3d16174cae649971bbe8846cacc5b0012fed404.architecture: Two-step pipeline: deep learning forecaster (SolNet) pretrained on synthetic PVGIS data then fine-tuned on observations (transfer learning); network type not specified in the abstract.
d3d16174cae649971bbe8846cacc5b0012fed404.data: Synthetic PV output from PVGIS plus actual production data from hundreds of sites in the Netherlands, Australia and Belgium, with weather data.
d3d16174cae649971bbe8846cacc5b0012fed404.result: SolNet improves forecasts in data-scarce settings and over baselines, with the largest transfer learning gains when observational data are limited.
d3d16174cae649971bbe8846cacc5b0012fed404.open_work: Guidelines on weather inputs, seasonality, synthetic data amount and location mis-specification; application globally.
d3d16174cae649971bbe8846cacc5b0012fed404.issues: Benefits shrink as observational data grow; sensitive to source location mis-specification and weather data quality.

6dd9a09d5eb388d7f8e119cf9564bd13cec13ae9.goal: Estimates county-level cropland area damaged by flooding to support disaster management and food security under increasing extreme precipitation.
6dd9a09d5eb388d7f8e119cf9564bd13cec13ae9.architecture: Convolutional neural network (CNN) using remote sensing images and weather fields, with separate early-season and late-season windows.
6dd9a09d5eb388d7f8e119cf9564bd13cec13ae9.data: Remote sensing imagery and meteorological fields for corn and soybean in the midwestern United States, 2008–2019, with county-level flood damage records.
6dd9a09d5eb388d7f8e119cf9564bd13cec13ae9.result: Mean relative error within ±25% and relative RMSE 35–75% in most counties for most years; meteorology-only inputs give acceptable accuracy.
6dd9a09d5eb388d7f8e119cf9564bd13cec13ae9.open_work: Seasonal forecasting of crop flood damage, future climate impact studies and global food security assessment.
6dd9a09d5eb388d7f8e119cf9564bd13cec13ae9.issues: Relative RMSE up to 75% is large; damage records may be incomplete; limited to two crops in one region.

b5f84bb16bd9ed1d03c46f86e89a5c69609b4f93.goal: Estimates daily snow water equivalent across the Rocky Mountains from gridded meteorology for water resources applications.
b5f84bb16bd9ed1d03c46f86e89a5c69609b4f93.architecture: Three temporal deep learning models (e.g., LSTM-type recurrent and temporal convolutional networks) compared with a conceptual SWE model, plus explainable AI attribution.
b5f84bb16bd9ed1d03c46f86e89a5c69609b4f93.data: SNOTEL station SWE observations as targets and high-resolution gridded meteorological fields over the Rocky Mountain region; comparison with interpolated gridded SWE datasets.
b5f84bb16bd9ed1d03c46f86e89a5c69609b4f93.result: All DL models give higher median NSE than the conceptual model and gridded datasets but higher mean squared errors; XAI shows precipitation and temperature dominate; normalizing SWE by historical maximum solves extrapolation.
b5f84bb16bd9ed1d03c46f86e89a5c69609b4f93.open_work: Improving spatial extrapolation to ungauged terrain and integrating remote sensing of snow.
b5f84bb16bd9ed1d03c46f86e89a5c69609b4f93.issues: Training only at SNOTEL sites limits representativeness at other elevations; higher MSE than baselines; extrapolation needs normalization.

98666391c6fffe54df70d426e9cd2090b3ad5ff7.goal: Improves extreme flood forecasting, which suffers from peak underestimation and high uncertainty.
98666391c6fffe54df70d426e9cd2090b3ad5ff7.architecture: Diffusion-based runoff model (DRUM), a probabilistic diffusion model for streamflow, compared with state-of-the-art deep learning benchmarks such as LSTM.
98666391c6fffe54df70d426e9cd2090b3ad5ff7.data: Representative basins across the contiguous United States with precipitation forcing, including operational forecast and measured precipitation scenarios.
98666391c6fffe54df70d426e9cd2090b3ad5ff7.result: DRUM improves nowcasting for the top 1 per mille flows in 72.3% of basins, extends reliable lead time by nearly a day for 20- and 50-year floods, and gains 3–7 days in some regions with measured precipitation.
98666391c6fffe54df70d426e9cd2090b3ad5ff7.open_work: Applying diffusion models more broadly in hydrology and Earth system science.
98666391c6fffe54df70d426e9cd2090b3ad5ff7.issues: Gains under ideal measured precipitation overstate operational value; regional variability; generative sampling cost not discussed.

ea612fd43aa69e665487568d03c21292ba3c1861.goal: Produces a high-resolution observation-based daily soil moisture dataset for Europe for hydrological and agricultural analyses.
ea612fd43aa69e665487568d03c21292ba3c1861.architecture: Long short-term memory (LSTM) network trained on in situ soil moisture with meteorological inputs; dataset product (SoMo.ml-EU).
ea612fd43aa69e665487568d03c21292ba3c1861.data: In situ soil moisture measurements and high-resolution meteorological data; 0.1° daily dataset over Europe for three soil layers, 2003–2020.
ea612fd43aa69e665487568d03c21292ba3c1861.result: SoMo.ml-EU agrees more closely with independent in situ data than its 0.25° predecessor and captures soil moisture variability including drought.
ea612fd43aa69e665487568d03c21292ba3c1861.open_work: Further regional studies and extension to other regions or periods.
ea612fd43aa69e665487568d03c21292ba3c1861.issues: Uneven in situ network density limits accuracy in sparse areas; no physical constraints; quantitative metrics not reported in the abstract.

231771d901b0fc448bfc7f4e6cac2b9ae40c9b65.goal: Compares ways of feeding numerical weather prediction (NWP) forecasts into deep learning models for photovoltaic power forecasting, to identify which integration approach is most effective.
231771d901b0fc448bfc7f4e6cac2b9ae40c9b65.architecture: Deep learning PV power forecasting models with alternative NWP integration strategies; the specific network families are not reported since the abstract is unavailable.
231771d901b0fc448bfc7f4e6cac2b9ae40c9b65.data: NWP forecast variables and PV plant power records; specific products and sites not reported in the abstract.
231771d901b0fc448bfc7f4e6cac2b9ae40c9b65.result: Not reported in the abstract; the title implies that the choice of NWP integration approach materially affects PV forecast accuracy.
231771d901b0fc448bfc7f4e6cac2b9ae40c9b65.open_work: Testing the recommended integration approaches across more plants, climates and NWP sources would establish generality.
231771d901b0fc448bfc7f4e6cac2b9ae40c9b65.issues: Abstract unavailable; conclusions may depend on the specific NWP product, sites and forecast horizons studied.

aa7c29e769bf5b3e0b40b1a3cdb2c1183ed8e6c5.goal: Assesses how hydro-climatic extremes affect hydropower reliability and urban electricity use in data-scarce Malawi, where river gauging and power data are limited.
aa7c29e769bf5b3e0b40b1a3cdb2c1183ed8e6c5.architecture: Random forest regression predicts river discharge in ungauged conditions from satellite predictors, followed by regression analysis linking discharge to hydropower output and nighttime light radiance.
aa7c29e769bf5b3e0b40b1a3cdb2c1183ed8e6c5.data: Satellite altimetry (TOPEX/POSEIDON, OSTM/Jason), VIIRS nighttime lights, MODIS, TMPA precipitation and AMSR-E plus field observations; Malawi 2000–2018 for hydrology and 2012–2018 for power.
aa7c29e769bf5b3e0b40b1a3cdb2c1183ed8e6c5.result: The validated framework shows significant impacts of hydro-climatic variability and dry extremes on both electricity supply and final electricity use in urban areas.
aa7c29e769bf5b3e0b40b1a3cdb2c1183ed8e6c5.open_work: Extending the framework to long-term infrastructure monitoring, other hydropower-dependent countries and climate change scenarios to identify vulnerable populations.
aa7c29e769bf5b3e0b40b1a3cdb2c1183ed8e6c5.issues: Single-country case study; nighttime lights are only an indirect proxy for electricity use, and random forest extrapolation to ungauged conditions may be uncertain under unprecedented extremes.

310ab919b7db5b5f5dd0e5a106c4c96520bf729e.goal: Projects future spatio-temporal runoff in the glacier-fed mountainous basins of the Third Pole, whose water resources are sensitive to climate change and glacier melt.
310ab919b7db5b5f5dd0e5a106c4c96520bf729e.architecture: LSTM-grid: a grid-scale long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network driven by monthly precipitation, air temperature and total glacier mass change at 0.25° resolution.
310ab919b7db5b5f5dd0e5a106c4c96520bf729e.data: Training targets are gridded monthly runoff and evapotranspiration from an observation-constrained cryosphere-hydrology model in headwaters of seven Third Pole basins, 2000–2017; verification 2013–2017; future climate projections as forcing.
310ab919b7db5b5f5dd0e5a106c4c96520bf729e.result: Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency exceeds 0.92 in verification; monsoon basins show faster runoff increase than westerly basins, spring runoff rises notably, and precipitation gains influence after peak glacier mass loss.
310ab919b7db5b5f5dd0e5a106c4c96520bf729e.open_work: Validating against direct observations and quantifying uncertainty from climate projections and glacier change scenarios.
310ab919b7db5b5f5dd0e5a106c4c96520bf729e.issues: Trained on output of a process model rather than observations, so it inherits that model's biases; monthly resolution; extrapolation to future climates beyond the training range is untested.

458e7d877425cf7a50940362de17352deaa12709.goal: Provides rapid urban flood inundation prediction that accounts for spatio-temporally varying rainstorms, which earlier deep learning surrogates often ignored, with added interpretability.
458e7d877425cf7a50940362de17352deaa12709.architecture: ConvLSTM (convolutional long short-term memory) network as an end-to-end surrogate of a physics-based flood model, compared with a 3D CNN, with Grad-CAM for interpretation.
458e7d877425cf7a50940362de17352deaa12709.data: Rainstorm scenarios and inundation simulations from a physics-based urban flood model over a 74 km² urban area, plus observed inundation points from actual storms.
458e7d877425cf7a50940362de17352deaa12709.result: Average Pearson correlation of 0.958 and MAE of 0.021 m against the physics-based model; predicts an event in about 2 s, 170 times faster; Grad-CAM highlights local and upstream rainfall concentration.
458e7d877425cf7a50940362de17352deaa12709.open_work: Transfer to other cities and integration into real-time flood early warning using rainfall forecasts.
458e7d877425cf7a50940362de17352deaa12709.issues: Single study area; trained on physics-model output so accuracy is bounded by that model; generalization to unseen rainfall patterns and extreme events is limited.

8ffb55e7eb9abfc84f9528e86fdbf6c6bfa10625.goal: Quantifies climate change impacts on wheat grain yield and nutritional quality (N, Fe, Zn) for food security under mid-century climate.
8ffb55e7eb9abfc84f9528e86fdbf6c6bfa10625.architecture: Automated machine learning (AutoML) training many models combined into a stacked ensemble, compared with traditional ML models.
8ffb55e7eb9abfc84f9528e86fdbf6c6bfa10625.data: Multi-site, multi-season field experiments with three cultivars and Fe/Zn treatments plus national yield statistics; projections from NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 downscaled GCMs (GFDL-ESM4, HadGEM3-GC31-MM, MRI-ESM2-0) under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5.
8ffb55e7eb9abfc84f9528e86fdbf6c6bfa10625.result: Stacked ensemble predicts yield (R² > 0.78), N (> 0.75), Fe and Zn (> 0.71); climate change raises yield 4.5% and protein 0.8% but lowers Fe 5.5% and Zn 4.5% by 2020–2050 versus 1980–2010.
8ffb55e7eb9abfc84f9528e86fdbf6c6bfa10625.open_work: Adding adaptation options, more GCMs and cultivars, and extending to other crops and regions.
8ffb55e7eb9abfc84f9528e86fdbf6c6bfa10625.issues: Only three GCMs; limited experimental sites and seasons constrain extrapolation to future climate; CO2 fertilization and management changes may be incompletely represented.

e123ab27dbbbf343f56b88e7100df21f74de9bee.goal: Develops parsimonious, interpretable catchment-scale hydrologic models with machine learning by finding the minimal architecture that explains a catchment's input-state-output behaviour across high, medium and low flows.
e123ab27dbbbf343f56b88e7100df21f74de9bee.architecture: Directed-graph architectures built from the mass-conserving perceptron (MCP) unit, a physically interpretable neural network element, explored with increasing complexity including input bypass and bidirectional groundwater exchange.
e123ab27dbbbf343f56b88e7100df21f74de9bee.data: Daily precipitation, potential evapotranspiration and streamflow at a single study catchment (the Leaf River basin in the authors' MCP studies).
e123ab27dbbbf343f56b88e7100df21f74de9bee.result: A HyMod-like architecture with three cell-states and two flow paths captures dominant processes; input bypass improves hydrograph timing and shape and groundwater exchange improves baseflow; multiple diagnostic metrics are essential.
